Nothing seems to happen.
What is it you would like to do?
Nothing seems to happen.
Nothing happens. Maybe you should reconsider your current course of action?
Nothing happens. More time wasted.
Nothing seems to happen. Perhaps you should try something else?
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Westedge". The sign also points to the west for the north-western Realmz, and to the east for the Sword Lands.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Highstone". The sign also points to the west for Mountedge, and to the east for Nur'Anaan.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Hillside". The sign also points to the south for Mountedge, to the west for the north-western Realmz, and to the east for the Sword Lands.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Mountedge". The sign also points to the west for Fort Hillside.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Endanuur". The sign also points to the north for Lantharond, and to the south for Tanirith.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Tanirith; Fort Tarterys". The sign also points to the west for Nur'Anaan, and to the east for Lantharond.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Riverside". The sign also points to the north for Tanirith, and to the west for Nur'Anaan.

This old, worn out sign reads: "Nur'Anaan". The sign also points to the north for Mountedge, and to the south for Fort Uppersea and Tanirith.

This old, worn out sign reads: "FRIENDSHIP ROAD". It also points to the west for Mountedge, and to the east Fort Friendship and Nur'Anaan.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Mountedge".
This old, worn out sign reads: "Mountedge Harbor".
You empty the pouch of its contents in order to make them your own.
This old, worn out sign points to the south for Seacrest, to the west for Calember, and to the east for Goldylock.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Goldylock".
This old, worn out sign reads: "Seacrest". The sign also points to the south-east for Wavyn.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Springdale".
This old, worn out sign points to the west for Calember, to the north for Edgemoor, and to the east for Seacrest.
Before falling unconscious, your comrade manages to gulp a potion of healing.
The putrid guts of the creature spill onto the ground.  Thousands of vile, buzzing insects had been feeding on the horrid creature's innards.
Upon its death, the creature becomes inanimate base materials, trapping your weapon.
Upon its death, the creature releases a gusting poisonous cloud!
Upon its death, the creature releases an exploding cloud of fire!
Upon its death, the creature releases a shockwave of lightning!
Upon its death, the creature releases a gusting cloud of hot vapor!
You are under attack!
The mentarch's essence dissipates with a devastating wave of psi-energies!

(Please answer the following question truthfully, since it is meant simply to allow this scenario to adjust itself for your better enjoyment. Answering one way or the other will in no way take away anything from this scenario. Thank you, and have fun!)
Which one of the following statements best applies to you?
Another day begins. Another day in the mines. Another day as a slave. That is how your life has always been ...

Lacking any mental powers -the 'Gift' as it is called-, you were therefore deemed a mongrel and thus born into the station of a slave. Born to serve your superiors and your masters who are blessed with the Gift; fit only to serve the Lankharhan people.

While you have known no other life than that of a slave, you have heard whispers among others of your ilk that the Lankharhans did not always rule as they do today. That non-gifted peoples used to live free.  But such a mythical age ended centuries ago.

Freedom, the whispered stories say, ended with the Second Rising of the God-like Mentarchs, those supreme rulers of the Lankharhan people whom you know better as 'Mind Lords'. The Mentarchs had been banished thousands of winters ago, the stories say.

But their leader, the Hierarch, eventually found a way to bring back four other Mentarchs and establish a Neo-Imperium of Lankharh, an empire that now stretches across both the continents of Realmz and Anarym. Thus, for the last six and a half centuries,

it has been Imperial Law that mongrels such as you be slaves and nothing else. Fit only to perform the most menial and back-breaking of tasks, to live a life of misery and hardship without end ... or rather, with the wish to die sooner than later,

in order to be free in death of this pitiful life that you were born to live. However, the whispered stories do offer some hope for those who would believe them: one day, the stories say, The Destined Ones will rise and destroy the Mentarchs for good.

Shaking those thoughts, you pick up with resignation your tools and rations for the day, and set yourself to mine once again for the Masters ... determined all the while to survive through one more day in order to live to see tomorrow one more time.
After many hours of reading the book, your priestly character gains a level from the divine insight gained!
You have no ore or rough gemstones to put into the carts. Perhaps you should mine first, thus ensuring that the Masters will not punish you for idleness ...
You dump the fruits of your hard labor into the carts.
You do not have a mining pick! How are you ever going to mine anything with your bare hands?
After hours of hard hacking at the earth and stone, you finally hit pay dirt!

You cross paths with a group of slaves from different races. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of dwarven slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of orc and goblin slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of ogre slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of human slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of kobold slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of elven slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of furfoot slaves. Exhausted and near to collapsing, they don't even acknowledge your presence, trying to be as inconspicuous as possible in order not to attract the attention of the imperial overseers.

You cross paths with a group of imperial overseers on patrol, each one a brutal warrior and loyal soldier of the empire, blessed by birth with the Gift. Force of habit and survival instincts make you lower your eyes so as to look subservient.

You come upon a slave who has collapsed from exhaustion and now lying near death. Force of habit and survival instincts make you walk away quickly from the dying slave, before a patrol of imperial overseers arrive to carry him outside for disposal.

You then remember a rumor that has been circulating for quite a while about the possible link between dead slaves and the slave-rations handed out by the overseers. You immediately try to push away the sickening thought and get on your way.

You come upon a patrol of imperial overseers dishing out punishment to a lazy slave, using their Gift to do so. As the poor slave lies on the ground, writhing in unbearable pain from having his nerves and brain ennervated by the overseers' mental powers,
you lower your eyes and hastily get on your way ... lest you be punished as well for idleness.

"I'm over here!" Someone whispers forcefully from the west-end of the passage. Squinting your eyes to see better under the poor lighting, you see Nasslass the kobold gesturing at you to come join him with haste.

"There ye are! Where've ye been?" Nasslass asks, quite worried about you. Smiling at your impatient slave-friend,  you shrug for lack of an answer. The kobold grunts, shaking his head: "Well, whot are ye trying to do? Get them overseers on our backs?"

He sighs. "I'm getting too old to nurse bums like ye!" He exclaims with mock frustration. Chuckling, he picks up his pick and winks at you: "Now that yer here, maybe we could mine our quota fer the day? We've only got about ten hours to kill, ye know!"

At that, your other friend, Nerylka, joins you: "Sorry for the delay." She whispers with a grave look. "I came across a patrol of overseers dishing out punishment to some poor dogres." She shakes her head in disgust. "I had to take a detour in the mines,

for I did not wish to be noticed by the imperial 'bastards'." Nasslass grunts again: "Quite early in the morn to be sadistic, eh?" He then sighs, finding his sarcastic humor out of place. Silently, he hands you some torches to light your way.

You look at each other with sadness, silently grasping your mining picks to begin another exhausting day as slaves and trying not to remember too vividly all those times when you have felt the punishing mental agonies inflicted by the overseers.
(Nasslass and Nerylka have joined your party; check out the Allies menu)
You finally return to the surface, welcoming one more time the smell and feel of fresh air, happy to have made it through yet another day in the mines without dying.
Numerous imperial overseers stand watch here.
Before allowing you and your fellow slaves to return to the surface, everyone is searched for concealed ore or gemstones, in order to prevent smuggling and trading among the slaves.
Having been found 'clean', imperial guards impatiently motion you to move on and return to the slave pens.

"And just where do you think you're going, mongrel?" An imperial snarls menacingly, as his collegues put their hands on their sheated weapons. "Your shift is not over yet, not until past the fifth hour after noon! Return to work NOW!"

Force of habit and survival instincts make you lower your eyes in subservience, as you back away from the gates to return to mine some more. "Stupid mongrels!" One of the imperial overseers mumbles behind you.

Since you are still in possession of mined minerals, you know that being caught 'red-handed' will earn you a confiscation of rations for a week along with a harsh punishment. Do you walk away in order to go back and dump your load in the carts?
This is your hut. Not much of a place, but it is the only 'home' you have ever known.
Back again to your little hut. Not much of a place, but at least you can take finally some rest.
This is your hut.
Finally back to your little hut, you look forward to take some rest.
You leave to return outside.

As your turn comes to be searched, sure enough an imperial overseer finds mined minerals concealed in your vestments. "Well, well, well!" He exclaims, grinning maliciously. "We have stupid mongrel thieves here!"

At this announcement, all other slaves move away while lowering their eyes. "You know the penalty for what you have done, mongrels!" The overseers snarls, as numerous of his collegues move to surround you. Do you attempt to fight your way out?

Seeing no point in commiting suicide by fighting the overseers, you lower your eyes in acceptance of your punishment to come ... hoping it won't be too painful this time. Immediately, the overseers spear your mind and nerves with their psionic powers.

Half-conscious and still writhing in pain, you are unceremoniously taken back to the surface and dumped in front of your hut. "And no food for a week, you mongrel trash!" The overseer snarls, as the gates of the slave pens are closed.
More overseers come to join the fray!
Your defiance rouses some of your fellow slaves to join you in revolt!

Yelling out with rage all the years of oppression that you have endured, you raise your mining pick and charge the overseers! "Fine!" One of them shouts back. "Time to teach you filthy mongrels to respect your betters, once and for all!"
As you try to flee for your life, you are mercilessly cut down.

Once again, you have failed. Once again, your wearied souls drift into to the Great Beyond. As you cross into this dark and empty world, one last thought remains in your fading consciousness: the Mind Lords will have the last laugh after all ...
Emboldened by this strange turn of events, you forge ahead to the surface with numerous slaves following you, as cries of "Revolt, revolt!" ring out loud!
This is one of the overseers' guard-houses. You decide it would be best not enter and be punished for it.
You and the revolting slaves ransack the overseers' guard-houses. To your delight and relief, you manage to scrounge up healing potions and other useful items.
"Ah! Weapons of usefulness!" Nerylka muses, as she picks up a few items that attracted her attention.

"Ye know," Nasslass mumbles angrily, "if ye'd told me this morn that ye planned an uprising against the overseers, I might've just stayed in bed!" He then winks at you good-naturedly, while picking up a few weapons for himself.

As the other slaves begin to vent their rage on the wounded and fallen overseers, a wave of nausea grips some members of your group. Bending over in pain, they feel as if their bodies are burning up! Is this the price for rising against your Masters?
The same terrible thing is happening to your friend Nerylka!

The pain then stops as quickly as it came. Gaping around in astonishment, those affected feel as if their beings were infused by a surge of power: although they have never felt like this before, their instincts tell them that this power is magical!

Looking at each other, you wonder how is this possible. Does this mean that the True Gods are alive, and not fallen by the hands of the Mentarchs, as you had been told? If so, why is this happening only to your group, and not to the other slaves?

Nasslass stares at Nerylka and the members of your group that were affected by this miracle, tears trickling down his reptilian eyes: "Could this be true? Could you guys be the foretold Destined that will save us from the Lankharhans and the Mentarchs?"
Moved by your friend's reaction, you clap him on the shoulder, reminding him that he *is* part of your group, and thus by definition a 'Destined' himself ... if you all are indeed so.
Considering the strange dreams that you have been having lately, you wonder if such dreams and this miraculous event are not somehow related. But if so, what does it all mean?

While sleeping, disturbing images invade your dreams once again. Haunting figures, the faces of whom are strangers to you, greet you as long-time friends. As they stand by your side, you brave countless dangers and face numerous nightmarish monsters.

Among these friends that you do not recognize,  you see a brave knight shrouded by a burning flame of goodness and a stubborn dwarf wearing an immaterial king's crown, along with a ranger and a swordswoman with mental powers not unlike the overseers'.

And in this dream, you feel *alive* - as if that is the life you have always lived and always wanted to live: experiencing adventures of such scope that they invariably find a place within the sagas and songs of bards and minstrels throughout the lands.

But how can this be, since you were born a slave and have never known anything else?  At this thought, you and everyone of your group wake up, startled. Looking at each other, you realize that you all had the same, disturbing dream.

As the eerie images gradually fade from your mind, you wonder whether some of the overseers did not use their mental powers to play tricks on you ... And yet, deep down, you *know* the dream was real and was meant to tell you something.
You return to the mines ... once again.
Returning to the mines at this time would be a serious mistake ... perhaps you should finish what you started?
You overhear a whispered conversation between slaves.

"Me heard that Zorg ta half-orc's making another of his meetings tonight." An ogre mumbles. "Zorg? Ta one that always wan'us ta revolt? Crazy Zorg?" A female goblin asks. "Yup." The ogre answers. "Ta meeting's at his hut again, like every other night."

"Me tell ye that the Gods aren't dead!" A dwarf mumbles angrily. "It be a lie that the god-emperors, them Mentarchs, killed our Gods! Lies, me say!" A bored orc shrugs while hacking away at the rocks: "Sure. Fine. If ya say so. "

"Me heard that secret tunels are about these old mines." A kobold muses. An elf maid sighs with exasperation: "So, we should use them to escape? And how are we to survive, out there? Without that cursed Gift, we'll be found easily and put to death!"

"I've heard rumors of slaves escaping and joining rebels that are camping in the area!" A man muses. "Really?" An interested gnome asks. The man nods: "Yup! And these rebels are said to give quite a headache to the Masters!" Both smile at that.

"I tell ye, I ain't eating anymore o' that food the overseers are givin' us!" A man proclaims. "Why so?" An ogre asks. "Cuz it's made from dead slave flesh, that's why!" The man replies. The ogre is confused at that: "An' why's that a problem?"

"Me heard that rebels are camping about ta area and raiding ta Masters of ta nearby town." A female gnath murmurs. "No kiddin'?" a furfoot asks. "Yup!" The gnath replies. "They're former slaves, me heard, and they be lead by a man called Wildstorm!"
Slaves here are busy at hacking away at the rock and earth with their picks.
"Another day, another shift in the mines." Nasslass muses. "Let us be done with it!"
"One more dreary day in the mines." Nerylka mumbles. "How I long for this to end."
Slaves here are busy loading their mined ore and gems into rusting steel carts.
Slaves here are busy pushing the loaded steel carts towards the gates, in order to bring them back to the surface.
You take water from the well, filling up waterskins to the brim.
You refill your waterskins.
Feeling the pangs of empty stomachs, each member of your party grabs a quick snack from the rations carried in your backpacks.
Without any rations with you, your weakened bodies suffer the effects of lack of food!
You quench your thirst with the water in your waterskins.
Without water with you, dehydration takes its toll!
Slaves are returning to the slave pens, under the watchful eyes of the imperial overseers.
As you cross the gates, your daily allotment of food rations is handed out by one of the imperial guards.
Once all slaves have crossed the gates, the iron doors are shut and locked.
As you cross the gates, the daily allotement of food rations are being handed out by some of the imperial guards.
"Nothing for them!" An overseers snarls as food was about to be handed to you. "They've been sentenced to a week without rations!" At that, you are pushed forward into the pen yards.

"And once again, all you mongrels better remember!" An overseer shouts from the battlement. "You better cross the gates no later than the ninth hour of the morn to return to the mines, or you will be punished for idleness!"
"One more of you was so caught this morning. I'm getting sick and tired of repeating the rules, you stupid mongrels!"
"Two more of you were so caught this morning. I'm getting sick and tired of repeating the rules, you stupid mongrels!"
"Although none of you were caught for that this morning, I know some of you will eventually. I'm getting sick and tired of repeating the rules, you stupid mongrels!"
"Six more of you were so caught this morning. I'm getting sick and tired of repeating the rules, you stupid mongrels!"
Returning to the slave pens at this time would be a serious mistake ... perhaps you should finish what you started?
The gates of the slave pens are closed. "What are you about, mongrels?" An imperial guard snarls. "Eager to start your shift in the mines, or sneaking about with the hope of escaping?"

Force of habit and survival instincts make you lower your eyes and back away from the gates, as the imperial guards laugh at you. "We open the gates between five and nine in the morn! No good for memory, eh, you stupid mongrels?"
Slaves are going out of the slave pens in order to begin another day in the mines, under the watchful eyes of the imperial overseers.
Taking great care as to be seen by no one, you cross past this secret door.
You have found a secret cave. You are quite certain that you could safely rest here.
You leave the safe cave.
You re-enter the safe cave.

As you come to the gates, you find numerous overseers waiting for you. "Well, well, well!" One of them exclaims, grinning maliciously. "Forgot that you had to return to the mines before nine in the morn? We have stupid mongrel slackers here!"

"You know the penalty for what you have done, mongrels!" The overseer snarls, as numerous of his colleagues move to surround you. "Punishment AND no food for a week!" Do you attempt to fight your way out?
Half-conscious and still writhing in pain, you are forcefully dragged to the mines. "And let that be a good lesson, you slacking mongrel trash!" One of the overseers snarls at you.
Emboldened by this strange turn of events, you forge ahead with numerous slaves following you, as cries of "Revolt, revolt!" ring out loud!
You and the revolting slaves ransack the overseers' watch-towers. To your delight and relief, you manage to scrounge up healing potions and other useful items.
Imperial guards hand out torches so that slaves can see a little, down in the mines.
You feel a strong draft coming from the ceiling here.
How are you going to do this without any tools?

Success! The ceiling falls away, revealing a shaft that can be easily climbed by hand! However, the rock in your immediate surroundings must have been unstable, for the ceiling behind you crumbles, hopelessly blocking the way back!
You climb to the surface.

You end up in a passage surrounded by mountains. Taking a deep breath while bathing in the fresh air, you have great difficulty from preventing yourself at shouting your joy for being free ... at last!

Deep down in your hearts of hearts, you feel the conviction that the strange dream you have been having meant to urge you, among other things that you have yet to figure out, to be brave enough to attempt to do what you are now doing: escape.
You climb back down to the dark underground.
Elated at being truly out of the slave pens, nagging questions haunt your thoughts: what now? Where to go next?
And most important: how to go about not being recaptured?
You find another secret passage, going east-southeast!
Suddenly, a wave of nausea grips some members of your group. Bending over in pain, they feel as if their bodies are burning up! Is this the price for defying your Masters?
Emboldened by this strange turn of events, you forge ahead in your newly found freedom ... and portentous blessings!
"Well, well!" Nasslass muses, obviously restraining his excitement. "I wonder where this will lead us, eh?" He winks at that.
"What an interesting find." Nasslass mumbles to himself, his curiosity piqued. "I hope we'll find a place to take some rest ... cuz my rusty bones are getting tired, eh?" He grins at that.
"Now, this is unexpected!" Nasslass whispers, his eyes dancing with excitement. "I wonder what we'll find in there ..." He bobs his eyebrows in expectation, while smiling mischievously.
"Unexpected find indeed!" Nerylka muses, her eyes dancing with anticipation.
"Hmmm." Nerylka muses to herself. "I hope we'll find a place to rest, for I am rather tired now." She sighs to emphasize her point.
"What an interesting turn of events!" Nerylka whispers excitedly. "I wonder what we'll find in there ..." She grins mischievously at that.
"Yes!" Nasslass whispers, obviously happy at the chance to take a nap.
"A little rest would be welcome!" Nerylka muses, obviously relieved at the chance to take a nap.
"Here we go!" Nasslass exclaims with glee. "Looks like we've found a good spot, eh?" He winks at that.
"Niiiiice!" Nasslass muses with a wide grin, finding pride in the hard work.
"I think we're on a roll, eh?" Nasslass quips with a mischievous wink.
"By the stars!" Nerylka exclaims with glee. "Looks like we've found a good spot indeed." She then smiles with satisfaction.
"Niiiiice!" Nerylka muses with a wide grin, finding pride in the hard work.
"I think the Masters will find us quite productive today! But don't expect any bonuses ..." Nerylka quips with a mischievous wink.
You enter this hut.

An old, one-eyed half-orc lives here apparently. His dour demeanor is an obvious sign that he is not happy with your intrusion: "Git outta Zorg's hut, ye fools!" he mumbles angrily. You ask him who is this 'Zorg'.

"Are ye lacking brains?" he asks in return. "I'm Zorg! If ye want to attend ta secret meeting, come by ta tenth hour of ta night! Now go, before them overseers suspect what's going on! Ye know how they be when they catch us slaves speaking together!"
Rebuffed by the insistence of Zorg the half-orc, you leave promptly.
No one seems to be about. However, one of the cots was apparently moved aside to expose this shoddy trap door. Listening carefully, you can hear muffled sounds coming from below.
Do you open the trap door?
Opening the trap door reveals a ladder going into some sort of basement dug underneath the hut. As you climb down the ladder, you realize that the muffled sounds you heard earlier are now silent.
Another meeting appears to be on tonight.
You come upon a small assembly of slaves. As you enter, you see them ready to jump on you, their mining picks held high in readiness.
Realizing that you are slaves like them -and not overseers-, they all relax and resume their muted discussions.
The debate on the pros and cons of rising in revolt against the Masters continues among the slaves.

The slaves appear to be debating about something very important. Some try to be persuasive while others shake their head in disagreement. At the back of this make-shift basement stands an old half-orc, shouting loud to be heard above the slaves' chatter.

"Me tongue's speaking ta truth!" Zorg booms. "Ta Gods are not dead! They've spoken to me in dreams! Ta time's near fer ta Destined to rise and deliver us!" Many slaves nod in agreement while others shake their head even more vigorously.

"Ye must hear me words!" Zorg adds. "All of this, all ta darkness that we've known ... it'll become like a nightmare gone! A memory that we'll not even remember! So have ta Gods told me in me dreams!" Arguments among the slaves are renewed at that.

The slaves appear to be debating about something very important. Some try to be persuasive while others shake their head. At the back of this makeshift basement stands the old half-orc Zorg, shouting loud to be heard above the slaves' chatter.

"Who are those destined, then? Can you tell us, old man?" Someone shouts aloud amidst the discussions. Immediately, everybody falls silent to focus their attention on old Zorg. Leaning on his staff, Zorg chuckles: "Me does not know who they be ..."

"But how could me know?" he adds quickly with a bellow, forestalling another eruption of arguments. "Ta Gods have shown in me dreams that ta Destined themselves don't yet know who, or what, they truly are! Their minds be as clouded as ours, see?"

Zorg chuckles anew: "But ta Gods are working ta pierce that cloud, trying ta show the Destined who they be, so that they realize and understand what they must do! As they speak to me in dreams, so ta Gods be speaking to ta Destined in theirs!"
Zorg's words hit you like a hammer. Could your strange dreams actually be the Gods' way to try to 'awake' you ... because you are the Destined?

"And that's why" Zorg's harangue goes on, "we've to do our part! We've to help ta Destined remember, fer they be among us! This me knows! So let us rise against ta Masters and stir ta Destined to realize who they truly be!"
At that, more fervent arguing resumes among the slaves, while Zorg looks on with grim determination, leaning heavily on his wooden staff.
"This be madness!" An ogre exclaims to another slave. "Let's wait fer them Destined to be revealed BEFORE we be starting a revolt!"
"We cain't be risin' againt ta masters!" A female kobold cries out. "They'll kill us with a single thought! They'll damn us to suffer forever!"

"How can them Destined be among us?" A dwarf asks aloud. "We're but slaves in a remote mountain outpost of the Imperium! Them Destined should be nearer to the Capitol, where they could do more damage!"
"A revolt?" An elf exclaims, incredulous. "This is folly! Without weapons and armor, the overseers will crush us!"
"Yes! Let us revolt now!" A female gnath bellows. "Time to give back to the overseers what they've been giving to us!"
"Me agree with Zorg!" A goblin shouts. "Our fates are our own, so it's up to us to show ta way for ta Destined!"
"Zorg's right!" A woman exclaims. "The Gods still live and the Destined are here! We must do our part: revolt, I say! Revolt! Death to our oppressors!"
"Me say death to the Masters!" A frantic orc shouts aloud. "Me've had enough of them bastards! Me want their blood on me hands!"

Just as the clash is about to begin, you hear old Zorg bellow from somewhere around: "Now's ta time! See? Ta Destined have finally chosen ta act! Ta arms! Ta revolt!" At that, Zorg and numerous slaves rush to your side against the oppressors!
Zorg walks up to you, grinning: "Me knew it! From ta moment me eyes saw ye, me knew ye were ta ones! Lead us forth, oh blessed Destined ... to victory!"
(Zorg has joined your party; check out the Allies menu)
"Let's not forget about them rebels!" A man exclaims with excitement. "They're sure giving headaches to the Masters! We'd better find a way to contact them before we do anything rash!"
"Whot about them rebels I keep hearing about?" A dogre asks of no one in particular. "They be real or not? If they be real, I say they should help us!"
"Shouldn't we try to make contact with those rebels we've heard about?" A female furfoot asks aloud. "These folks must be better organized than poor us! They could help!"
How do you respond?
Zorg the one-eyed half-orc nods to you in greeting: "Me welcome ye. Me glad ye could come to this meeting."
"Be welcome here." Zorg the one-eyed half-orc greets you, his head nodding slowly. "Me is glad that you be attending this meeting."
"Be welcome here." Zorg the one-eyed half-orc greets you, his remaining grey eye peering at you with intensity. "Me is glad that you be here."

Zorg raises his eyebrow in surprise: "This be a strange question indeed. Ta answer is simple: we be meant to be free! On a deeper level, ta answer be more complicated ... Ye see, ta Neo-Imperium of ta Lankharhans is wrong. It wasn't even meant to be!"

He chuckles at your incredulity: "Aye, yer minds be clouded indeed. But truth be in me words, because ta Gods have shown me ta truth! All our lives, all of ta Neo-Imperium, even ta God-Emperors -ta Mentarchs-; they all be lies made real."

He then sighs. "It be hard to explain. Even me has difficulty understanding this. But it be truth nonetheless." He then turns his remaining piercing grey eye on you: "But ye'll come to understand. Aye." He mumbles cryptically, with a wistful smile.

Zorg chuckles. "Me be an old man. Too many years as slave already! What me has to lose?" He then goes on with a more serious tone: "Me has been chosen as ta messenger. Me must do what me must do: to spread ta word and wisdom of ta Gods."

He opens his arms wide, as if to encompass all the slaves attending: "What better way to do this? With me meetings, me can stir hope and courage and determination! Me can tell ta truth of our Gods and tell all that we're meant ta be free!"

He then sighs. "But also," he mumbles more to himself than to you, "to find ta Destined and tell them ta truth as well, because ta Gods have shown me that they be here with us, in this remote part of ta Neo-Imperium. Me message will stir them too."

He nods to himself at that, before turning his piercing grey eye on you: "And me is doing just that, as ta Gods have required me to do. It be always nice to see ta truth of ta Gods be made reality." He mumbles cryptically, with a wistful smile.

Zorg chuckles while leaning on his staff: "Zorg an old fool may be, but crazy not!" He slowly shakes his head at that: "Yes, ta Gods do speak in me dreams. But me is only ta messenger, not meant to be ta leader. It be ta Destined that're to be leaders!"

He then turns his piercing grey eye on you: "But lead us free, just us slaves on this remote part of ta Imperium, is but a small step fer ta Destined. A step to fully realize who they be! Their true journey be in what they must do in the end ..."

"And that is to restore ta world to what it was supposed to be, instead of ta lie it's now! So have ta Gods shown me, and so ta Destined will come to understand too." He whispers. "Yer minds will be unclouded, aye." He adds with a wistful smile.
"No bother." Zorg replies with a nod. "Me glad to be doing what be required by our Gods." You leave him at that.

Leaning close to him, you blurt out that your dreams have been invaded by strange images lately. Zorg chuckles: "That was expected, fer ta Gods be speaking to ye as well. Haven't ye realized yet that ye be ta Destined?" He nods to emphasize his point.

"Aye. That ye are! But me won't tell ta others ... not yet. Ye must first fully realize what ye are, then choose yer actions accordingly! Find ta courage that's in ye to do so. That's all me can tell ye, as ta Gods want it so. Nothing else can me do."

Zorg then smiles at you, his remaining eye alight with fire, passion and hope: "Think things through!" He whispers. "Ye'll know what to do and when. Ye'll seize ta opportunity. And when ye do, we'll follow!" He nods respectfully at that.
Perplexed by such revelations, you take your leave.
These are the gates of the warehouses, where the ore and rough stones are stored before being shipped out by caravans.
Wandering there at this time would be a serious mistake ... perhaps you should finish what you started?

Of course, the gates are heavily guarded. "What do you think you're doing, mongrels?" One of the overseers snarls. "Get back with the other slaves!" Force of habit and survival instincts make you lower your eyes and comply.
"I don't care what you all think," a frowning Nerylka whispers, "but I have a hard time believing anything this old fool said ..."
Nasslass chuckles: "That old Zorg's one weird and fog-minded fella!"

Zorg is surprised to see you at this time of the day: "Ye have to leave here!" He whispers with much urgency. "Ye know at what time ta meetings are on! We mustn't be seen speaking like this by them overseers!" He then shoos you away.
Zorg is clearly displeased at seeing you: "Me told ye already when ta meetings are on! Are ye dumb? We mustn't be seen speaking like this by them overseers!" He then shoos you away.
Slaves are returning to the mines, under the watchful eyes of the imperial overseers.

A contingent of imperial soldiers are waiting for you and the revolting slaves at these gates. "Stand down now!" A commander intones menacingly. "Only your leaders will face justice, while the rest of you will be returned without harm to your huts!"

In response, you raise your fist defiantly! The other slaves do the same, bellowing their rage and anger! "Fine!" The commander shouts back. "Time to teach you filthy mongrels the lesson you deserve!"
"Let us search the guardhouses on the other side of the gates!" Nerylka exclaims, still on a high after this clash. "Maybe we'll find something useful against the rest of these bastards!"
"What a bash!" Nasslass exclaims, a wide grin across his reptilian features as he wipes clean his weapon.
The imperial guards make an attack!
The gates lie open and broken.
The slaves run into the inner yard with defiance and elation. You can't help but smile at that.
"Ta lesson will be yers to learn, fools!" Zorg yells back, just as the battle is engaged.

These gates are heavily guarded. "What do you think you're doing, mongrels?" One of the overseers snarls. "Get back with the other slaves!" Force of habit and survival instincts make you lower your eyes and comply.
The imperial guards were waiting for your approach!
"We're actually gaining ground!" An elated Nerylka exclaims. "Let's assault the Master's mansion as quickly as possible, while he and his men are still reeling from this defeat!"

The slaves run into the main yard with defiance and elation. You can't help but smile at that; however, you are worried that such chaos may cause a lack of cohesion when you face the rest of the imperial garrison stationed here.

The Imperial Master in charge of the mines is standing outside of his mansion, surrounded by numerous imperial overseers. "Stand down now!"  He intones with authority. "What you are doing will arouse the wrath of the Mentarchs! Think about this!"

He then smiles benevolently and with kindness. "I would not wish for this to happen to you, for you have always been hard working and well behaved. So, only your leaders will be punished, while the rest of you will be returned without harm to your huts!"

In response, you raise your fist defiantly! The other slaves do the same, bellowing their rage! "You've made your choice, then!" The Imperial Master snarls. "May the Sublime Mentarchs find it in their holy hearts to have mercy on your benighted souls."
With these final words, the battle begins!
You and the rebelling slaves ransack the Masters' mansion. To your delight and relief, you manage to scrounge up some useful items.

"Let's bring them front gates down," old Zorg cries out to you and all the slaves, "and onward to our freedom won!" All slaves shout their agreement at this, while Zorg throws you a mischievous wink from his one good eye.
The front gates are wide open. From the looks of it, what remained of the garrison has fled the premises ... most likely to the nearby town, in order to bring back reinforcements.

"We part ways here." Old Zorg mumbles. "Me will take us freefolks deep into ta mountains to hide, while ye must go on." He smiles kindly: "Ye've taken yer first steps into yer journey of self-rediscovery, as ta Gods wanted ye to. But it's not over."

He sighs. "All me is allowed to tell ye is that ye've to seek ta leader of ta rebels of this area. He's known as 'Wildstorm'. Don't ask me why ye must do this: me doesn't know, only relaying what ta Gods want ye to know." He takes a deep breath at that.

"Freedom." He intones reverently, grinning. He then frowns: "Me's no fool. Chances are many of us will be caught again, and put to death. But with ye free to go on, me know that all will be fine with ta world soon." He nods to emphasize his conviction.

"Whathever happens, none of it will matter or even be remembered ... once ta world is set back to what it's supposed to be!" He winks at that, before turning to face the assembled rebel slaves: "We've done our part!" He shouts to be heard by all.

"Ta Destined've done theirs. We must go to ta mountains, while they must go on their journey to set ta world right!" With a sweeping gesture of his staff, Zorg motions the slaves to cross through the gates and follow him.

Jubilant, yet also fearful, the slaves rush out through the gates to head into the mountains. Initially overwhelmed by this mass of running and yelling people, many of them clapping your shoulders and shaking your hands in parting well-wishes,
you finally manage to make a run through the gates.
Going back to the mines would be a sure way to be caught by imperial soldiers!
As you near the well-guarded mines and slave pens, you decide to stay well enough away ... after all, you would not want to be found and captured!
The gates are double-locked.

This looks like the armory and supply depot of the imperial garrison stationed here. The place has been left unguarded, as the bulk of the garrison has been positioned around the mansion of the Imperial Master.
Grinning, you seize the opportunity to grab what you feel you need!
Imperial officers quartered in these barracks rush out to attack!
You and the rebelling slaves ransack the officers' barracks. To your delight and relief, you manage to scrounge up some useful items.
This sign reads: "Ylsasnorh - Northwestern Khanark Rockies Mining and Trading Center".
This sign reads: "Ylsasnorh - Northwestern Khanark Rockies Mining and Trading Center". It also points to the north-east for the Imperial Mines.
This sign reads: "Imperial Mining Center of the Northwestern Khanark Rockies". It also points to the north and west for Yslasnorh.

With them, you contend against powerful beings whose faces and names you cannot fathom. Yet, you know somehow that these shadowy beings are linked with your oppressors, the Mentarchs. So you face them off with a grim smile, trying to smite them all!

A new day begins for you. All your life you have been a slave in the Imperial mines. But you eventually discovered a way to escape this hopeless place, finding enough courage to free yourselves at the risk of being hunted down as escaped slaves.

in order to be free in death of this pitiful life that you were born to live. However, the whispered stories did offer some hope for those who would believe them: rebels, all escaped slaves as it was told, were fighting against the oppressors. Somehow,

such stories did keep hope alive and strong within you, eventually inspiring the courage to escape from the dreary imperial mines and seek out these rebels. And today, after weeks of hiding and fleeing imperial patrols, you have finally found them!

As you gaze around the rebel camp, a bit at a loss, a man and a woman walk up to you. "Welcome to New Canaan!" The man greets you, smiling. The woman nods in greeting, smiling as well. "He's Riel Half-Elven," she explains, pointing to the man, "and I'm

Starina Tearmoon. 'New Canaan' is the name we've given our camp." Riel winks: "I assume you must be hungry and thirsty and all," he adds, "but first we have to take you to our esteemed leader ... you know, making proper introductions and all that."

Starina chuckles. "Riel is ever one for grandiose events and formalities, despite that he's a true scoundrel at heart!" As Riel pretends to be offended by this remark, you laugh along with Starina, having almost forgotten such feelings of elation.

"Miscreants!" Riel adds with flourish. "Here I am trying to restore civility and good manners in us ex-slaves, and what do I get?" He shakes his head gravely, adding to his pretense of dramatic despair. "Come, now!" Starina chimes in, still chuckling.

"Let us go see our leader before our good Riel faints at our utter contempt for proper etiquette! Our leader's house is just ahead, near our temple." You raise your eyebrows at that. "Yes," Riel adds with a smile, "the Gods are still alive!"

You've often heard rumors that the Mentarchs had not killed all the Gods, contrary to what the Neo-Imperium always claimed, and that the Gods were in fact preparing the arrival of the Destined - those who would free all races from the Mentarchs.

Riel shakes his head: "A thousand questions you must have ... naturally! Let us go now see our Leader, and almost all of them will be answered!" At his insistence, and that of Starina's, you let yourselves be taken to the house of the rebel Leader.
(Riel Half-Elven and Starina Tearmoon have joined your party; check out the Allies menu)

As you walk through the camp, you see numerous kinds of folk ... from goblins to ogres, dwarves to elves, and so on. Some are going about menial tasks such as farming or constructing huts, while others are honing their skills at arms.
"Here we are." Starina announces, as she and Riel both motion you to enter this large house.

As the eerie images gradually fade from your mind, you wonder whether the long journey you endured so far did not somehow affect your weary soul ... And yet, deep down, you *know* the images were real and were meant to tell you something.
Looking at each other, you wonder if the dream and this incredible, miraculous event are somehow related. If so, who or what is behind all of this? And what does it all mean?
"Aye." Riel nods. "But you've had yours instantly returned by the Gods! I am sure of this! Could you then be the foretold Destined who will rid the world of the Mentarchs?"
Moved by the reaction of your friends, you smile, reminding them that they *are* part of your group, and thus by definition 'Destined' themselves ... if you all are indeed so.

As you struggle with these questions, you see Riel and Starina gaping at you with awe. "We've had to painstakingly relearn our magical powers from those rebels who had themselves rediscovered them." Starina whispers.
Suddenly, a wave of nausea grips some members of your group. Bending over in pain, they feel as if their bodies are burning up!
The place is closed at this hour.

"Greetings and be welcome!" This man intones, shaking your hand while smiling. His grey eyes are lit with a shrewd intelligence and betray much wisdom and goodwill. "I am Anthraxus Wildstorm." He adds, his voice deep and strong, yet warm and friendly.

A vivid image suddenly flashes into your mind, where Anthraxus Wildstorm's features are replaced by those of a mighty warrior clad in full plate armor. His face becomes hidden by a fearsome, full-face warhelm as he raises a powerful sword!

From within this warrior's helm, Anthraxus' piercing grey eyes burn with the fires of lust for power, of hunger for victory and of unrelenting ruthlessness. How could you have such an unsettling vision, when you have never met Anthraxus before? And what

does this mean? As you begin to sway and reel from the vision's power, you feel Riel grab you to prevent your collapse. "What is wrong?" A concerned Anthraxus asks. "These poor folks must be tired." Riel mumbles, while trying to keep you on your feet.

"It is customary for all newcomers to be introduced to me," Anthraxus continues, "but in your case, I shall make this short so as to allow you a well-deserved rest. A hut will be made available to you: this will be your new home."

Anthraxus smiles: "Go there to rest. I also invite you to go to our commissary to get some basic equipment, as well as food and water. We all share here, so feel at ease to take whatever you need. Then, come back to speak again with me."

He then turns to Starina: "I believe there is plenty of room in yours and Riel's hut?" Starina nods with a grin: "There certainly is! I welcome more folks, since their presence will keep Riel and his advances away from me at night!"

As everyone has a good-natured laugh at Riel's expense, Starina enjoins you to follow her. "Come!" She chuckles, "I'll show you to your new home." Riel lets out a grunt while throwing you a wink: "No one's taking my bed, however!"
As you take your leave, Anthraxus returns to his discussions with his advisors.
"Here we are." Starina announces, as she and Riel both motion you to enter this small hut.
This door is locked.

Numerous folks are sitting at a large table covered with maps and papers. They are actively discussing with each other. All manner of people and races are sitting at this table, such as orcs, gnaths, goblins and elves. Out of these, one man stands out.

Although dressed in simple trousers and shirt, his calm demeanor exudes leadership. Next to him is a robed man who appears to be busy listening to all that is being discussed by the others. This robed man then sees you, peering at you intensely.

With a nudge, he brings your presence to the attention of the first man, the one that appears to be the leader, who in turn smiles and motions you to come to him. Looking at Riel and Starina, they also enjoin you to walk to this man, with a nod.
Armed rebels are standing watch at the gates of New Canaan.
Armed folks are standing watch at these gates. You see among them all sorts of races, such as kobolds, dwarves, furfoots and humans.

"Who are ye and whot are ye doing here?" A burly orc demands sternly, as his armed comrades train spears and arrows in your direction. You hastily tell of your escape from the imperial mines and of your journey as escaped slaves.

"We'll see ta truth of yer story." The orc replies, as a dwarf dressed in brown robes mumbles to himself while gazing at you. "They speak truth." The robed dwarf then proclaims, smiling at the same time. At that, the others clamor their approval.

"Then be welcome here!" The orcs booms with a wide grin. "Be welcome among your peers!" He adds, while motioning you to cross through the opening gates. Amidst the shouted congratulations from the other armed folks, you go through the gates.
"It would seem that we've found the rebel camp!" Nasslass intones with a wink.
The robed man nods politely to you, his piercing gaze being quite unsettling.
This old sign points to the North for Bywater, and to the South-east for Ylsasnorh.
Strong, wailing winds are coming out of this large cave opening.
This large commode would be useful to store any excess equipment you have.

"Welcome back!" Anthraxus beams, smiling warmly. "I trust that you've rested well?" You nod as he invites you to sit along with him. "I understand that all must seem a bit confusing to you right now." He tells you, while glancing at Riel and Starina.
"Welcome to the commisary." A bored storekeeper mumbles as you approach. "Take what ye need, but don't be too greedy. Ye hafta leave some fer the others."
"Yer not allowed there!" The storekeeper warns you.

Anthraxus goes on: "As your new friends may have already explained, you are in New Canaan, our haven and refuge for all escaped slaves of this area of the Khanark Rockies. Over the years since this place was settled, our population has grown!"

He chuckles. "New families have been founded, while other slaves like you have managed to find this refuge of ours ... and all are of course welcome. And so today, New Canaan is a largely self-sufficient community, hiding from our oppressors."

The robed man next to Anthraxus then coughs, prompting another chuckle out of the rebel leader. "Of course," Anthraxus adds, "us rebels have had help all along from those lankharhans who oppose the God-Emperors, good folks like Oberon here."

The robed man bows politely at that, his piercing gaze never leaving yours. "Indeed," Oberon adds, "not all of us born with the Gift of mental powers approve of the mad God-Emperors. In many ways, we are their submissive subjects and thus lack freedom."

Anthraxus nods. "Aye. We non-psionics may be slaves or born of slaves, but all psionics must blindly obey the God-Emperors or face the same end as ours for disobedience: death." He pauses, then brightens:

"However, much hope has been renewed for all slaves and lankharhans since we've found the means to speak with the True Gods once again!" Oberon steps forward at that: "The God-Emperors managed to fool all of us, and our ancestors, into believing

that they had killed all the Gods. Ever since their Second Rising, and establishment of this Neo-Imperium that now rules over much of the World, they have been crafty at erasing magic and faith, thus ensuring the supremacy of psionics as the only power."

"But," Anthraxus interjects, "many throughout the centuries never forgot about the Gods. And of course, the Gods never forgot about us! Thus, slowly but surely, magic and faith was rediscovered, as you have witnessed already." Anthraxus pauses once more.

"Unfortunately, trouble is brewing." The rebel leader goes on. "The God-Emperors have somehow sensed the rebirth of magic and faith, and are therefore wary. In the case of our beloved community, being so close to an imperial town like Ylsasnorh,

we stand much in danger of being discovered by the God-Emperors. Indeed, our magic and faith are begining to stand out as beacons easily spotted by any God-Emperor who would happen to look our way." He sighs while shaking his head in despair.

"It is therefore only a matter of time before New Canaan is discovered: should this happen, we are not strong or numerous enough to withstand a single God-Emperor, let alone one leading a full imperial army against us!" Oberon then gestures to you:

"This is where all of you come into the picture" The robed man muses. "Our priests have received auguries from the Gods, showing them the means by which New Canaan could be shielded from the mental scrutiny of any God-Emperor." Anthraxus nods at that.

"Aye." The rebel leader adds. "There is a cave east of here, called the Cave of Wailing Winds. The auguries have said that this cave leads to a means of protection for New Canaan. Some kind of holy book to be found there, the auguries said." He pauses.

"So," Anthraxus continues, "I charge you to journey to this cave and find this holy book, then bring it back to us so our priests can study it and find the prayers that will create this protection that the auguries spoke of. Here is a map for you."

"I wish you all safe journeys and safer returns." Anthraxus adds, after handing you the map. "Yeah, boss. Thanks a lot!" Riel mumbles, pretending to be irritated. "And do not forget." Oberon adds, while struggling to suppress a chuckle, "Stay clear from

Ylsasnorh, lest you be caught by the imperials!" Starina clicks her tongue: "No worries with me along!" She replies. At that, Anthraxus clasps your arm: "If you haven't yet, go equip yourselves at our commisary." With a firm nod, you take your leave.
Oberon nods to you, his piercing gaze never leaving yours.
Anthraxus is busy conferring with his rebel lieutenants. Having nothing new to report to him, you decide not to disturb him for nothing.
Rebels are standing watch at the gates. Because of the time of the day, no one else is about. However, having been recognized, you are allowed to pass unchallenged.
Rebels are standing watch at the gates, while others pass through the gates going to the farming fields or coming from them.
Folks working the fields wave at you in friendly greetings.
Folks pulling carts loaded with fruits and vegetables are going back to New Canaan. They smile warmly as they pass you by.
Folks pulling empty carts are heading for the fields, no doubts to fill them up with the latest harvest. They nod and smile in greeting as they pass you by.
Folks working in the fields nod and smile in greeting as you pass them by.

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. An elven priestess walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. A furfoot priest walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. A dwarven priest walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. An orc priestess walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. A human priestess walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"

Priests of different races are tending this small temple, while others are conversing with folks seeking guidance or succor. A goblin priest walks up to you, smiling warmly: "Welcome! How may I be of assistance?"
Denizens of the woodlands eye you as prey!
Monstrous versions of nature attack!
You are waylaid by evil creatures!
You are waylaid by opportunistic adventurers!
You are waylaid by marauders!
You are waylaid by barbarians!
Denizens of the area eye you as prey!
You arrive in a dark, damp cave complex. The place is eerily quiet; this makes you wonder how or why are winds gusting out loudly from the surface entrance ...
Pushing on this sliding rocky wall, you find a dark passage leading deeper underground.
You hear some faint rumbling and roaring coming from further up in the north-west of this large cave.
The stalagmites and stalagtites in this area suddenly sprout tentacles and move menacingly toward you!
Overwhelmed, you flee for your lives! Luckily, the ceatures do not seem willing to chase after you.
"Ugh!" Nasslass exclaims with a disgusted grimace, as he is wiping his weapon clean. "Them foul beasties don't even taste good! What a waste, me tell ye!" He then chuckles.

"Hmmph!" Nasslass grunts while wiping his weapon clean. "To think that me heard such nice things about the joy of wanderin' and adventurin' about the world! Bah! More bloody work than fun, me says!" He then winks at you mischievously.
"Well!" Nasslass exclaims, panting and tired. "Never a dull moment fer us, eh?" He then grins mischievously.
"By the Gods!" Riel exclaims, panting and tired. "I knew there would be days like this, but this is getting ridiculous!" He then chuckles to himself.
Riel sighs loudly while wiping his weapon clean. "Is it me, or are we indeed attracting trouble for ourselves?" He then shakes his head, chuckling to himself.
"You know," Riel mumbles while wiping his weapon clean, "we'll reach our quota of allowed kills long before the day is done, at the rate we're going!" He then winks at you.
Nerylka clicks her tongue as she surveys the fallen: "Tsk! I wonder if this mean we're in for a long day or not ..." She muses.

Nerylka bends forward, trying to catch her breath: "You know, this adventuring would be much easier if those stupid things were not so intent on getting in our way!" She then shakes her head in resignation.
"Once again!" Nerylka mumbles, as she sits down a bit to catch her breath. "Another death-defying battle won. How many more before we finally bite the dust?" She sighs loudly at that.
"Damn their eyes!" Starina mumbles angrily while glowering at the fallen bodies. "That'll teach them to try to stop us!"
"Pfah!" Starina exclaims in disgust. "These foul things even smell bad! Who ever said that adventuring was glamorous?" She then chuckles to herself.
"Just once," Starina mumbles between clenched teeth, "you'd think that we would have it easy? But nooooooo! More blood had to be shed instead!" She then shakes her head in disgust.
"Better to live today still," Riel mumbles between each breath, running for his life along side of you, "and then come back to fight another day!"
You hear Nerylka swearing under her laboring breath as you all run away. "Why tempt the Fates in the first place?" She mumbles with irritation.
"Yup! Durn good call!" Nasslass mumbles between clenched teeth, looking warily behind while he runs in order to make sure that you are not being followed.
"That's a nice change!" You hear Starina mumble, not bothering to hide her sarcasm and frustration.

You find skeletal remains lying all about the place, most likely past victims of the creatures you defeated. Seeing that the remains belong to different races, you wonder if you are actually the first ones to have been sent to retrieve the holy book ...
Searching the remains lying here, you find some items of interest.
You hear some faint shuffling sounds coming from the south-west of here.
A swarm of spiders fall from the ceiling!
Your extensive search of this cave allows you to find very interesting items hidden underneath the layers of thick webbing.

It would appear that the queen spider of this place amassed a small treasure from what she would find throughout the caves. Perhaps she was preparing to lay eggs here? Just the thought makes you shiver with dread.
The insides of this cave are filled with webbing. This was probably the lair of the queen spider that you just defeated.

Your close examination of this human skeleton makes you notice something peculiar about it: indeed, the right arm is entended with its index finger pointing to the north-east. It would seem that this person died that way, for some reason or another.
You also find some interesting items.
You notice that the rocky wall here is brittle and cracked all about. Faint glimmers are glimpsed through the cracks: it would appear that something metallic has been covered by dirt and rocks here.
Without proper tools, there's not much you can do.
Success! The rock crumbles and falls away. Through the cloud of dust and dirt caused by the crumbling rocks, ancient doors of rusting steel are revealed!
Thank you for playing Wrath of the Mind Lords. Safe journeys and safer returns!

The ancient doors are covered with arcane and holy symbols, the meaning of which you cannot fathom. However, strong magical energies are coursing through the doors, emanating with an eerie hum that raises hairs like static electricity.
You also notice a large keyhole on one of the doors.

Try as you might to pick whatever lock there is, the doors just won't budge. It looks like the powerful magic coursing through these ancient doors is there to prevent any tampering ... and thus, you would need the appropriate key to open these doors!
Tentatively, you put the rusted key you found  into the keyhole and give it one good turn clockwise ...
The key then disappears into shimmering light and the ancient doors open to leave you free passage!
The ancient, rusted doors remain open, allowing you to come and go as you wish.

Large columns of marble have been erected here. Visibly ancient, they are now brittle, crumbling with age and abuse by the prevailing dampness. Why are those columns here and who put them in this remote place?

The opening of this cave is lined with strange arcane and holy symbols which, from the look of things, where chiselled into the rock ages ago. Unfortunately, you cannot fathom the meaning of those symbols.
Peering into the cave, you see that it leads deeper and down into the ground. Do you go in?
You return inside this cave.

You come into a large cave. At first appearing to be empty, you then notice far to the back a large, eight-armed statue dressed like a warrior. A gleaming sword in each hand, the statue stands poised to attack - although it remains still and silent.

As you approach the back of the cave, you notice a stone coffer flanked by two crumbling columns of marble. Suddenly, the strange, eight-armed statue comes to life! At first turning its head left and right as if shaking off a stiff neck, it then gazes at
you with its glowing eyes. Without taking its eyes off you, the statue takes a few steps forward in order to position itself between you and the stone coffer.

"I AM THE GUARDIAN OF THE KEY." The statue intones, its mouth not moving. "BEGONE OR BE DESTROYED!" It adds, while making swift moves with the swords it is holding to emphasize the point. For a seemingly old statue, it looks quite agile and quick.
Do you leave?
Backing away, the glow in the eyes of the statue dissipates and the statue returns to stillness and silence.
As you step further in challenge, the warrior-statue gives a final twist to its swords in answer. "YOU WERE WARNED." It intones, before launching itself right at you.
The Guardian defeated, it crumbles into rubble and dust. Panting and tired, you set yourselves to look into that stone coffer it was guarding.
Upon your approach, the warrior-statue returns to life. "I AM THE GUARDIAN OF THE KEY." The statue intones once again, its mouth not moving. "BEGONE OR BE DESTROYED!" It adds.
As you approach the stone coffer, its lid begins to glow and lifts up! Peering into the coffer, you find a strange, rusted key.
The stone coffer then disappears!
This cave looks to be empty. You are quite certain that you could safely rest in there.
You spot dangerous-looking creatures in the distance. Will you approach?
The ceiling of the cavern suddenly seems to drop on you!

The trap appears to be activated by pressure of feet, most likely opening the floor to a deep pit. What do you want to do?
Success!
You have managed to jam the triggering mechanism, thus allowing free passage without fear of the floor opening beneath your feet.
Your fumbling triggers the trap, revealing a 20'-deep pit filled with steel spikes!
"Durn good, sturdy building!" Galduur mumbles appreciatively while stroking his long beard. "Methinks this Kith Khanaan must've had dwarven blood in him!" He then chuckles at that.
A trap door opens right under you, revealing a 30'-deep pit filled with pure acid!
Your fumbling triggers the trap, revealing a 30'-deep pit filled with pure acid!

This old, heavy headstone has been etched with intricate bas-reliefs, including an inscription that reads: "FRIENDSHIP ROAD -CONSTRUCTED IN 528 R.R. BY THE PEACEFUL FOLKS OF MOUNTEDGE, NUR'ANAAN AND THE FOREST-KINGDOM OF AURYSTAN".
You take water from this fountain spring, filling up waterskins to the brim.

"Wait for a moment." Raack Strongbow interjects, a look of worry on his face. "I don't think Galduur, or I, are meant to follow you on this journey." Galduur chuckles: "Mayhaps not ye, me old friend, but me knows me can! Me read it in their

little book!" Startled by this revelation, you turn to him. "Well, we was camping and me got bored and found me something to read. How could me know it was not meant fer me to read?" Galduur answers your unspoken question, with a rueful smile. "Anyways,

me's meant to vanish, right? So's the history says in yer book! So, me goes along with ye!" He then turns to a confused Raack: "Here's me shield, old friend. Get it back to the Halls, fer truly it belongs to me kin. Don't ye worry about old me: things'll

be fine and dandy." Galduur then chuckles: "Besides, me got a feeling we'll be seeing each other soon again." He adds cryptically. After embracing a still-shocked Raack and giving him his shield, Galduur sets himself to follow you.

"Well? Let's be off!" He yells. Raack sighs with resignation: "Safe journeys and safer returns, my old stubborn, valiant, fool of a friend." The ranger then turns to you: "Walk far and safe -and take care of him." You nod, clasping his arm in parting.
From out of the shadows of the night, a band of suspicious-looking thugs and rogues surrounds you. "Yer moneys or yer lives!" The largest one demands. Do you hand over all your money to them?

You hand over all of your gold. "Our thanks, good gents!" The large rogue replies with a sneer. "We'll be merciful and let ye live, 'cuz ye were right cooperative!" At that, the band returns in hiding into the shadows of the night.
"Yer lives then, and after that yer gold too!" The large rogue intones, as the band of marauders attack!
You expect a militia patrol rushing in, even if after the fact ... but no one comes.
You wonder just where in the Nine Hells are the patrols at this time of the night.
It would seem that the local militia is not overly fond of patroling the streets at night.
You cross paths with a large, heavily armed patrol of the local militia. Although some of the soldiers eye you suspiciously, you are otherwise not bothered.
You are accosted by a shaggy-looking and alcohol-smelling beggar: "Alms fer da poor?" He asks with a raspy voice.
You are accosted by a young woman holding a sick child: "Please, me lords." She begs, tears rimming her tired and sad eyes. "Could ye spare a few coins so I may feed me family?"
You are accosted by a scraggy-looking kid: "Greetings, mylords. Spare a few coins fer me, so me can help feed me brothers and sisters?"
Do you give one gold piece?
Handing out a gold piece, you then get on your way.
Without further due, you go on your way while ignoring the pauper.

An accolyte from the temple wakes you up: "Apologies, but I must ask you to leave. Might I suggest you return to your homes or, if you are passing through, go rent a room for the night?"

"This ain't no charity! No money, no service!"
"Go take yer seats and a wench will bring ye yer servings."
Soon enough, you are served pitchers of the local brewery. The beer is bold, but bitter.
Rather quickly, you are served large cups of rhum. It is quite tasty, but a bit too spicy.
Soon enough, you are served large goblets of red wine. Quite strong, it is however rather fruity.
"Pfah!" Galduur exclaims with disgust. "Me've had better spirits than this from orcs! It's times like these me wishes me were back in me Dwarven Halls."
"A serving of food is 5 golds apiece, so 30 golds total."
Soon enough, you are served large bowls of steaming beef stew. Although rather salty, it is nonetheless quite filling.
Rather quickly, you are served large plates of bacon-filled meatballs, with vegetables and spicy potatoes. The servings prove to be quite filling and rather nice to the taste.
Soon enough, you are served steaming bowls of chunky beef and vegetable soup. Although the broth is watered down a tad too much, the servings still hit the spot satisfyingly.
"Not bad." Nasslass mumbles, while gulping down his serving with gusto. "Not bad at all, me says!"
"Ugh!" Starrune exclaims, while eyeing her serving with disdain. "Considering what we paid for this slop, why not instead go to a city and pay a little more for *real* cuisine?"
"I guess I have no choice but to drink this ... stuff." Lindanyl intones with disdain, before taking a sip of her drink.
Riel sighs loudly after taking a sip of his drink: "It's not bad. But how I long for some Tanirith wine or even some Wailsrond rhum!"
"Foods with drinks are 10 golds apiece, so that'll be 60 golds total."
Soon enough, you are served large bowls of steaming beef stew and goblets of red wine. Although rather salty, the stew is nonetheless quite filling. The wine is quite strong, but rather fruity.

"It may not be haute cuisine," Nerylka muses between sips of her drink, "but it changes us from those iron rations!" She then attacks the rest of her serving.
"This *is* better than what we'd eat on the road." Raack muses, winking mischievously, before returning to his serving.
"As long as meat's in there," Mrrysh muses, eyeing his serving critically, "then me'll have nothing to complain about!"
Ssyslak is busy (and loudly) eating and drinking his serving, obviously enjoying the meal. However, his table manners are somewhat lacking in decorum.

You overhear a conversation.

"Me tell ye!" A woman exlaims, adamant. "The King's be drowning in debauchery and all sorts of evilness! Each sevenday, he sends out his High Guard to snatch away young girls of proper morals for him to use and abuse in his disgusting orgies!"

"All I know," a merchant intones, "is that the roads aren't safe anymore fer trading! Bands of highwaymen do whathever pleases them, while orcs and goblins have come back in our lands without bother. Our kingdom is doomed, I say!"

"Me heard" a wench muses, quite confident, "that ghosts be roaming around the forest of Aurystan and that they're seeking to leave their cursed ruins to haunt and kill all of us poor folk! Me heard some mage says that they be seeking revenge on us all!"

"Me know me've heard rumors that king Endanuur II be feeble of mind, or crazy, or even both!" A farmer intones. "He's not ruling the kingdom at all, but instead it be nobles and lords of the Iron Court that are the true rulers! What will happen to us?"

"What about the high prices we all have to pay fer our goods?" A shopkeeper demands, her eyes lit with anxiety. "With all them bribes taken by those who should protect us, banditry runs unchecked and the losses they cause'll drive all to ruins!"

"As if this was not enough!" A man exclaims. "Monsters of all sorts are said to be roaming about the cursed elven forest of Aurystan. I've heard mention of a gate in the ruins that opened all by itself, allowing fell beings to enter our world!"

"And what about these unfair taxes we have to pay?" A another woman demands, indignant. "We're being bled dry from all sides while them lords and nobles keep fattening their money pouches! Me tell ye: it won't be long afore we all die of starvation!"

"And what's being done with all this evil banditry and such?" Another man demands, quite angry. "The kingdom's soldiers hide in their forts when there's trouble about but they sure're quick to kick our behinds when we complain too loudly about the King!"

"But that's not all." Another woman adds. "Me also heard that mages have decided to take over the Kingdom, and no one dare stop them! That's why our lords, nobles and soldiers be doing nothing to protect the people -they're all in thrall of them mages!"
Mulling over what you have heard, you get on your way.

A huge metallic door stands here, wedged within megalithic frame of granite, set into the mountain wall. Plain and without any visible markings, the door appears quite of out place here -except maybe for the vegetation overgrowth covering parts of it.
Although obviously ancient, the door is remarkably rust-free and devoid of any signs of deterioration. Try as you might, you find no lock or device which would make this gigantic door open.
Those that have tried are smarting from the effort ... which was to no avail in any case.
With much noise, the huge metal door rises!
You find no trap here.
"This must be the kind of door that requires that strange key." Muses Lindanyl, focusing her attention on the door while frowning pensively.
You stand before another megalithic door of metal.
With much noise, the huge metal door rises. At the same time, the tellurian key shatters apart, obviously spent and now rendered useless.

A beautiful elven priestess stands here, smiling at you: "Greetings, strangers. I have been waiting for your arrival." She announces, with a quiet, but rich, voice. "My name is Lindanyl Goldenfair; I am a humble servant of Labelas Enoreth." She bows

respectfully to you, before continuing: "The Eternal One has been blessing me with a recurrent dream, which commands me to perform two tasks of service. The first task is a message the dream entrusted to me and which I must now impart to you:

To open the doors of old Lankharh, one must find a key created in the golden days of an even older empire." She then pauses, allowing you to absorb this strange message. "Although the dream did not give me any clues as to what kind of key the

message alludes to, nor any hints as to which empire it is speaking of, my own thinking on this has led me to speculate that this key may be some artifact or relic from either the empires of Macremia or Telluria, which preceded that of Lankharh."

She then smiles, excitement lighting her amber eyes: "I am happy to tell you that tellurian ruins lie north-west of here, near the center of the Scaleswamps!" You nod your appreciation at that. "As for my second task," Lindanyl goes on,

picking up from a chair her traveling gear, "I am to join in your noble quest to destroy the Mentarchs once and for all." She then smiles mischievously, locks of her curled golden hair falling rebelliously on her shoulders. "So lead, and I shall follow!"
(Lindanyl Goldenfair has joined your pary. Check out the Allies menu.)

The money is pocketed: "A goblin tribe, the Bloody Bones, has settled south-west of Nur'Anaan. This tribe is ruled by a fearsome shaman-king named Shanaurak. This tribe's been causing lots of trouble and grief -especially around Fort Uppersea."

The money is quickly pocketed: "An orc tribe, the Stormriders, has settled south-west of Mountedge. This tribe is ruled by a fearsome king named Zum Bonecrusher. This tribe's been causing lots of trouble and grief -especially around Fort Hillside."

The money is pocketed: "Lately, a large band of ruthless marauders has been attacking trade caravans around and about Nur'Anaan. Me's heard that their lair lies hiden in the Timberwoods, just next to the city. No one knows who their leader is, however."

The money is swiftly stashed: "Lately, a large band of bandits has been attacking trade caravans around Fort Friendship. Me's heard that their lair lies hiden in the Greenleaf Forest, east of the fort. No one knows who their leader is, however."

The money is pocketed: "Centuries past, the Cult of Graaz'z was strong and sought to conquer the region, but the cult was hunted down and eradicated. To this day, ruins of temples can be found in many places -ruins that are said to hold lost riches."

The money is quickly pocketed: "A Warlord has constructed a castle-fortress west of Mountedge and has been attacking trade caravans regularly. Rumors say he's sponsored by a powerful mage, or that he is allied with orcs."

The money is swiftly pocketed: "Me knows that crypts and tombs of dead kings and queens can be found near Mountedge, Nur'Anaan and Tanirith. These are said to hold countless riches and powerful artifacts -one just has to know how to find and reach them."
