The gates of this castle are guarded heavily by numerous soldiers of fortune, each looking as tough and as grim as the most seasoned veteran you've ever met.
"Hey! Ye stepped on me boot ya durn fool!" A burly warrior intones with a growl. You motice that he is with many friends, who all look eager for a fight.

A drunken warrior bars your way: "Me says ye all look like a bunch of faeries!" He sneers, obviously looking for a fight. You notice that he is backed by many of his comrades, equally drunk and eager for a brawl.
"Hey! Ye made me spill me beer!" A drunken man exclaims, visibly offended. You notice that he is with many friends who are equally drunk.

A drunken man bumps into you: "Hey! Why don't ye watch where ye're going, ya bunch of sorry-looking drudges!" He bellows, obviously irritated. You notice that he is backed by many of his comrades, equally drunk and eager for a brawl.
"Let's dance, then!" The man replies with a snarl, as he and his comrades move against you!

As you try to step away from the fight, you are quickly overwhelmed. Beaten and bloody, some of the brawlers throws you out while laughing aloud. Only later you realize that your money pouches have been also emptied.
The fight turns into an all-out brawl!

Once the fight -and the excitement- is over, everyone returns to their business of enjoying themselves among friends. In the meantime, staffers quietly but swiftly remove the uncounscious brawlers and throw them outside of the place.
"Hah! Me knew ye were nothing but a bunch of sissies!" The man bellows, as he and his comrades enjoy a good laugh at your expense.
As you walk around the place, you bump into other people also moving about. Only after you realize that your purses feel lighter -much lighter.
The place is rather lively, with folks chatting and laughing around a meal or a drink -or both.
You enter the private appartments of the owner of the place.
This chest is empty. Obviously, it was placed here to provide a homey atmosphere to the place.

However, closer inspection reveals a false bottom in the chest. Removing it, you see that the chest is in fact bottomless, opening to a hole in the ground. In this hole, you see a small lever. Without hesitation, you pull on it.
This is the kitchen.
"WHAT ARE YE DOING HERE?" The chef demands, all indignant. "Patrons aren't allowed in MY kitchen!" As he goes on ranting and raving, a wench politely takes you back to the tap room.

A halfing is renting this room: "Who are ye?" He demands, all indignant. "Git out of me room or me'll call the owner!"
A woman is renting this room: "Who are you?" She demands, quite angry. "Get out or I'll call the owner on you!"
A couple is renting this room: "Who in the Nine Hells are you?" The husband demands, all indignant. "Get out or we'll call the owner on you!" The wife shrieks angrily.
A man is renting this room: "Just who the hell are ye?" He demands, quite angry. "Get out or I'll sick the owner on ye!"
You hear a screaming woman being beaten. the sounds clearly coming from behind the door next to your right. Without hesitation, you rush into the room.

You find a poor wench -barely 18 years old- lying on the half-naked bed, her face bloodied and her dress ripped to shreds. A man in robes standing over her turns his attention to you, his face flushed with anger and his eyes burning with hatred.
"Get out of here and mind your own affairs!" He snarls. "You don't know who you are messing with! Michiko may own this place, but *we* run it! And we do as we please!"
At that, the man raises himself erect and starts spellcasting!
From seemingly out of nowhere, grim-looking and shady characters join in to help your opponent!

After the clash, the poor wench runs back downstairs, in tears. Not long after, staffers come to the room to remove the bodies. They say nothing to you, but often they throw your way quick looks of worry and fear. What would they be afraid of, exactly?
You find more of the electromancer's belongings.

To your surprise, you find shady-looking men lounging around the room, as if it was their own. "Who are ye and whot are ye doing here?" One of them asks with a snarl. You notice his comrades slowly putting a hand to the scabbards of their blades.

"Do ye know who we are, who we work fer?" He demands again, before chuckling coldly. "No one messes with us! Too bad ye stuck yer noses where they didn't belong - you'll learn a proper lesson, me says!"
"Welcome again to the Sleeping Dragon." Michiko greets you, smiling warmly.
At that, the shady characters attack!
Attracted by the commotion, Michiko stumbles into the scene, quite shocked. Looking at you, then in turn at your opponents, she smiles grimly and enters the fray at your side!

After the fight, a bloodied and battered Michiko approaches you. "I've been aching for the chance to give those disrespectful ruffians the punishment they deserve and, thanks to you, now I have!" Smiling, she bows to you in gratitude.

She then frowns: "However, this is not the last of them. They moved in a few months ago, taking control of my inn in order to turn it into some kind of base of operations. I was helpless to stop them, since I was alone. But not anymore!"

"I suspect they are part of that marauder gang that has been terrorizing the roads lately. More of them have taken residence in my cellar: get rid of them for me and you will be well rewarded! To reach the cellar, simply go through the storage room."
With a determined nod, you get on your way.
"I've been aching for the chance to give those disrespectful ruffians the lesson they deserve and, thanks to you, now they have learned!" Smiling, she bows to you in gratitude.
Attracted by the commotion, Michiko stumbles into the scene to investigate. Looking at you, then in turn at your fallen opponents, she smiles grimly.
Not having completed your task, you decide not to bother Michiko and leave her to tend to her business.

Smiling, you tell Michiko that you have rid her inn of those ruffians once and for all. "Splendid!" She exclaims, visibly relieved and happy. "I shall honor my word as you have honored yours, noble adventurers." At that, she produces a small chest.

"And something else." Michiko adds, producing a strange pair of gloves. "These belonged to my great-great-great grandmother who was a wandering monk before settling down. She found those gloves during one of her many adventures, and they have since been

passed down in her family from one generation to the next. However, I feel your monk is better deserving than I to honor the memory of my ancestor. I trust these wondrous gloves will be put to good and noble use, instead of acquiring dust."
"Again, I thank you, noble ones." Michiko bows to you once more, out of respect and gratitude. With a nod in return, you leave her to tend to her business.
You go downstairs.
You return upstairs.
You spot a loose tile on the floor, near the wall here. Pushing on it, the wall slides to the right to reveal a door embeded in the stone!
Numerous marauders and bandits are lounging here. Upon your entrance they all turn around to look at you: "Who? What? Get them nosy bastards!" One of them exclaims.
After the battle, you search the chests lying about the place and find some interesting stuff.
You find an interesting map.
This ranger nods politely at your approach, before returning to his conversation with his dwarf comrade sitting next to him.

On second glance, you are startled by the uncanny ressemblance of this man with Strider, the mysterious and secretive ranger you met during your previous adventures in the Sword Lands! But how can this be?

"Is it me, or does this man could easily pass himself off as Strider?" Riel whispers to you, confirming your own questions. "I mean, he looks like him, albeit just a bit younger -by no more than two or three years, I'd say! This is amazing!"
This dwarven warrior nods politely at your approach, then returns to his conversation with his ranger comrade sitting next to him.

This dwarven warrior nods politely at your approach. Then, with a mischievous smile, he turns to the ranger sitting with him: "Me told ye they'd do it. Ye owe me drinks fer the next sevenday, as our bet calls!" He announces proudly, with a chuckle.

"Indeed, you have the keenest eye for bets!" The ranger replies jokingly. "I am Raack Strongbow," he goes on, seeing your confusion, "and this dwarven 'Lord of Bets' is Galduur Ironshield." You manage to hide your surprise upon hearing the name.

"We've been keeping an 'interested' eye on you, ever since your arrival in the area." Raack adds, smiling warmly. "Bah!" Galduur interjects, "What me old friend's trying to say is that he wanted to take care of them bad guys the way ye did already."

The dwarf then leans closer to you in a conspiratorial manner: "Ye see, this goody-two-boots feels he's to take care of everything by himself to protect the folks of the kingdom. Since me knows better than him what's good fer him," he adds with a wink,

"me bet him that ye'd do it by yerselves! And ye did!" Galduur turns back to his comrade, laughing aloud: "See? Me told ye that ye needed to enjoy a good rest, fer once!" In response, Raack pretends to be offended: "Sure. All along, this bet was

an excuse for you to drink your mead without a care, and with this bet you covered your back for a chance to drink some more!" Raack intones, pointing an accusing finger at his friend. "Me couldn't lose either way!" Galduur replies, laughing more.

Then suddenly, Galduur swigs the last of his tankard. "Nothing but me beloved Dwarven Halls mead fer me!" He tells you, with a wink. "In any case," Raack continues, turning back to you while pretending to be annoyed with the dwarf, "I wish to extend well

deserved congratulations to you, for the deed you've accomplished. Galduur and I have been looking into these banditry problems in the last few months, and we've arrived at the conclusion that these marauders and bandits are the tip of a big iceberg."

"Aye." Galduur goes on, with a very serious tone in his voice. "We think there be some kind of network of camps like that one, ultimately leading to someone very powerful who seeks to conquer the Iron Kingdom!"

"Be that as it may," Raack interjects with a wink, "it seems that you brave folks have these matters well in hand: we trust you'll be able to uncover the power behind these ruffians, if you haven't already. Galduur and I will busy ourselves with some

other mischief!" Galduur grumbles at that: "Aye. Fire giants be threatening the new kingdom of Lantharond. Innocent folks be in grave danger there, so off we go!" The dwarf then gathers his gear: "Safe journeys and safer returns!" He bids you,
clasping your hand. "Walk far and safe." Raack adds, doing the same. At that, the two heroes leave the Sleepless Dragon.

"We've been keeping an 'interested' eye on you, ever since your arrival in the area." Raack adds, smiling warmly. Not only does this man looks like the Strider you know, but his voice and his mannerisms are the very same as well. How is this possible?
"Bah!" Galduur interjects loudly, wrenching you away from your musings, "What me old friend's trying to say is that he wanted to take care of them bad guys the way ye did already."

With great care, you explain to the two heroes how you came to be in the past and why. "An amazing tale, indeed." Raack muses, with a rueful grin -so much like the Strider you know. For an instant, you have the urge to ask him about this. However,

Oberon's spell then kicks in to warn you silently against this course of action. "It is somewhat ironic" Raack goes on, "how the long dead past of ages ago collided with the future -your present-, and then finding an escape in our present -your past-!"

Galduur then groans: "Enough! Me's getting a headache already from all that time nonsense!" He then starts batting his hand in irritation at your reaction of disapointment: "Me believe ye, me does." He adds with a gruff voice. "There be folks to be saved

and it don't matter that they be from the durn future -so, of course we'll help ye!" Raack then chuckles mischievously: "Besides, from your account, there's some 'time' before that Primus fellow gets here ... so, why don't we join forces in the meantime

to find out who is the true power behind those marauders and bandits?" In response, Galduur raises a newly refilled tankard of Dwarven Halls mead: "Me'll drink to that!" After gulping down his drink, the dwarf gathers his gear. He then turns to you:

"Well?" He demands gruffly, his fists planted on his hips. "What're we waiting fer? Let us be off, then!" Laughing while pretending resignation, Raack gathers his gear as well: "Are you sure you want the pair of us fools along?" He asks with a wink.

This chest is empty.
Paying close attention to these crates, you notice a loose tile right next to them. Removing the tile reveals a little something that must have been droped and rolled under it, a long time ago.
People come in and out of Nur'Anaan through its imposing gates.

You stand before Nur'Anaan's imposing gates, which are closed at this time. Numerous guards stand on watch from the battlements. "Halt! Who goes there?" The Watch Commander asks. You explain that you are travelers seeking to pass through the gates.
"It'll cost ye and yer friends the sum of 30 gold pieces fer us to open the gates." The Watch Commander intones. Do you pay?
"No money to spare, eh? Then begone, ye paupers!"
"Go on ahead." The Commander tells you, as the gates are being open to let you pass.

"We won't be encouraging them corrupted fools." The caravan Master tells you. "We'll instead set up camp outside the gates until the morn, when the doors will be open. In any case, a job well done!" He then hands you your pay.
With a last farewell in parting, the Master goes on to direct the caravans to set up camp.
The caravan Master comes up to you: "A job well done! We'll now go to the warehouses and unload the caravans." He then hands you your pay.
With a last farewell in parting, the Master goes on to direct the caravans to the warehouses.

A caravan Master comes up to you, already mounted on his horse: "There ye are! The rules be simple: ye get yer pay once we reach the gates of our destination -in the meantime, stay on the road as we journey there!"
The caravan Master then steers his ride around to direct the caravan to depart.
An angry caravan Master rides up to you: "Stay on the road, me said! Better follow me order, or me'll dock yer pay!"
You are waylaid by the main denizens of the Forest of Aurystan!
You see a trade caravan under attack by goblins. Do you help?
Not wishing to be bothered, you leave the ongoing fight behind you.
"Let's give then foul goblins the Hell they deserve!" Galduur yells out, running to the battle and drawing you in as well.
After the fight, a bloody and battered caravan Master comes up to you: "Ye have our thanks, brave strangers! Please accept this token of our gratitude." At that, he hands you a money pouch.
Biding you farewell, the caravan Master rides off to lead the convoy to its destination.
You see a patrol of knights under attack by goblins. Do you help?
"We must help them!" Raack exclaims grimly, drawing his blade and rushing ahead, leaving you no choice but to follow.

them down, but for some reason I can not fathom, they simply refuse to act." He then shakes his head slowly in resignation: "I guess, in the meantime, we'll keep on meeting them head on when they raid. Fare you well, good strangers!"
At that, the knight commander rides off with the remaining of his knights.

"Well, time fer us to be off. Safe journeys and safer returns!" The priest adds in parting, returning to his group and getting the dwarven caravan on its way.

Galduur laughs. "Aye, me's having lots of fun. As ye see, me even found meself new friends to play with, aside from the goody-two-boots ranger!" The priest lets out a bellow: "Bah! Yer all alike, ye adventurers! And we praise Moradin fer that!"

Galduur chuckles: "Aye! Me's been playing a lot lately, with all sorts of beasties and nasties, and praising Clanggedin fer that each time me be drawing me weapon!" The priest laughs: "Count yer blessings! Things're surely too quiet in the Halls lately!"

Galduur laughs:"Aye! Me's been running around and about the lands, looking fer trouble each step of the way!" The priest laughs in turn:"And always finding it, me's sure! Me's looking forward to hear yer tales, once ye decide to drop by the Halls again!"
Although the fort's gates are open, numerous soldiers are on watch at the battlements.
"Time's a-wasting! We cross right through and resume our journey!" The caravan Master orders.
"We're going the wrong way!" The caravan Master tells you, with much irritation and anger. "Time's a-wasting! Turn about now!" He barks.
"We're going the wrong way!" The caravan Master tells you, with much irritation and anger. "Time's a-wasting! We cross right through and resume our journey!" He barks.
This heavily guarded building houses the City Hall and the Magistrates Hall.
These are the mess halls for the troops.
These are dwarven fortifications. Numerous dwarves stand watch from the battlements.
"Only trade caravan convoys may pass through Highgate." A dwarf priest tells you, also standing on the battlements.
"Me bid ye all safe journeys and safer returns." The priest adds in parting. At that, you get on your way.
The Garrison Commander's castle is heavily guarded.

The gates of this goblin settlement are manned by warriors numbering in the hundreds -too large numbers for you to tackle alone. Thanking your lucky stars that none of the golblins have seen you, you walk away from the gates.
More warriors join the fray!

Goblin warriors numbering in the hundreds are lining the battlements. Having spotted the approach of your warparty, they are ready for the fight. "KILL'UM! GLORY TO US!" A goblin leader yells, just as the goblin forces rush out of the gates.

A bloodied knight commander comes up to you: "We'll finish things up here then head back to the Fort to report the news. You should find the golblin king and capture him -or at least, kill him." At that, he returns to lead his troops for the 'clean up'.
The gates of the deserted goblin settlement lie battered, broken and twisted.
The goblin king and his last followers rush out of this cave to make their last stand!
Searching about the cave, you find the accumulated wealth of the goblins.
You also find interesting items.
The garrison commander is standing outside of his castle, reviewing some of his troops.
He nods politely to you as you walk by, before returning his full attention to his troops.

"Be welcome to Fort Uppersea." The garrison commander greets you, as you walk by. "I've heard many good things about you folks, especially concerning the excellent job you did against those marauders and bandits. Resources are hard to come by these days,

and my superiors seem afraid to give us proper orders to act against those who would put the security of the good people of the kingdom in jeopardy. That is why we've been able to do hardly anything against those highwaymen. However, your travails have

given me great confidence in your characters and abilities, and thus I would make you an offer: lead a small contingent of troops and knights against the goblins that have settled south-west of here, and eradicate them. You will be rewarded
generously for this!" Do you accept the commander's offer?
"Of course, we accept." Raack Strongbow interjects, eyeing you sternly.

"It would seem that my confidence in your characters was grossly misplaced." The commander replies with disgust at your refusal. Without further word, he returns his full attention to reviewing his troops.
Do you reconsider and accept his offer to go and rout the goblins?
The garrison commander of Fort Uppersea is sitting outside of his castle, enjoying a breath of fresh air while smoking a pipe.

"Glad to hear it!" The commander replies, quite glad of the turns of events. "Head to the goblin settlement south-west of here; a contingent of troops and knights will be following you from afar, but they'll be right with you once you reach the goblins!"
At that, the garrison commander gets back into his castle
Not having marched yet to the goblin settlement, you decide not to bother him for nothing.

"Victory!" The garrison commander bellows, quite happy with the turn of events. "One of my knight commanders returned and gave me the news. I knew you could do it! As promised, here's your reward." At that he hands you a small chest.
"Thank you again for your fine help and leadership!" The commander adds. "Safe journeys and safer returns." He bids you in farewell, before returning inside his castle.
Do you open the trap door?
The trap door leads to a large, sloping corridor going underground.
A dozen or so horses are here, this large room carved into the rock being obviously used as a makeshift stable.
This is a large commisary. Numerous men are sitting at tables, eating, drinking or just relaxing. Upon your entrance, they all turn to you. "GIT THOSE NOSY FOOLS!" One of them yells.
This is the kitchen. Nothing of interest is to be found here, except for some foodstuffs.
This is a dormitory. Men are in here, relaxing. Upon your entrance, they rise to attack!
You find nothing further of value or of interest here.
You find a couple of chests here, in which the personal belongings of the ruffians are kept.
This is a conference room, with a large table at its center.
Unfortunately, your entrance has disturbed those that were busy planning caravan attacks.
On this large conference table, you find a curious map, among hastily sketched raiding plans and other such paperwork.

This is a nicely furnished study room. Several folks are here, sitting in comfortable chairs. Upon your entrance, they all rise up, ready to fight. "Who in the Nine Hells are ye?" One of them demands. Tall and quite muscular, his dark eyes shine with

At that, Jax and his lieutenants attack!
Chests are here ... but they are empty.
This is a dormitory ... but it is deserted.
This makeshift horse stable is empty, safe for the hay covering the floor and abandoned haystacks.
This looks like Jax' bedroom.

On this work desk, you find an intriguing letter: "Greetings Jax. I agree with your concerns regarding those goblin interlopers. Of course, Bonecrusher wants only to have them be crushed -but it would be catastrophic if he would lead his warriors through

the lands just to get to those goblins. I have of course sent word to Stygiax and he wants us to stay as far away from the goblins as possible while, at the same time, keeping up the rates of our attacks. He told me he is considering the matter.

I suspect he'd like nothing better than to lure those goblins to his side but, obviously, that is an impossibility as long as his lot remains with Bonecrusher -who is, in my own opinion, the surer bet for all of us. I bid you success. Signed: Ariel."
You find a chest here. It is locked.
You set off a trap!
You disable a trap.
After bashing the chest open, you pick up what's valuable from the mess you made.
You find the accumulated ill-gotten wealth of the marauders!
On this large conference table, you find find curious maps, among hastily sketched raiding plans and such other paperwork.

At that, Ariel and her lieutenants attack!
This looks like Ariel's private room.
You find the accumulated ill-gotten wealth of the bandits!

No one seems about this old shack. However, you hear loud snores coming from inside.

An old hermit is sitting on a rocking chair, smoking a pipe. "Greetings, strangers!" He cackles, his face lined by years of outdoor life. "Ye look like fine, swashbuckling adventurers, eh? Well, me got maps to old royal crypts that me could sell ye!"
"Here's what me have. Which map tickles ye fancy?"

"Yes, the Nuramin Dynasty. This was the first royal dynasty to have ruled Nur'Anaan of old, before Ptaraz conquered the city and absorbed it into his Iron Kingdom. This map'll costs ye 2000 gold pieces, so 20 gems in all. Which one of ye'll pay?"
"No money to pay, eh? Well stop wasting me time, then!"
"Here's yer map. Good treasure hunting to ye!" The old hermit adds, with a wink.

"Yes, the Tarturian Dynasty. This was the first royal dynasty to succeed King Ptaraz to the Iron Throne of the Iron Kingdom. This map'll costs ye 1000 gold pieces, so 10 gems in all. Which one of ye'll pay?"

Upon closer inspection, you notice that one of the bas-relief acts in fact as a button. Pressing it, the stone slab slides to the left, revealing the entrance to an ancient crypt!
You return in the crypt.
You notice a loose tile on the floor here. Removing it, you uncover a rusting lever.
Pulling on the lever, you heard something moving with much noise down the corridor ahead.
This rusting lever is hopelessly jammed.
This crypt is empty.
A seemingly bottomless pit blocks passage here.
The door stubbornly refuses to give way.
You have failed.
You nearly stepped on a pressure-tile but, thanks to your attentiveness, you side-step it. With a few rocks, you jam it so as not to cause any problems for you.
You have stepped on a pressure-tile!
The corridor is now hoplessly blocked by a devastating cave in. It would seem that the builders of this crypt made sure no one would go any further than this.
Six large iron statues animate upon your intrusion, moving to attack you!
You come face to face with more crypt guardians!

Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "Queen Nurami II, Seventh in the line of the Nuramin. Reigned 404-421 R.R. Felled by Ptaraz the Mighty; Last Monarch of independent Nur'Anaan".
The door has been somehow fited into the surrounding stone in order to seal this crypt. You see no lock or opening mechanism for this door.
The spell unseals the door from the rock, allowing you to open the door by simply pushing on it.
Your spell unhinged the heavy iron door completely, as its sealing rock crumbles.
You open Queen Nurami II's sarcophagus by sliding its cover. You find only the decomposed corpse of the queen, still wrapped in her death shroud.

You notice that the human shape sculpted on the sarcophagus' cover is holding a semblance of a box, made of old marble as the rest of the sarcophagus. Feeling around the box, you find a little push-button.

Immediately after, a spectral apparition stands behind you!
"Begone from my place of rest, or be rewarded with death!" The floating apparition intones, its voice both whispy and tenebrous.
Do you comply?
As you back away from the sarcophagus, the apparition returns to the beyond and the fire bowl extinguishes itself ... as if nothing happened.

"Ye were warned!" The disembodied voice of the apparition intones. Immediately, it summons help from the shadows, while at the same time the mummified remains of Nuram II rise up from the sarcophagus!
All then move in to attack you!
Looking into the now empty sarcophagus, you find a few things of interest.
You notice a false bottom in the sarcophagus. Removing it, you find many items of interest.
Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "King Nuram I, Founder of the Nuramin Dynasty, First Monarch of Nur'Anaan. Reigned 179-214 R.R.".

The sarcophagus of Nuram the First appears like a solid bloc of black obsidian, without any visible cover or moving parts. It is beautifully etched with bas-reliefs of a wise and brave warrior-king. A faint magic aura also emanates from the sarcophagus.

"The sarcophagus must be protected by powerful magics." Starrune muses, frowning with wariness. "It is best to leave it alone -besides, haven't any of you heard before of the powerful curses great kings can bestow from the afterlife to crypt robbers?"
"I agree." Raack adds, visibly uncomfortable with the whole idea.
"Bah!" Galduur mumbles gruffly. "Me ain't fer liking this tomb raiding we be doing. Me surely wouldn't want any grave robber sniffing around tombs of mine ancient kings!"
Upon closer inspection, you notice that a small bas-relief shaped like a crescent moon can be turned to the left like some sort of flat knob.
Do you rotate it?
The block of obsidian slides loudly to the left, revealing an opening!

As you approach, something rises out of the sarcophagus -the mummified remains of Nuram the First. "Ye have violated my place of eternal rest." The mummy intones with an netherwordly voice, its dessicated eyes glaring with a red glow of anger.
"Now ye shall know the curse of the Nuramin!" The mummy adds, as it summons help from beyond to help it destroy you!
With his last sparkle of undeath energies, king Nuram I curses you!
Galduur goes into a fit: "Me knew something like this would happen, ye bunch of stupid, hard-headed, sons-of-orcs!" He then goes about in a corner by himself, fuming and mumbling more angry words.
In the now empty sarcophagus of Nuram I, you spot some interesting items.
"I told you, haven't I?" Starrune intones, frustrated and angry.
Do you want to force or sneak your way in this cave?

Oberon's 'time' spell begins to ring silent alarms in your head, warning you off against such a course of action. It would seem that tampering with whathever's in this cave is likely to cause dangerous ripples through the timeline.
You enter this cave.
You have found the treasure of the Narosian Dynasty!
You notice that this marble statue is much better preserved than the one to the left. Also, this statue hold the likeliness of a sword.
The statue breaks apart ... and you are left with nothing but useless rubble.
The sword's features shimmer and twist, before becoming real!

"Stand back and turn around." An outerwordly voice intones, as you enter this place. From out of the shadows comes some sort of large armored skeleton warrior, it baleful eyes glowing white with anger. "I am the keeper of these crypts, and no one shall
defile them!" It adds. Do you back away?
"You were warned." The tenebrous apparition snarls, as it summons help to attack you!
You notice that the left hand of this statue can be pulled down like a lever. Pulling it, a large tile on the floor slides over!
Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "King Varos I, The Paladin-King. Fourth and last of the Narosian Dynasty. Reigned 271-302 R.R.".
You trigger a summoning spell as you approach this sarcophagus!
After the fight, you open King Varos I's sarcophagus by sliding its cover. In addition to the decomposed corpse of the king, still wrapped in his death shroud, you also spot an interesting item.
More guardians are summoned by the triggered spell!
Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "King Belos I, Third in the line of the Narosians. Reigned 235-271 R.R.".
You open King Varos I's sarcophagus by sliding its cover. Other than the decomposed corpse of the king, still wrapped in his death shroud, you find nothing of interest.
You notice something glittering amidst the centuries-old soot and dust in this rusting fire bowl.
You trigger a magical trap!
You find a magical trap here.
The trap is disabled.
You are not strong enough to counter this magic!
You detect that this large tile on the floor is covering an entrance of some sort ... however, you can't find anyway to move or slide that tile by itself.

Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "King Naros II, Builder of the Friendship Road, Second in the line of the Narosians. Reigned 196-235 R.R.".
Runic inscriptions are etched on this old steel door. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can read them: "King Naros I, Founder of the Narosian Dynasty. Reigned 157-196 R.R.".

As you approach, the mummified remains of King Naros I rise from the sarcophagus. "Pray, intruders." The mummy whispers, its voice as if coming through an echoing fog. "Pray, for you are about to die for defiling my resting place!"
"Now ye shall know the curse of the Narosians!" The mummy adds, as it summons help from beyond to help it destroy you!
With his last sparkle of undeath energies, king Naros I curses you!
In the now empty sarcophagus of King Naros I, you find nothing of interest.
After the fight, you open King Naros II's sarcophagus by sliding its cover. In addition to the decomposed corpse of the king, still wrapped in his death shroud, you also spot an interesting item.
You enter the inner yards of this old, abandoned castle.

The inner yards are littered with the skeletal corpses of elves. It looks as if they died in some great battle -however, they must have all been stripped of their battle gears after, since only rotting and shriveling clothes remain to cover them.
This rotting ladder leads to the upstairs battlements. Nothing of interest is to be found there, except maybe for more remains of fallen elven warriors.
This looks like a dining hall. More skeletal remains of fallen elven warriors litter the place.
This looks like a humble throne room. The elven lord who lived here must have used this place to receive dignitaries, hear petitions or settle disputes among those under his charge.
Paying close attention to these rotting books has paid off!
This looks like a kitchen.
This is a dormitory.
Some nasties have taken residence here!
This is a storage room.
You spot something glittering under this cot.
Paying close attention to this rack of rotting and shriveling clothes has paid off!
You notice a false bottom to this seemingly empty chest. Opening it, you find something of interest.
You notice that this floor plank is covering some sort of secret compartment. Hacking it off, you discover interesting items that had been hidden there.
You notice that this crumbling column can be moved aside. Doing so, you find a ladder leading underground!

This is some sort of shrine. Beautiful bas-reliefs have been sculpted and painted on the walls and columns, depicting the day to day life of the elves that lived here. From the scenes that you see, their life must have been very close to idyllic.
An invisible barrier prevents you from going further!
The barrier responds with a backlash of pure magical energies!
Guardian spirits appear to repel the intruders that you are!
This place looks like some type of storage room. You see many chests and coffers about.
Opening this chest, you find many items of interest.
You find something of interest here.
You enter these crumbling ruins.
This place appears to have been once a library.

However, its floors are littered with the skeletal corpses of elves. It looks as if they died in some great battle -however, they must have all been stripped of their battle gears after, since only rotting and shriveling clothes remain to cover them.
More beasts join the fray!

As you are about to enter these ruins, Oberon's 'time' spell raises silent alarms in your head, warning you against this course of action. It would seem that exploring these ruins could cause alterations in the timeline.
You then recall having explored buried elven ruins this area in your time, probably this very one -hence, exploring these ruins in this past could indeed cause temporal problems.
You enter this old temple dedicated to Miellakkar, Mistress of the Forests.

The floor of this place is littered with the skeletal corpses of elves. It looks as if they died in some great battle -however, they must have all been stripped of their battle gears after, since only rotting and shriveling clothes remain to cover them.
A powerful magical barrier surrounds this altar, preventing anything from approaching it.
The altar, made of solid marble, is etched with bas-reliefs depicting various forest animals, dwellers and trees.

Paying close attention, you notice that the base of the altar is set into what looks like grooves etched into the floor -probably as part of a sliding mechanism. Looking around the altar, you notice that a bas-relief of a priest of Miellakkar holds a
miniature staff which can be turned like a knob. Doing so, the altar moves!
This place looks like a small chapel.

Suddenly, guardian spirits appear out of nowhere to block your passage. "Defilers!" One of them intones, her whispy voice echoing through the chapel. "Prepare to pay the ultimate price for violating Miellakkar's holy grounds!"
"That's a nice change!" You hear Starrune mumble, not bothering to hide her sarcasm and frustration.
This room is eerily quiet and peaceful.
More banshees appear!
The treasure of this temple is now yours.
The gates to the castle of the Royal Governor of the city are heavily guarded.

Oberon's 'time' spell then raises silent alarms in your head, warning you against seeking entry through the gates. It would seem that seeking out the Royal Governor could cause alterations in the timeline.
You walk right into a harpy nest!
Searching around the place, you scrounge up a few items of interest.
This looks like a business and trade center.
Merchants, caravan masters and job-seeking folk come in and out of the busy and bustling place. Inside, you see a kiosk marked "JOBS". Walking to it, you are greeted by a middle-aged furfoot.
"Looking fer a job, eh?" The furfoot asks, eyeing you critically at the same time. Then, with a petulant sniff, he shows you a parchment sheet: "This is whot me can offer ye. Which job do ye want?"
The furfoot is incensed. "Git out of here and don't bother me no more, ye bunch of sorry bums!"
The furfoot is incensed. "Whot? Ye think me's stupid? Ye already've been assigned a job! Git out of here and don't bother me no more, ye bunch of sorry bums!"

"All right." The furfoot replies with disdain as he scribbles down your names on parchment. "The caravan master'll be waiting fer ye at the *main gates* of the city, first thing in the morn. He'll give ye further instructions then."
You stumble into a greckle camp!
You stumble into a hag camp!
The gates are closed shut here, with double the guards than at the other gates.
"No one crosses into the rebel province!" A captain intones upon your approach. "By decree of his Royal Majesty Endanuur II, the border is closed. Begone!"
At the same time, Oberon's 'time' spell raises silent alarms in your head, warning you against crossing into Lantharond. It would seem that doing so could cause alterations in the timeline.
This musoleum is where King Ptaraz the Mighty and his consort, Queen Tanira, are buried.
Oberon's 'time' spell suddenly raises silent alarms in your head, warning you against entering the musoleum. It would seem that doing so could cause alterations in the timeline.
You then recall having explored this area in your time -hence, exploring this musoleum in the past could indeed cause temporal problems.
The gates to Castle Tanirith are heavily guarded.

As you approach the gates, Oberon's 'time' spell raises silent alarms in your head, warning you against this course of action. It would seem that seeking out the Iron King could cause alterations in the timeline.

You stand before Tanirith's imposing gates, which are closed at this time. Numerous guards stand on watch from the battlements. "Halt! Who goes there?" The Watch Commander asks. You explain that you are travelers seeking to pass through the gates.
"It'll cost ye and yer friends the sum of 50 gold pieces fer us to open the gates." The Watch Commander intones. Do you pay?
People come in and out of Tanirith through its imposing gates.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Fort Tarterys".
This old, worn out sign points to the east for Fort Tarterys, Tanirith and Fort Endanuur. It also points to the south for Fort Riverside and Nur'Anaan.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Surfwoods Hold". It points to the north-east for Tanirith and to the south-west for Nur'Anaan.
This crumbling statue is a representation of Lharishar.

As you enter the main hall of this seemingly abandoned temple, you see a skeletal figure coming to life, slowly raising itself up from a wooden altar, then looking at you with its netherwordly gaze. "I serve the Goddess of Life, even in death." The

apparition intones, its tenebrous voice echoing in the empty hall. "I am charged with keeping this holy place unviolated by would-be robbers and defilers!" With a wave of his bony hands, he summons creatures to help him defeat the intruders that you are!
"Maybe tourism might be better fer me old bones after all" Galduur mumbles, running along side of you as fast as he can on his short, stubby legs.
You find a trap door here. Opening it, you see a flight of stairs leading down.

This hall is filled with columns of solid marble, each column etched with bas-reliefs paying hommage to Lharishar and life itself. Magic permeates the place -probably some kind of preservation magic, since the whole place appears untouched by time.

The spectral wizard you faced off against upstairs materializes before your unbelieving eyes, none the worse for wear after you fought him! "Fools." It intones. "As long as Lharishar's heart beats within these halls, I shall remain to protect them!"
At that, it summons more help to attack you!

This is another statue representing Lharishar. As opposed to the one upstairs, where the Goddess is represented as a caring mother and caretaker, this statue shows the crusader side of the goodly Goddess, bearing shield and sword against evil and death.
Some items sculpted on the statue shimmer and twist, before becoming real!
This is another statue representing Lharishar, now devoid of its 'crusader' gear.
You notice at the base of the statue a small button that you can push. Doing so, the wall behind the statue sinks into the floor!
It looks like you have found the temple's secret treasure trove!
The place is rather lively. Wandering bards and minstrels are playing music, entertaining the patrons for small fees.
A sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "The River's Tap".
One of the wenches calls out to you: "Me apologies, good sirs and ladies, but patrons can't go in there."

As you are going about your way, you hear someone scream: "It's them! They're the ones that foiled Jax!" You barely have time to turn around to see who's yelling before you are forced to fight for your life!

As you are going about your way, you hear someone scream: "It's them! They're the ones that foiled Ariel!" You barely have time to turn around to see who's yelling before you are forced to fight for your life!

As you are going about your way, you hear someone scream: "It's them! They're the ones that foiled Ariel and Jax!" You barely have time to turn around to see who's yelling before you are forced to fight for your life!
"Welcome, good gents!" A burly barkeep greets you, smiling. "What be yer fancy fer today?"
"No money to spare, eh?" The barkeep replies, with much disdain. "NEXT!" He then bellows, looking over your shoulder for the folks standing in line behind you.
"Sure!" The barkeep muses smugly. "It'll cost ye 10 gold pieces fer that, though!" Do you pay?
You leave to to mull over what you just learned.
"Anything else?" The barkeep asks.
"Sure!" The barkeep muses smugly. "It'll cost ye 25 gold pieces fer that, though!" Do you pay?

The money is swiflty pocketed: "There's an old, abandoned temple of Lharishar in the Kragwood, on the west side of the Tarterys river. Me's heard that holy relics have been left there fer safe-keeping! But me also heard that the place be haunted!"

The money is pocketed: "Me's heard that a green dragon has taken into lairing somewhere in the southern tip of the Howling Forest, which is south-east of here. It has already attacked trade caravans and such! Folks're saying its hoard must be huge!"
The money is quickly stashed: "Apparently, a band of brigands have recently set up a base of operation in the Surf Woods, south-west of here. Me knows they've already been attacking trade caravans!"

The money is quickly pocketed: "Rumor has it that the late Warlock Hashuur, who attacked fortress Tanirith some 120 years past, had constructed an underground base on Crab Island, just south of here. His lost hoard may yet still be there!"

You find a large mound in the middle of a small clearing here. Walking around it cautiously, you find a wide entrance leading further underground. However, as you peek into the entrance, two large menacing reptilian eyes stare back at you!
You enter this cave.
As you are about to enter this room, one of the wenches steps in to block your way: "Me apologies, sirs and ladies, but this is the Lords' Taproom -fer members and their invited guests only!"

"Please, let them in!" A richly dressed man, sitting alone in the corner of the room to your left, calls out to the wench. "I believe they are with me!" He adds, smiling while motioning you to join him. Reluctantly, the wench lets you pass.

"Please, do sit!" The richly dressed man greets you. "I know you must be wondering why I'm pretending to know you, but it was necessary for the wench to allow you in. For indeed, I do know of you and wish to speak with you!" He smiles warmly at that.

"My employers and I have heard much good of your recent exploits -mainly concerning your routing of the bandit, marauder and brigand camps. I can tell you with great confidence that my employers are much impressed by your abilities!" He nods to emphasize

his statement. "Forgive me, but where are my manners?" He then exclaims with mock alarm and a chuckle. "I am Ayed Al'Rabin, at your service." He continues, bowing respectfully. "On behalf of my employers, who are constantly seeking men and women of

character and bravery, I would tender their offer for a well paid employment.  All you need is go meet with them, and they'll explain further what they wish to employ you for. Of course, you may refuse -but I tell you: they pay very generously!"
He nods again to emphasize his statement: "Go to their castle, and simply tell the gate guards that I, Ayed Al'Rabin, sent you. The castle is in the Western Province: here's a map of its location!"

After giving you the map, he finishes his wine with one swig and rises to leave: "I sincerely hope you will come and meet my employers! You will see: you shall not regret it -guaranteed!" He adds with a smile and another respectful bow, before leaving.
"I find this a tad too convenient and easy." You hear Raack mumbling to himself.

The gates of these richly estates are heavily guarded. As you approach, Oberon's 'time' spell starts ringing silent alarms in your head. It would seem that interacting with court nobles and lords could cause trouble and affect the timeline.
The predominant denizens of this island eye you as prey!

These old, massive doors of rusting steel are wrought with numerous bas-reliefs of demons and other netherwordly creatures. In large runes, the word "Hashuur" is etched on the upper parts of the doors. No opening mechanism, let alone a lock, are evident.
Pushing the doors open, you return into the underground complex.
You leave this underground complex.

You come into some sort of underground complex dug out of the rock. From the prevailing dampness and the amount of slime and grime on the walls, this place was probably constructed at least a century ago -and left by its constructors not long after.
The question is: what creatures, if any, are now sheltering in this place?
"Something ain't right about this here wall." Galduur mumbles to himself, absentmindedly stroking his beard while scrutinizing the wall to the north.
Searching about this wall, you realize that it is an illusion!
You stumble into some of the new occupants of the place!

From the moldy cots lying about the place, this room must have been used as a dormitory. In a way, it is still used as such by its new occupants -however, because of your previous clash, they were ready for your intrusion and now are ambushing you!
From the moldy cots lying about the place, this room must have been used as a dormitory. In a way, it is still used as such by its new occupants!
An invisible barrier of some kind is blocking your way here.
The invisible barrier is letting you pass!
This used to be a conference room. Nothing of interest has been left here since it was vacated.
As you enter this room, you see many chests lying about -most likely holding a hoard left behind when this complex was abandoned.

Suddenly, a huge demon appears before you, its baleful eyes filled with evil and darkness piercing right through your souls. "I was bound to protect this treasure of the Warlock Hashuur." It intones, acid saliva dribbling from its fangs to the floor.
"My binding servitude irritates me to no end: I am grateful for having this chance to vent it!" At that, the demon summons help to his side to destroy you!
The demon summons more help!
Hashuur's hoard is now yours to take!
These were once the private quarters of the Warlock Hashuur. You find nothing of interest here.
You find a chest filled with treasure here. It looks like you found the true hoard of Hashuur!

From the moldy cots lying about the place, this room must have been used as a dormitory. In a way, it is still used as such by its new occupants -however, they heard your approach and now are ambushing you!
This part of the complex has caved in and sea water is seeping in.
This old temple in ruins is seemingly abandoned. From the remaining markings, scuptures and bas-reliefs, this used to be a temple dedicated to Graaz'z, God of Might, Power and Evil.
Whatever is left of this place is overrun by weed and grass growths -as hard as you try, you find nothing of interest here.
More creatures join the fray!
Aghanauroch summons more help to his side!

Upon your approach, a magical rune appears in flames on this door. Not only does this glyph of warding magically seals the door, but just the sight of it instills a powerful urge to fear this place and turn back with fright!
The glyph is erased!
The flaming glyph on the door responds with a backlash of pure magical energies!
This is an armory.

The moment you step down the last flight of stairs, you are assailed by a darkness of the soul and the foulest of evil that pervade in this place. The old 'holy' places dedicated to the Dark Lord of Might remain untouched by time and are potent still!
The cursed, corrupted spirits of former priests of Graaz'z that died in this temple still roam the ruins, seeking to torment the living foolish enough invade their domain!

You enter a small chapel. You immediately notice two torture beds, covered with long-dried blood stains, lying on both sides of a demonic statue representing Graaz'z. This must have been where the priests made human sacrifices to their Dark God.

Out of thin air, a huge, fearsome demon appears before you. Seemingly made of pure fire and wielding a powerful spear, he stands amidst a circle of flames that burn with malice and hatred. The demon is also accompanied by six, towering fire elementals.

"I am Aghanauroch, servant of the Dark Lord of Power and Might!" The demon announces, his bellowing voice thundering throughout the chapel. "None may defile this place. As decreed by the Dark lord himself, the punishment for doing so is death!"
At that, Aghanauroch and his fire elementals attack!
As his corporeal body disintegrates, Aghanauroch utters a word of power against you before being banished back to the netherworld!

This throne of solid marble is litterally part of the floor. It is as if a huge block of marble had been sculpted into the shape of a throne, its base acting as a part of the floor. This is where the high priest must have sat while presiding ceremonies.
Your discover secret spell tells you that something is hidden underneath the throne. However, you do not know how to access it!
Paying closer attention, you notice a small button at the back of the masive throne. Pushing in, a chest-sized drawer slides out from the base of the throne!

"It would seem that we have visitors." A huge female green dragon intones, as she gets out from the mound. To your horror, she is followed by her mate *and* four dragonets. The sight of this draconic family makes you want to run away as fast as you can!

"It is too soon for us to be discovered." Her mate replies, aloof. "Our children are not fully grown yet." The female dragon grins: "Since I was about to go hunt for our brood, I guess these fools will suffice!" At that, she and her family attack!
Panting and tired, you rummage through the cave-like underground lair of the green dragons ... and find much valuables!
As you enter a small clearing, you stumble into a band of thugs and their dogs who had apparently set up camp here!
Opening the trap door, you go down through a flight of makeshift, wooden stairs.

You enter a hall occupied by many brigands. The place is filled with cots and chairs -apparently being used as both a dormitory and dinning hall. Upon your entrance, all present fall silent and look at you, dumbfounded: "Get'em!" Someone finally yells.
This looks like the private quarters of whoever is the leader of these brigands. Sparsely furnished, it would seem that the occupant moved in here only very recently.

Many brigands have been waiting for you, obviously having heard the clamor of your previous clash. From their attire and grim looks, it would seem that you are now faced with the leading members of this band of brigands. One of them walks forth to you:
"Me don't know who ye are," he snarls, "but as sure as me name's Durnon Ironclaws, ye've put yer dirty noses into someone else's business fer the last time!" At that, he signals the others to attack!
Panting and tired, you take a quick look around about this room: from the large table set in the center and covered with maps and raiding plans, this must then be a conference room.
This corridor is unfinished -obviously, this whole place was only recently constructed and remained to be completed.

On the conference table, you find a hand-written letter tagged onto a small map: "I know this is a burden, Durnon, but this is where Stygiax and Maladore want us to meet their liaison agent from now on, when we need to report verbally".

"Apparently" the letter goes on, "all has been set up for you, Jax and me with the proper privileges and free access to meet the bosses' liaison in the place's member-exclusive area. Until next time, I wish you success! Signed: Ariel".
You find a chest here. Fortunately, it is not locked.
You notice that this chest has a false bottom. Removing it, you find more valuables!
You find the illgotten accumulated wealth of the brigands.
Strewn about in this corner is the brigands' pantry.
As the river flows quietly down to the sea, small fishing boats are anchored with no one about the dais at this time of the night.

Fishing is in full swing on the river, with boats sailing up and down the waterway. Many boats are already reigning in their catches, or other fishermen busy themselves on the dais at preparing their catches for the markets.
All is quiet about the docks at this time of the night, save for the gentle waves of the Sea of Ukkor and the creaking of anchored boats being slowly rocked by the waves.

Fishing is in full swing, with boats sailing up and down the coastal area. Many boats are already reigning in their catches, or other fishermen busy themselves on the docks at preparing their catches for the markets.
You stumble onto a pack of silverbacks resting here!
You stumble onto a pack of evil forest creatures resting here!
You stumble onto a pack of wolves resting here!
You see a caravan convoy under attack by brigands. Do you help?
You see a patrol of knights under attack by brigands. Do you help?

After the fight, a bloody and battered knight commander comes up to you: "You have our much appreciated thanks, good strangers. These brigand raids keep increasing by the day!" He then sighs. "I wish our superiors would give us the order to finally hunt

The gates of the fort here are closed shut and heavily guarded. A corporal walks up to you: "Passage to the wilder lands beyond require a toll, as decreed by the Royal Governor of Mountedge." He intones. "The toll amounts to 1 gold piece a head."
Do you pay?
Not having any money to spare, you walk away.
The gates are opened to let you pass through.
Do you wish to leave or enter the fort?
Enter
Leave
This old, worn out sign reads: "Royal Mines of the Iron Kingdom".
A large bronze sign hangs above the gate leading to this estate. It reads: "Phantagolia Sanctum".
You notice a proclamation of some sort that has been nailed on the wall nest to the estate's gate.
The gate opens by itself!
The gate is locked with powerful magic.
You notice a proclamation of some sort that is nailed on a wall here.

You stand before Mountedge's imposing gates, which are closed at this time. Numerous guards stand on watch from the battlements. "Halt! Who goes there?" The Watch Commander asks. You explain that you are travelers seeking to pass through the gates.
"It'll cost ye and yer friends the sum of 60 gold pieces fer us to open the gates." The Watch Commander intones. Do you pay?
People come in and out of Mountedge through its imposing gates.
A sign hangs above the door of this place: "The Rowdy Tankard".

The money is quickly pocketed: "Me's heard that an old adventurer lives alone somewhere in the Central Province, at the foot of the Khanark Rockies. He's said to have maps to ancient crypts and such."

The money is quickly pocketed: "Me knows fer a fact that there are often agents of this Warlord Maladore hanging about this place. Maladore is the warlord that has set up shop to the west of here -its seems he wants to be kept well informed of our city."

The money is swiftly stashed: "That mage that has built a castle to the south-west of here? Well, me heard that he's a master of lightning and keeps a score of understudents with him, teaching them to become as evil and as powerful as him!"

"Please, do sit!" This richly dressed man greets you. "I know you must be wondering why I'm being so forward, but I was hoping to run into you. For indeed, I do know of your exploits and wish to speak with you!" He smiles warmly at that.

"'Ware!!!" Riel suddenly shouts, as he throws himself into a member of your party. As both crash to the ground, you see a dagger flying past where your comrade was standing a moment before! "Assassins!" Riel snarls, in warning.
From seemingly out of nowhere, daggers hit the mark on members of your party -killing them on the spot!

As everyone scream at what just happened, you try to find those who have assassinated your comrades. But with the ensuing commotion, you can't figure out the culprits. Not wishing to remain live targets, you rush out of this place.
Drawing your blades, you turn around and spot the would-be assassins. Finding themselves exposed, they decide to finish the job out in the open!
"'Ware!!!" One of your assassin comrade shouts, swiftly and deftly deflecting a flying dagger coming your way. In an instant, you realize that you are the target of hired murderers!
Thanks to your hightened awareness of your immediate surroundings, you instinctively deflect a dagger flying straight at your heart. In an instant, you realize that you are the target of assassins!

The gates of the fort here are closed and heavily guarded. "Only caravan convoys heading to the west are allowed to pass." One of the guards tells you, in a tone of voice that hints that he will accept no argument.

You stand before rows of open mines. Scores of miners and helpers come in and out of the mines, with cartwheels loaded with minerals and ores of all kinds. Not wishing to be in the way of such industrious activity, you walk away.
The gates of these orcish fortifications are closed shut. Fortunately, no guard seems to be on watch at the battlements.
The gates of these orcish fortifications are closed shut. Hundreds of orc warriors are standing watch on the battlements. Coming out in the open against them would surely spell your doom.
Deciding to act on the better part of valor, you run away to fight another day. It would seem that you will need to find another means, or another time, to infiltrate these orcish fortifications.
Some of the orc warriors have seen you and sound the call to arms! The gates are quickly opened to let out a swarm of angry orcs!
Sleeping orc warriors on watch are aroused by the noise you make and sound the call to arms! The gates are quickly opened to let out a swarm of angry orcs!
Shapeless and amorphous, you seep through the cracks between the gates and cross to the other side!
You bypass the gates and land on the other side!
The gates are still closed shut ... fortunately, the orcs on watch are still sleeping.
All too obvious in plain daylight, you are quickly spotted by watchful orc warriors!
Deciding to act on the better part of valor, you leave as fast as you can to fight another day.
You pull on the lever to slide off the large steel bar that locks the gates, allowing you to open them.

You pull on the lever to slide off the large steel bar that locks the gates, allowing you to open them. Deciding to act on the better part of valor, you leave as fast as possible to fight another day.
Stealthly, you make your way through the huts as silently as you can.
Warily, you make your way through the orc village being as careful as you can of not rousing anyone.
With as much stealth as you can muster, you make your way silently through the orc huts hoping that you won't rouse anyone.
Your sight being hampered by the darkness, you accidentally bump your boot into some cookery left on the ground here!
Not being able to see much in the darkness, you accidentally tangle your feet into a small armory left lying here on the ground!
With visibility being near to nothing in the darkness, you accidentally bowl over a rack of spears that was standing here!

The orc guards on watch at the open gates of this castle are all asleep. From the bottles lying about them, they must have fallen asleep after having drunk too much rhum and wine. Thanking your lucky stars, you enter the inner yards of the castle.
Wardogs trained by the orcs are lounging about the inner yards of the castle. The moment you step foot in the yards, they rise to alarm!
They are immediately joined by their masters to attack the intruders that you are!

"We must now make a choice." Raack intones, his eyes glittering with excitement. "The castle is surely roused by now, so it is likely we'll be facing orcs at every step we take. Thus, either we leave now or go forth!"
Orcs try to ambush you!
This the the main floor of a guard tower. the orc warriors inside were waiting for you!
These stairs lead to the upper battlements.

Upon entering this feast hall, you find yourselves facing a large orc king, accompanied by his conclave of generals and lieutenants. "Dogs!" The king snarls at you, his eyes blaring with anger. "Ye dare invade Zum Bonecrusher's domain, eh? Ye think

that me castle is nothing but a house to raid and plunder, eh? Well, time's come fer ye to be taught a lesson!" At these words, Bonecrusher's entourage rumble their approval. "Choose one of ye to fight me in battle -just the two of us! Me wins, ye all
will be put to a swift death! Refuse me this, and ye'll all die slowly and painfully!" At that, Bonecrusher's men clamor their approval.
Do you accept Bonecrusher's one-on-one challenge?
"A slow death fer all of ye, then!" Bonecrusher roars.
Which member of your party will fight Zum Bonecrusher?
The fight is on!
"Let the better and mightier win!" Bonecrusher roars, as he draws his battle axe.

As the other orcs celebrate the victory of their king, Bonecrusher turns to you: "Me wins, so ye die swiftly as me promised!" Not about to let yourself be executed without a fight, you raise your weapon defiantly, daring Bonecrusher to come and get you.
As shamans rush in to heal their king, the other orcs advance on you to avenge him!
With the fall of their king and their best warriors, the orcs flee for the mountains.
The gates of the orc fortifications lie open and unattended.
You return in the abandoned castle.
As the commotion dies down, you realize that king Bonecrusher's body is now nowhere to be found!
With a gut-wrenching battle cry, a healed up and refreshed king Bonecrusher joins the fray, along with the remnants of his entourage!
You enter king Bonecrusher's private quarters.

On this table, you find strategic maps of the Iron Kingdom, along with scribbled notes and symbols likened to planned troop manoeuvers and fortifications building. Looks like king Bonecrusher was planning a conquest of the Iron Kingdom.
Among the scribblings on the maps, the following words attract your attention: "Maladore", "Stygiax" and "Marauders".
You find Bonecrusher's personal fortune.

As you approach these gates, you hear a loud, booming voice thundering about you: "LEAVE FROM HERE! TRESPASSERS WILL BE DEALT WITH DEADLY FORCE!" Try as you might, you can't figure out from where exactly this voice is coming from.
From out of nowhere, a party of mages appear and attack!
More electromancers appear in order to join the fray!

The gates open by themselves, allowing you through. "YOU WERE EXPECTED. DO COME IN." Intones a loud, booming voice thundering about you. Try as you might, you can't figure out from where exactly this voice is coming from.
You enter this foreboding castle.
This is a dining room. Unfortunately, mages are waiting for you here!
You come into a study. Unfortunately, mages are waiting for you here!
Rumaging through the room, you manage to find a few interesting items.
A loud, booming, echoing laugh welcomes you as you enter this place.
You enter a laboratory of some sort.
Upon its death, the creature releases a final burst of deadly electricity!
The guardians of the laboratory materialize to repel the intruders that you are!
You enter a large conference room. Many electromancers are waiting for you here!
Help is summoned!

You find many maps of the Iron Kingdom here, all scribbled over with battle plans and troop movements. They look very similar to those you found already in the castles of Zum Bonecrusher and Yon Maladore.

"Welcome!" An old mage greets you as you enter this room. Old and withered in appearance, he nonetheless stands proud and strong. To your dismay, you see Zum Bonecrusher and Yon Maladore standing beside him, their gaze full of hate glaring your way.

Two other electromancers are also standing beside the old mage, looking at you like prey. "You have caused many disruptions in my plans." The old mage continues, with a chuckle. "In fact, you have cost me dearly. But I am a patient man and thus I have no

qualms about having to start over. As sure as my name is Stygiax, I will conquer the Iron Kingdom and become its new monarch - thereby doing away with the shallow idiot currently ruling and wasting away the kingdom's resources." He sighs.

"While I am a patient man, I am however not very forgiving. Much you have cost me, both in time and resources, and now I demand payment from you with your miserable lives!" At that, Stygiax and his allies attack!
Upon closer scrutiny, you notice a small latch on the ceiling here. Pulling on it, you open a trap door with a sliding ladder!
The personal fortune of Stygiax is now yours!
"Begone from here!" One of the warriors intones, menacingly. Do you back away?
The gates are swiftly opened and out comes a large party of riders and warriors to teach you a lesson!
"It's them! They're the ones that have been causing trouble fer our lord!" One of the warriors shouts.
You find Ayed Al'Rabin standing at the gates, arms crossed and grinning. "Lord Maladore will be pleased that ye took the bait!" He intones, before drawing his weapon.
With the gates of the castle lying wide open, do you enter now?
The moment you approach, the gates are swiftly opened and out comes a large party of riders and warriors to teach you a lesson!
These are barracks. Unfortunately, many warriors are here waiting for you!
These are stables.
This is the castle's commisary.
Unfortunately, warriors are waiting for you here!
This is an armory.

On this table, you find strategic maps of the Iron Kingdom, along with scribbled notes and symbols likened to planned troop manoeuvers and fortifications building. Looks like Lord Maladore was planning a conquest of the Iron Kingdom.
Among the scribblings on the maps, the following words attract your attention: "Bonecrusher", "Stygiax" and "Marauders".

As you enter this conference room, you are greeted by a mighty warrior standing proud and menacing among his entourage: "I am Lord Yon Maladore, and I welcome you to my domain." He intones. "You have caused us, my allies and me, much distress."
He chuckles coldly. "But your meddling ends now!" At that, he gives the signal to his entourage to attack!
Upon his death, Maladore's entourage and henchmen flee to the countryside!
Amidst the commotion, you realize that Lord maladore's body has disapeared!
The stables are now empty.
Warriors try to ambush you!
You enter the abandoned castle.
You find Lord Maladore's personal fortune.
An old mariner is sitting on the front porch of his house, slowly rocking on his chair while smoking his pipe. "Well, hello there folks! Are ye looking fer a boat to rent?"
"No money to spare or to part with, eh? Very well then." The old man replies, returning to his pipe smoking.
"Renting me boat costs 150 gold pieces. Which one of ye will pay?"

"Me boat's anchored just at the end of the road here." The old man replies. "Me think me'll get into the city and live the big life a little, with these here money!" He adds with a wink, before leaving his chair and walking away.
The old man doesn't seem to be home.

As you are about to knock on the door of this imposing tower, a chest appears magically. Opening the chest, you find a note atop much treasure. The note reads: "Thanks. Can't meet with you to congratulate you personally due to other obligations. Sorry."
You are then whisked away!
Quite the rude reception!

Oberon is waiting for you, all solemn. "No need to tell me what transpired." He says softly, with a tone of defeat. "I must confer with my peers so that we may decide on what to do, now that Primus has flown the coop." He then sighs, smiling meekly.

"At least, and that is no small feat, you have managed to restore the timeline to its original course. The only problem lies with Maximus and three Mentarchs being still alive -especially Maximus. He is a very clever one, he is!" Oberon nods to emphasize
his point. "We should have thought about this possibility ourselves as well, but ... I suppose you wonder how he managed to power that machine of his to send himself back to the present?"
You were indeed wondering about that, considering that powering time-machines seem to require power stones -the last one of which you yourself saw used up by Primus/Maximus, last year.

"Many old ruins were more or less intact still, back in 529 R.R." Oberon goes on. "He must have explored some of the old macremian ruins in the Khanark Rockies and managed to find a power stone good enough to power his make-shift machine."

Oberon sighs again: "Well, again, the great news is that the timeline has been set aright. Now, it's a matter of formulating the proper course of action to put Maximus, and his three surviving siblings, in check once and for all."

The chronomancer then looks at Galduur, mouth agape and in shock: "What? Who- How?" He then looks at you in panic: "What is *he* doing here with you? And how come my time protection spell did nothing to prevent this?" Galduur winks at you, grinning.

The dwarf hero is obviously enjoying the situation. Oberon finally manages to gather is composure back: "Umm, well ... I *must* discuss this with my peers as well, to ascertain any potential damage to the timeline for having brought Galduur here!"
"Go take a good rest, and we'll meet on the morrow." Oberon finally adds, taking back the Stone of Recall and the Lexicon, before disapearing.
"Ye sure keep strange company!" Galduur muses, chuckling to himself. "So? How about that rest? And mayhaps there be some decent mead here, somewhere?" He adds with a wink.

Oberon is waiting for you, smiling warmly. "Good, you are back! I have great news!" He seems genuinely excited. "After much discussion with my peers, we have established that Maximus must indeed be destroyed -as long as he remains, in a host

or without one, he will always be too great of a threat and is likely to try to alter the timeline again. So, I am sending you back to the present -the correct one, that is, thanks to your efforts- on the continent of Anarym. The Azure Coast area, to be

more precise." Oberon smiles kindly at your surprise. "To make a long story short, the Mentarchs were created through magics and sciences that have been lost since the fall of the Lankharh empire. The place where this was done is now known as the

Forbidden City, located deep in the Forgotten Valley. In turn, this virgin, tropical forest valley lies just east of the port city of Seacrest, on the Azure Coast of Anarym. Once there, you must find the means to access the Forbidden City -sadly, we

haven't yet found out how this can be done, so I'm afraid it will be up to you. Once you reach the city, I'll join you then. We are convinced that Primus/Maximus returned there, after fleeing from you in the past. So, find him and destroy him, along
the three other Mentarchs he rescued!" You nod with determination at that.

Oberon then turns to Galduur, with a mischievous grin: "It would seem that you being brought along with these heroes fits exactly with the historical records concerning your 'mysterious disapearance' and thus poses no danger to the integrity of

the timeline. Furthermore, with the normal timeline restored and all, we called upon someone else to join all of you -someone that I'm sure sir Galduur will be happy to see again." At Oberon's words, in walks Strider!

"Me knew it!" Galduur exclaims, rushing to his old friend to clout him affectionately on the shoulder. "Me knew there was something about yer lifespan!" Smiling ruefuly, tears riming his bright blue eyes, Strider smiles down on Galduur: "Aye, my dear

old friend. All these centuries, how I have hoped that a day like today would come and that we'd be reunited once again!" Strider then looks at you: "I know that I have a long story to tell about my -very- long life, especially to you and to Galduur."

He chuckles. "Let's just say that many centuries ago I fell into a potion bath, and this potion soaked through my whole body, making me age only one day for each year that passes. And yes, I *did* recognize you back when we met 'for the first time' in

the Sword Lands -but of course, I could not tell you that I had already met you in the past!" He winks at that. "Ye silly fool! Always taking on the burden of the world on yer shoulders!" Galduur adds, laughing with joy. After the laughter dies down,

Oberon harrumphs: "Well, of course, we of the Hourglass took a special interest in this exceptional man Zaal -" he then stops himself as Strider looks at him with a friendly warning. "-Strider, I meant!" Oberon catches himself. "Suffice it to say
that this valiant man performed many services for us!" Strider then chuckles: "Well, in any case, it's time to save the world -yet again!" "Durn right!" Galduur adds, with much enthusiasm.
(Strider has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu.)
"Well?" Galduur demands, looking sternly at Oberon with his fists planted on his hips. "What are ye waiting fer? Send us away already!"

Oberon smiles: "I'll use a simple spell of teleportation to send you to Seacrest. My little time spell won't be of much use, except that it will still allow you to understand and read any language. So, we'll meet again once you reach the Forbidden City!"
At that, Oberon casts his teleportation spell.
This ranger is enjoying a good meal with his dwarven companion, sitting next to him.
This ranger is enjoying a good drink with his dwarven companion.
This ranger is in deep discussion with his dwarven companion sitting next to him.
"Now begone and don't bother me no more!"
You remember that you have to meet a caravan master at the main gates of the city.

"You do not know what ye have done." One of the cleaning wenches whispers to you, as if answering your unspoken question. "These ruffians have taken over Lady Michiko's inn. They even lounge in the lady's private quarters -but do not bother lady

Michiko with this, for she is too proud to ask for help, and she is always watched by those sitting in her quarters. Ye should simply leave things well enough alone, so as not to endanger Lady Michiko and us!" With a sniff, the wench walks away.

You approach Michiko and begin to ask her discreetly about what is going on. With a sharp shake of her head, she wards off any questions. Pretending to look over some paperwork, she then hands you a quickly scribbled note:

"Secret lever in chest. Corridor to luxury rooms." Without anything further and still acting casually as not to arouse any suspicion, she motions to the patron standing in line behind you in order to serve him.
Michiko has removed the lever to open the secret door.
A large pool of water is here. From the darkness of the water, this pool must lead deep under the earth and most likely back into the sea.
You overhear a conversation.

"I dunno." A merchant mumbles. "Seems to me that this old hermit living all by himself to the north, in the wilderness, is just plain crazy!" A woman nods. "Yup! Me heard that he worships demons and all!"

"I tell ye!" A man mumbles. "A bunch of ruffians have taken over the place! And lady Michiko can't do a durn thing about it!" A woman agrees: "Oh my! Yes! What is she to do, all alone, against those bandits?"

"Me saw it with me own eyes!" A man mumbles. "A bunch of ruffians have taken over the place! And they keep roughing up the poor wenches!" A woman agrees: "Oh my! Yes! What is lady Michiko to do, all alone, against those bandits?"

"Me tell ye!" A man exclaims. "These guys in the corner are Galduur Ironshield and Raack Strongbow!" Another man makes a grimace: "Bah! Even if these be who ye say they be, them high and mighty adventurers speak only with their own -when they want to!"
The creatures summoned by Chlorophus swiftly return to the swampish grounds from whence they came!
Chlorophus summons more help!
This statue representing Graaz'z in his demonic form radiates an almost palpable aura of evil.
Risking possible retribution by the evil God, do you try to destroy the statue?

The statue crumbles loudly under the barrage of your bashing. With this unholy icon destroyed, it will be only a matter of time before the aura of evil permeating this place eventually fades into nothingness.
The statue's aura disappears, rendering it quite normal. With this unholy icon nullified, it will be only a matter of time before the evil permeating this place eventually fades into nothingness.
Graaz'z sends a few demons to avenge the affront you have commited against him!
As the waves of the Everspring Lake wash gently over the shore, small fishing boats are anchored with no one about the dais at this time of the night.
Fishing is in full swing on the Everspring Lake, with small boats already reigning in their catches or other fishermen busying themselves on the dais at preparing their catches for the markets.

An old fisherman approaches you, sucking on his lit smoking pipe: "Ahoy, there! Would ye be looking fer a boat to buy? I'd sell ye mine fer 500 gold pieces!" He tells you,  showing a toothless smile. What do you answer?
