"Great!" The old fisherman replies gleefully, as he pockets the money. My boats anchored just at the end of the dais. I wish ye good sailing!" At that, he walks away.
"Not enough money, eh?" The old man cackles. With a snort of disgust, he walks away.
The old fisherman is still walking around the dais, smoking his pipe. Do you approach him to buy his boat for 500 gold pieces?
Calling out the old man, you walk up to him in order to announce that you've reconsidered his offer. "Oh, really?" He asks, showing his toothless smile. "Fine by me, if ye have the money!"
This old watchtower looks to have been slowly crumbling to ruins out of neglect for decades on end. However, you notice that its front door is rather new, probably for having been installed recently.

As you open the door, an old, graying druid stands in the way, his arms crossed and glaring at you with anger. He is covered by years of dirt: "Be ye gone from me place!" He snarls, as a wild look slowly creeps into his dark eyes. Do you leave?
Without a word, you leave the old druid alone.

"I told ye to be gone from here!" The old, dirty druid screams, standing within the door's frame of the crumbling watchtower. "I, the great Chlorophus, have me plans of conquest  to take care of! I can't be bothered by scum like ye!"
"I'll show ye, bottom-feeding scum that ye are!" Chlorophus replies, frantic and agitated. He immediately begins to chant a spell: "Spirits of the swamps, I bid thee to come to me help!"
Chlorophus has summoned creatures to fight by his side!
Curious, you decide to take a look inside the old, crumbling watchtower.
You return inside this place.
You hear low growls and much water splashing coming from behind the two steel doors just ahead of you.
You enter a large, featureless room. It is dimly lit and filled with swamp water.
The waters suddenly come alive!
You enter a messy and dirty laboratory. Bottles of foul smelling chemicals as well as other suspicious components lie about the floor and tables of the place.
You also notice numerous discarded egg shells, dessicated and difformed crocodile embryos, as well as half-dissected small crocodiles, littering the floor and tables.
In this heated hearth, you see half a dozen large crocodilian eggs incubating. Their outer shells are rubbery and therefore very recently layed.
These stairs are filled with rubble and debris.
This room looks to have been Chlorophus' private chamber. Obviously, the mad druid was not much into the pursuit of comfort and luxury.
You find Chorophus' most valued belongings.
You enter what is obviously a dark and damp cell. Numerous bones and skeletons lie about the moldy floor. Opposite of you, you notice a lizard man chained to the wall.

The chained lizard man is dressed in his traveling gear. Although not showing any wounds, he does look drawn and weak -probably from lack of water and food. Do you quench his thirst and feed him a bit?
After freeing him, the lizard man gulps down the water and the food you gave him -all the while staring at you cautiously with his piercing yellow eyes.

"You have my thanks, good strangers." He intones with a rumbling voice, bowing his head in gratitude. You are somewhat surprised that he speaks the common tongue with near-perfection. "My name is Ssyslak. I am a pariah among my people."

He emits a sound akin to a sigh of sadness. "My people all too often stand on the dark side of things, which has always went against my own principles. Still, I was tolerated for I am the best hunter and tracker of my village. But lately, evil snake-like

human priests have taken over my village, claiming kinship with my people but in truth beguiling them into becoming their puppets." He pauses to take another sip of water. "Like I said, my people are well known for their dark ways; however, they

have never bothered the humans and elves to the south, preferring to keep to themselves here in the swamps. But these snake priests are enticing my people to actually march against those to the south, for their own dark plans." He shakes his head slowly.

"So I spoke out against those evil strangers -but then was forced to flee from my village in order to save my life. For a while, I wandered in these swamps -which I know rather well- until I decided to make the trek to the south and warn the good peoples

there, perhaps even recruiting help to free my village from the dark influences of the snake priests. Unfortunately, I was captured by this mad druid." Obviously grimacing with pain, Ssyslak goes on: "He has been experimenting with crocodilians,

seeking to mutate them into powerful monstrous versions. That crazy man told me that, since I'm a lizard man, he wanted to try the process on me to see what would happen. And then, you came along and freed me from whatever dire fate awaited me."

Ssyslak then rises up from the damp floor to bow respectfully to you: "Again, I thank you for your generosity. I would be proud to fight by your side, if only to repay in a small way the debt of gratitude that I owe you."
Do you take Ssyslak into your party?

Grinning -and thus showing his fearsome rows of teeth- Ssyslak takes out a wrinkled sheet of parchment from his backpack: "I am happy that you accept me into your group. Please, have this map that I have made of the swamps."
(Ssyslak has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu.)

"Forgive me for asking," Ssyslak continues as he sets to follow you, "but I would be honored if you'd consider helping me get rid of the snake priests from my village. I know I'll remain a pariah, but at least I will have done what's right by my people."

This lizard man has been dead for at least a week or two. The foul smell of his decomposing corpse makes you sick to your stomach. The poor wretch must have been captured by Chlorophus for whatever mad designs the druid had in store for him.
Ssyslak bows his head in an obvious gesture of disapointment. "I understand and respect your decision. By your grace, I shall take my leave." Without further due, the lizard man walks away.

"My friends." Strider chimes in. "As I am a ranger, so is this noble, principled lizard man. This I know to be the truth that I sense from him. I'm convinced that he would be an invaluable asset to us, especially in these dangerous swamps."
Do you reconsider?
From the corner of your eye, you notice Strider shaking his head slowly. He is obviously at odds with your decision.

"Ye know," Galduur grumbles with a low voice, standing right behind you to make sure that you hear him, "Me've always known that only brain-dead fools refuse to listen to me friend's wise counsel. Until today, me never thought of ye as such."
At that, he turns around to stand by Strider's side, not bothering to hide his scowl of contempt for you.
Not wishing to be bothered, you leave the lizard man to his cruel fate.

"I'll not stand idly back while you decide to be cruel!" Strider intones with much anger, glaring at you as he takes out water and food from his backpack. "I sense goodness in this one -perhaps you shouldn't be so quick to judge." He adds with a scowl.
After freeing him, the lizard man gulps down the water and the food Strider gave him -all the while staring at you cautiously with his piercing yellow eyes.

Mentally reviewing what Oberon told you before you arrived in the past, a quick calculation of the time elapsed since your arrival tells you that Primus/Maximus has probably landed in the past by now.

The gates of Castle Lorill are closed. "No one is to see the king at this hour!" An elven guard yells out, from the battlements. Only then you notice that several elven soldiers are standing watch on the battlements, their bows at the ready.
The gates of Castle Lorill stand wide open but heavily guarded by elven warriors.

"Halt, strangers!" An elven commander wards you. "Only folks with a duly scheduled appointement may have an audience with his Majesty, King Olorin Starsong. And I would know if a party of wayward adventurers such as you have indeed such an audience!"

As you walk away, you hear one of the soldiers mumble to one of his comrades-in-arms: "Say, doesn't the high priestess of Labelas Enoreth mentioned something about having to find a group of strangers for a quest, or something?"

As you back away, the commander adds as an aftertought: "I don't know if this can apply to you, but honored Lindanyl Goldenfair has left word that she is seeking a party of strangers for some reason or another. She is at the temple of Labelas Enoreth."

As you walk away, you hear an elven warrior mumble to one of his comrades-in-arms: "Funny coincidence, but I heard that the high priestess of Labelas Enoreth is seeking a group of strangers for a quest, or something. I wonder if these folks are them?"

"Be welcome, honored one." An elven commander intones respectfully to Lindanyl. The elf priestess acknowledges him silently with a bow of her head. "King Olorin will be pleased to see you again." He adds, as you are lead to the King's throne room.
Seeing that you are ready to leave, elven warriors respectfully escort you out of Castle Lorill.
A small fountain gently trickles water into a small shallow pool. Numerous exotic fishes swim lazyly within the water.
"Halt!" An elven commander wards you. "Only folks with a duly scheduled appointement may have an audience with his Majesty, King Olorin Starsong!"
A fanfare heralds the entrance of new visitors into the glorious Court of the elven king of Lorill.
"Visitors of the Court may not enter here!" An elven warrior wards you.
Creatures from the underearth are wandering into this dark place in search for prey!
Curious and bold creatures are wandering about the place, in search of prey!

The elven king is attending to the affairs of the Court, discussing about matters of state with his advisors and generals. One of the advisors sees you and whispers in his ear. Turning to look at you, the king nods and invites you to approach him.
"Greetings to you all and be welcome." King Olorin Starsong intones, noding his head slightly. His demeanor is rather aloof and distanced.

"It is good to see you again, Lady Lindanyl." He adds, smiling warmly to the elven priestess. "I trust these are the adventurers you were meant to meet and accompany?" Lindanyl bows respectfully: "Yes, your Majesty. We are soon to leave on our quest."

"As you may have already surmized," the King goes on, looking at you severely, "our fair and prosperous kingdom remains guarded from the intrusion of strangers. our policy is to allow only trade caravans within our border, but not curious or likely ill-

intentioned wanderers. This policy may seem harsh, if not xenophobic; however, it has allowed the preservation of our kingdom, its beauty and its values despite lying so close to cities of men and gnomes. Even lizard men and trolls from the Scales Swamp

seldom intrude within our borders, knowing all too well the fate that awaits them at the hands of our valiant -and ever vigilant- warriors. Thus, I trust that you are aware of the honor we have granted you by allowing you freedom of wandering within our
borders, and that you shall behave accordingly. I bid you safe journeys and safer returns." At that, the king returns to his discussions with his advisors and generals.
"You honor us with your blessings, your Majesty." Lindanyl replies, before bowing respectfully to king Olorin. Following on her cue, you bow in turn and take your leave.
King Olorin Starsong is attending to the affairs of the Court, discussing about matters of state with his advisors and generals. Not wishing to bother him for nothing, you walk away.
A sign hanging above the door of this establishment reads: "The Griffon's Lair - Tavern and Inn".
"Our rates are 10 gold pieces per head, so that'd be 60 golds total." Do you pay?
"Rooms are upstairs. Take the stairs at the south-east end of the inn; yer room's the one at the end of the corridor."
You enter your rented room.
You leave your rented room.

"Me's heard that them elves of Lorill are as protective of their borders as ever!" A man exclaims. "Well, it's their kingdom! They simply do what other kingdoms do!" A woman replies. "Beside, they do good trading, so who cares?" Another man chimes in.

"Did ye heard the howls from Grag Keep last night?" A frightened woman asks. "Aye. Me've always known this foul place to be haunted!" A man replies, gravely. "Good thing the old Keep sits isolated in the middle of Everspring Lake!" The woman adds.

"What happened to that crazy druid, Chlorophus?" An old man wonders aloud. "Ye mean since he was driven out of the area after trying to conquer us with his earth monsters? Rumor has it he's lying low in the old Watchtower in the swamps!" A woman chimes.

"Me tell ye that Librunae's spirit haunts the ruins of her house!" A man exclaims. "How so? The witch was destroyed by that foul wyrm Black Kiss, ten years ago!" A woman replies. "May she rest in peace, the good soul that she was." Another man mumbles.

"Me tell ye: she's that dragon-hunter, Draconia Nah'Li!" A man whispers, looking over to a woman clad as a warrior and sitting alone. "Really? She must be hunting fer the wyrm Black Kiss, then!" A woman adds, nodding in earnest.

This woman, clad like a warrior, is sitting alone at her table. Silently eating her meal, her dark brown eyes reflect a rough and brooding nature. You can tell from the dust and dirt on her clothes and armor that she travels a lot.
Do you approach her?

"Whot do ye want?" The warrior-woman asks you testily, noticing your scrutiny. Satisfied at having taken you aback, she smiles mischievously: "I be Draconia Nah'Li, dragon-hunter by trade and dragonslayer by fame. Whot are ye about?"
What do you reply?

"Really?" Draconia asks coldly, slowly rising from her table. "How about one of ye jesters put up some muscle behind them fighting words?" At that, she draws her sword. Which one of you will face off against this dragon-hunter?
"Let's dance, then!" Draconia Nah'Li adds, as she waves her sword masterfully in a dizzying flurry of moves.
"Not bad, fer a jester!" Draconia muses with a smirk, sheating her sword while picking up her gear. "Next time, be careful to who ye mouth off!" She snarls, before calmly walking out of the place.

"Not bad, fer a jester!" A battered and bloodied Draconia mumbles, before quaffing a healing potion. "Not bad at all. Too bad yer a bunch of fools, else we could've made a durn good team." She adds, before calmly walking out of the place.
"Stop bothering me, then!" Draconia retorts with a snarl, before returning her attention to her meal.
Draconia Nah'Li, the self-appointed dragon-hunter and dragonslayer, is again sitting here eating a warm meal. Her clothes are still dusty and dirty from traveling.
"Whot do ye want now?" She asks with exasperation.

"Really? What chance indeed!" She replies, smiling warmly while shaking your hand. "I happen to be chasing after the same wyrm. The Lord of Calember has recruited me services just fer that -he'll pay me well!" She chuckles at that.

You mentioned that you also took the job from Adventurers Inc. "Hah!" She exclaims, quite amused. "Well, me don't see why that'd be a problem -all me needs to do is bring back one of the wyrm's horns as proof. So, why not team up, then?"

"Praise Huurme for this chance meeting!" Draconia exclaims, visibly happy with your choice. "Together, we can't fail! Me suggest we search around the ruins of Librunae's house. She was a good witch that fought Black Kiss ten years ago, when the wyrm

came to the area to hunt for food and treasure. She died in the battle, although she wounded the beast badly and forced it to retreat to its lair -somewhere in the Scales Swamps. Here's a map of Librunae's ruins: maybe we'll find a clue or two there?"
After giving you her map, Draconia Nah'Li picks up her gear and sets herself to follow you.
(Draconia Nah'Li has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu.)
The gates of Castle Calember are heavily guarded.
"No one is to disturb the King!" One of the guards snarls.

"Well, it be time fer me to claim me reward!" Draconia muses, grinning. "It's been fun!" She adds as she shakes your hand, before walking to the gates. You are surprised to see the gates open quickly for her.
Just as you set yourselves to follow her, the gates are swiftly shut. "No one is to disturb the King!" One of the guards snarls.
The gates of Calember are closed.
"No one enters or leaves the city at this time of the night!" A guard intones. Looking up, you see numerous guards standing watch on the battlements, armed and ready for trouble.
People and trade caravans are coming and going through the gates of Calember.
All is quiet about the docks at this time of the night, save for the gentle waves of the Azure Sea and the creaking of anchored boats being slowly rocked by the waves.
The docks are quite alive with activity, with mariners, sailors, fishermen and merchants going about their business .
These gates of Edgemoor are closed shut, barricaded and heavily guarded by the town's militia.
"Sorry, good gents," one of the guards tells you, "but these gates must remain closed. Too often do dangerous creatures from the Scale Swamps wander here and try to enter our peaceful town."
Edgemoor Manor is well guarded by the town's militia. "No one is to bother the Lord of Edgemoor!" One of the guards intones, before escorting you off the premises.

The gates of the town of Edgemoor are closed shut at this hour. You also notice numerous militia soldiers manning the gates; one of them throws you a warding glance. It would seem to no one is to enter or leave the town at this time of the night.
The gates of Edgemoor are open, with a few militia soldiers standing watch.

There is a lot of coming and going through the gates of Seacrest. Indeed, merchants, travelers, sailors and all sort of people pass through the gates. You also notice numerous soldiers on watch at the battlements.
The royal estates of the King of Seacrest are heavily guarded. Right now, the gates to the estates are closed shut.

Court nobles are entering the royal estates of the King of Seacrest, probably after having been summoned to attend a session of the Royal Court. Numerous soldiers keep watch at the gates, preventing commoners from entering the estates.

A royal carriage is leaving the royal estates of the King of Seacrest. Considering the size of the escort, a member of the royal family must be sitting inside. Numerous soldiers keep watch at the gates, preventing commoners from entering the estates.

A luxurious carriage is leaving the royal estates of the King of Seacrest. Considering the size of the escort, members of the nobility must be sitting inside. Numerous soldiers keep watch at the gates, preventing commoners from entering the estates.
"Begone from here!" One of the soldiers intones in warning. "Lurkers in the night are not welcome near his Majesty's property!"
These are the barracks and military headquarters of the royal army of Seacrest. You notice numerous soldiers and knights standing watch or training.

The gates of Wavyn are closed shut at this hour. You also notice numerous militia soldiers manning the gates; one of them throws you a warding glance. It would seem to no one is to enter or leave the town at this time of the night.
The gates of Wavyn are open, with a few militia soldiers standing watch.
You spot a patrol of elven warriors. They leave you in peace.
Seemingly out of nowhere, numerous elven warriors surround your party!

"Peace and prosperity to our glorious kingdom." Sarin Moonbow announces to the warriors. "As a loyal subject of King Olorin Starsong and warrior of Lorill, I offer myself as voucher for these friends of mine - whom I am escorting as guests as well."

"Free passage granted." An elven commander replies, before giving the sign to his troops to resume their stealthy patrol. As the warriors disappear through the forest, Sarin winks at you: "Good thing you chose to have me along, eh?"

"Strangers are not allowed within the borders of our Kingdom of Lorill, unless escorted and spoken for by one of our own!" An elven commander intones. "We offer you the choice of leaving our lands in peace or by force."
What is your choice?
Peace.
Force.
Choosing to leave peacefully, the elven warriors escort you politely outside the borders of their Kingdom.
"Repel these intruders!" The elven commander orders his warriors.
Overwhelmed, you flee for your lives! Luckily, the warriors do not seem willing to chase after you.
Panting and tired after this clash, you decide to leave the territory of the Kingdom of Lorill. You certainly do not wish to have more elven warriors drop on you.
Folks working the fields wave at you in friendly greetings.
Folks pulling carts loaded with fruits and vegetables are going to the markets of Seacrest. They smile warmly as they pass you by.
Folks pulling empty carts are heading for the fields, no doubts to fill them up with the latest harvest. They nod and smile in greeting as they pass you by.
Folks working in the fields nod and smile in greeting as you pass them by.
All is quiet in Wavyn at this time of the evening, with no soul about the fields. Even the militia soldiers of the town seem sparse.
Militia soldiers are standing watch around Wavyn Manor.
"The Lord surely can't be distrubed at this time!" A militia soldier intones, having spotted you. Giving you a final warding glance, he resumes his watch.
"If ye wish to see the Lord, ye might find him in his farming fields." A militia soldier intones, having spotted you. Giving you a final warning glance, he resumes his watch.

You find a portly man toiling the fields here. Every so often, he stops to give instructions to his helpers strewn about the fields. You notice that he is watched over by four militia soldiers. As you approach him, they turn to stare at you in warning.

"What brings visitors to our quiet community?" The portly man intones with a smile, wiping his hands on his breeches to shake your hand. "I am Nathan Wavion, Lord of Wavyn. I bid you welcome!" He greets you. "What brings you to Wavyn?" He asks.

Trying not to be too obviously evasive, you reply by mentioning that you are travelers simply enjoying the countryside of Seacrest. "Ah ... adventurers, then!" Lord Wavion muses with a wink. "It is good happenstance that you came to Wavyn, for we've been

having some problems lately with giant humanoids. They live in the mountains nearby just north of our town, they they all too often try to breach our battlements - most likely to raid from our fields and cause other types of havoc. Although we have a

protection treaty with Seacrest, I am loathe to ask them for help on this matter - since the treaty is mostly related to outright aggression from another city or kingdom. So, I ask you good adventurers instead: if you get us rid of these fearsome
creatures, I'll reward you handsomely!"
We'll do it.
We're busy.
"Great!" Lord Wavion replies, obvisouly happy at you decision. "Come back when you'll have done the deed - you know where to find me!" He adds with a wink and final handshake in parting.
As you leave, Lord Wavion returns to toil his fields along with his helpers.

Smiling, you tell Lord Wavion that you have taken care of the problem. "Really?" The Lord replies, quite surprised. Glancing to one of his helpers, he asks: "Good Lander. Would you be so kind as to verify the truth of this claim for me?"

Wiping sweat from his brow, the man named Lander turns around to face you. You notice that he wears a holy symbol dedicated to Agrah, Goddess of agriculture. After a quick spellcasting and a short moment of concentration, he opens his eyes: "They do

speak the truth, Lord." He proclaims, smiling warmly. "Superb!" Lord Wavion exclaims, shaking your hand. Digging into his pocket, he hands you a small pin: "This heirloom is one of many that belong to my family. It is now yours with my gratitude!"
With final partings, you take your leave.
"As you wish." Lord Wavion replies, visibly disapointed by your refusal. "I bid you a peaceful stay in our town." He adds, before returning to the toiling of his fields.
The portly Lord Wavion is again busy at toiling his fields along with his helpers.
Not wishing to bother him without a valid reason, you continue on your way.
Rummaging around the cave of the giant trolls, you find a few items of interest - no doubt acquired by force, theft or murder.

This tower-fortress looms silently and mysteriously. Obviously thousands of years old, its crumbling walls are littered with holes and gaps that have formed after ages of disrepair and neglect. You doubt that any of its upper floors have survived either.
Do you enter inside this tower-fortress?
You find on this strange wall dwarven runes which you manage to decipher.
You read once again the dwarven runes etched on this strange wall.
A bright light envelops you and transports you somewhere else!
As you step on the stairs, a bright light envelops you and transports you somewhere else!
You disturb the current occupants of these ruins!
Wandering creatures eye you as prey!
You find what seems to be the accumulated wealth of the barrow trolls. They probably amassed this after extensively foraging around the ruins.

You enter a large hall filled with stone columns. Evidently thousands of years old, the place is damp and slimy, yet quiet and still. You notice that numerous bas-reliefs of dwarven kings, heroes and warriors are sculpted on the towering columns.

"If this place ain't the upper level of a dwarven undercity," Galduur mumbles, quite awed,  "then I'm a bearded elf!" He then shakes his head in sadness: "The place must've been abandoned ages ago - chances are lots of nasties have moved in since."
From the broken cots and rusted weapons lying about this room, you reason that this must have been once barracks for dwarven warriors.
From the broken tables, chairs and shelves lying about this place, you guess that this once was a meeting room of some sort.
From the broken cots, chairs and shelves lying about this place, you guess that this once was a resting place for dwarven officers.
From the broken chairs and tables lying about the place, you reason that this once was a common eating hall.
This place was once a kitchen.
This old, slimy and damp storing room is occupied!
"This here wall feels strange!" Galduur mumbles while stroking his beard pensively, as he is gazing critically to the wall next to you. "Me's sure that the thing can be moved!"
Paying closer attention, you notice that one of the rocks on the wall is loose - pulling it, the wall sinks into the floor!
Paying closer attention to the wall next to you, you notice that one of the rocks on this wall is loose - pulling it, the wall sinks into the floor!
Thanks to your detect secret spell, you feel that something is amiss with the wall next to you. You are sure that the thing can be moved to reveal a secret passage - if only you could figure out how.

You come upon another large hall filled with columns that are sculpted with bas-reliefs of dwarven kings, heroes and gods. However, the place is littered with refuse of all sort and is quite foul-smelling. You can also hear occasional shouts or screams.

A makeshift barricade of rocks and woods has been erected here. Numerous bones and skulls of various humanoids have also been put in display about this barricade, as if to ward off intruders. Luckily, no one seems about.
You have entered a section of the dwarven undercity that must have been once a highly populated residential area. Now, all you see is accumulated refuse, dust and rubble lying all about the place.
You run into a patrol of the creatures that have taken residence in the area!
The sounds of the battle attract more creatures!
It would seem that you have found the accumulated wealth of the creatures inhabiting this area of the abandoned dwarven undercity. This wealth must have been gathered slowly by constant foraging.
You have entered a section of the dwarven undercity that must have been once a residential area for the wealthy. Now, all you see is accumulated refuse, dust and rubble lying all about the place.
The mystic wall lets you pass through!
An invisible mystic wall prevents your passage!
You teleport yourself on the other side of the mystic barrier.

You notice a makeshift barricade of rocks and pieces of wood erected at the end of this corridor. Numerous troll-like creatures are standing watch at this barricade. Lucky for you, you have not been spotted yet.
The defenders of the barricade sound the call to arms at your approach!
You enter a dwarven hall of worship. Aside from more huge columns sculpted with bas-reliefs of dwarven kings, heroes and gods, you notice a large altar of stone at the other end of the hall.
This altar of stone radiates strong magic and appears to remain undesecrated, despite its age and the millennia since the dwarven undercity was abandoned.
Upon closer inspection, you notice a small button at the frontal base of the altar. Pushing on the button, the altar sinks into the floor!
You find treasure!
You also notice numerous stygian trolls that have taken up residence here - and they are not very amused by your intrusion!

You enter a large communal hall which served once as a market place, a center of craftmanship and a processing station for mining spoils. Numerous rooms that were once shops, forges and smitties are set all around the central hall.
Something that looks like it used to be a large mining shaft has been boarded-shut here, probably by the stygian trolls. Do you remove the wooden boarding planks?

With a few sound sweeps of your weapons, you blast the wooden planks to shards, revealing a shaft going deep into the underearth. There used to be an elevator, but it is rusted and beyond use. However, old stairs go down the shaft as well.
Using the old, crumbling stairs, you get down this mining shaft.

You come upon a large throne hall, probably the one used by the past dwarven kings of this abandoned undercity. Now, numerous stygian trolls and strange creatures wander about the hall, obviously at the service of a wizard sitting upon a large throne.
"Who dares disturb me?" The wizard demands angrily as he stands from the throne, his voice booming from the other end of the hall. "Who dares disturb Mergamnon?"

"Mind Lords? You mean, Mentarchs?" Mergamnon replies in surprise. "I remember reading somewhere that they were created during the hey-days of the Lankharhan empire, but ..." He frowns pensively, then snaps his fingers in earnest.

"Yes! I remember now: they were created in what is known today as the Forbidden City. This old and ancient place lies in the south of the Forgotten Valley, which lies to the east of Seacrest." He then frowns again: "Now that you have your information,

I'll be sending you back. I do not want to be disturbed with impunity, and that is why I established myself here so that I may conduct my magical research in peace. It looks like I'll have to reinforce my mystical walls to prevent any more intrusions

such as yours. Bad enough I've had to 'convince' those stygian trolls to serve me, while keeping away the rest of that useless ogre, gnath, dogre and minotaur rabble!" At that, Mergamnon weaves a spell and teleports you back to the surface!

"Tellurian key?" Mergamnon replies, a bit confused. "You mean, crafted by Tellurians? This place used to be a dwarven undercity, not a Tellurian city!" He exclaims, quite offended by your question. He then frowns: "However, I've heard that the lich

Aztranak once found one - but why he needed one, I do not know. What I DO know is that the lich's resting place lies somewhere in the Scales Swamps, north of Seacrest." He then frowns again: "Now that you have your information,
"Then pay for your impudence!" Mergamnon spits in reply, ordering his servants to attack!
"Now is the time to face me, fools!" Mergamnon intones, flanked by his understudies and his personal servants!

"I'll be sending you back, then. I do not want to be disturbed with impunity - that is why I established myself here so that I may conduct my magical research in peace. It looks like I'll have to reinforce my mystical walls to prevent any more intrusions
This massive throne of solid granite was once sat upon by mighty dwarven kings. You see numerous dwarven mystical runes and holy symbols etched in silver all about its base.
Upon closer inspection, you notice that one of the etched symbols is protruding slightly from the granite. Pressing on it, the throne sinks into the floor!
This place looks like a dormitory. No one is present at this time. However, searching about the place allows you to find some interesting items.
This room has been set up like a large laboratory equiped with its own library. unfortunately, those currently running experiments are not happy at all to see you!
Rummaging through the lab and library, you uncover a few items of interest to make your own.
You stumble into Mergamnon's private chambers, along with his personal fortune!
"I thought I had seen it all," Sarin muses as he wipes his weapon clean, "but it looks like I was mistaken - again!"
"Do things ever get any easier with you folks?" Sarin wonders aloud with a wink, as he cleans his bloodied weapon.
"I've always fancied myself the unyielding adventuring type." Sarin mumbles as he tries to catch his breath. "Now, I find myself longing for the peace and tranquility of my Lorill!"
"I knew the road to our quest would be frought with perils," Lindanyl muses aloud while trying to catch her breath, "but I never imagined we'd face such odds!"
Lindanyl shakes her head in resignation as she wipes her weapon clean: "You know, this adventuring would be much easier if those obstacles were not so intent in stopping us!"
"Another one!" Lindanyl mumbles, as she sits down a bit to catch her breath. "How many more battles before we are sent to the Mystic Halls of the Infinite One?" She sighs loudly at that.
You are ambushed!
This part of the ancient dwarven mines is flooded.
You hear disturbing, slurpy sounds coming from the end of the cave here.

You come upon a pool of the darkest liquid you have ever seen. This liquid seems as if made of pure shadows, slurping and swirling around slowly within the pool. You are nearly overwhelmed by a nauseating aura of evil radiating from this liquid.
Do you get closer to investigate further?
You swiftly back away.
Just as you make one step closer to the pool, a large globe of darkness rises out from the pool!

"I AM OBLIVIOX." The shadow globe intones, communicating to you via telepathy. "I DO NOT WISH TO BE DISTURBED FROM MY POOL OF SHADOWS. OTHERS DID THAT, AGES AGO, AND I WAS FORCED TO DESTROY THEM AND DRIVE THE REST AWAY. PREPARE TO MEET THE SAME FATE!"
Obliviox summons help from the shadows!
At that, Obliviox attacks!
The pool reverts to normal, underground water!

"Looks like we now know what brought about the fall of Duhelarholme." Riel muses aloud, as he gazes in surprise at the pool. "The dwarves must have dug too deep here and exposed some kind of portal to the plane of Shadows."

"I agree." Strider chimes in. "This Obliviox creatures must have kept the natural portal open throughout the ages, probably feeding on anything that wandered too close to the pool." He nods pensively at that.
It would seem that you have indeed found the cause for the abandonement of the dwarven undercity, all those centuries ago.
The gates of Goldylock are closed and locked-shut at this time. You notice numerous gnomish warriors on guard at the battlements.
The gates of Goldylock are open, allowing trade caravans and travelers to come and go. You notice numerous gnomish warriors on guard at the battlements.
Numerous gnome warriors are standing watch at the castle of their King. "No one is to disturb our good King without proper invitation from him!" One of the warriors intones.
You disturb a den of wolves!
A sign hanging above the door of this establishment reads: "Moorholme, Tavern and Inn -Use the basement stairs".

Mrrysh sniffs his drink and makes a grimace of disgust: "Phah! This no good! Me hates alcohol!" Pushing his drink away, he whips up a gourd filled with milk and takes a large swig from it. "Ah! That's a drink fer a warrior!" He intones with satisfaction.
Without a word, the barkeep leads you to your room upstairs.

"Nothing much," the barkeep mumbles, before leaning to whisper in a conspiration manner. "Except fer that durn catman, who sits alone in the corner of the tavern. Now, me don't mind him much, 'cause he keeps to himself and bothers no one. Me heard

that he's from that place called the Forgoten Valley. What riles me the most is that the fellow won't drink nothing but milk, juice or water! How can me make money then?" With a sniff of disgust, the barkeep returns to his affairs.
"Many to tell ye!" The barkeep replies, smiling greedily. "But each one'll cost ye 20 gold pieces to hear!" Do you pay?

The barkeep pockets the money. "Me's heard that the elves of Lorill are very protective of their borders. Ye can enter their territory only if ye are accompanied by one of their own, not just any other elf! So, be advised if ye plan to visit there."

The barkeep swiftly takes the money. "Rumor has it that the crazy druid Chlorophus is lying low in the old Watchtower in the swamps, just north of here! He once tried to conquer the Seacrest area but was driven out by adventurers. He's a dangerous man!"

The barkeep quickly grabs the money. "Me heard that Librunae's spirit haunts the ruins of her house. The good witch was destroyed by that foul wyrm Black Kiss, ten years ago. No one knows why her spirit remains ..."

The barkeep pockets the money. "Me heard that ancient ruins lie in the middle of the Scales Swamps, just north of here. But with the place crawling with crocs, trolls and lizard men, no one's ever had the guts to explore these ruins."

The barkeep swiftly grabs the money. "Me heard that a powerful lich of old made his crypt on a small island in the Scales Swamps. Me don't remember his name, but that lich once ruled over almost all of the Azure Coast, hundreds of years ago!"
This cathoon warrior seems quite out of place, sitting alone while brooding over a tankard of milk. Do you approach him?

"Greetings." The cathoon growls, in the typical speech maneurism of his people. "Me is Mrrysh Walksfar, of the honorable Leorrh Nrresh Pride. Me be on a quest to find help. My Pride be threathened by evil Mayaltecs. Ye want to help Mrrysh?"
"Fine." Mrrysh replies with a snarl. "Leave me be then."
Mrrysh Walksfar is still sitting here alone, nursing a tankard of milk. Do you offer to help him?

Mrrysh nods silently to show his gratitude at your acceptance to help him. "Me pride is peaceful, living off hunting and farming in the Forgotten Valley. The Mayaltecs not always evil, but snake priests have poisoned their brains. Now they want to

destroy us Cat People. We need strong warriors and mages like ye to help us defeat the snake priests. Me also is searching for Tecoltitan, honorable mayaltec warrior and friend who also fights to drive away the evil from his own people. Us must then go
to Forgotten Valley and fight the evil snake priests as soon as we can travel there. Here's a map of the area where my pride lives." After handing you a map, he gathers his gear to join with you.
(Mrrysh Walksfar has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu.)

The entrance to this mine is closed off with tons of rubble. The crumbling of the entrance was obviously done intentionally and deliberately, with the evident purpose to seal completely the entrance of the mine.

A gnome miner stops by your side, seeing your inquisitive scrutiny at the collapsed mine entrance. "Good day, strangers!" The gnome beams. "Yer probably wondering why we did that, eh? Well, sixty years ago, we tried to reach the fabled mines of

Duhelarholme and ended up running into the same evil darkness that destroyed the dwarves of then. Because this happened thousands of years ago, we never thought that this evil would still be down there - but it sure was! So, we had no choice but to

collapse the whole mine and, to make sure, the entrance too! Since then, we've never had to fear of this evil darkness, especially since our other mines do not communicate with the old ones from Duhelarholme! Some tale, eh?"
"My pleasure, folks! Safe journeys and safer returns to you!" The gnome miner replies, before stomping off to join his bethren in a nearby mine.
This mine remains hopelessly closed off with tons of rubble.

"Duhelarholme is an ancient dwarven undercity that was founded thousands of years ago, right under Lake Everspring just west of here. On the small island in the center of the lake, the founders constructed a fortress-tower to act as fist line of
defense against the outside world and also as a trading post. Today, that fortress-tower is called Grag Keep."

"The dwarves that founded this ancient undercity were of the clan Duhelarhym, and so they named their city Duhelarholme. It is said that even to this day, only dwarves of this clan -if it still exist- can enter the undercity from Grag Keep. In any case,

legend has it that the dwarves of then dug too deep in their search for valuable minerals and metals, and ended up awakening a great darkness of evil. This nightmarish being killed almost all of the dwarves - the few that survived abandoned

Duhelarholme, never to return. It is believed that the lost undercity is cursed - but maybe not. Me say this because rumors abound that a powerful mage chose recently to settle all by himself in the abandoned undercity - for what purpose, me don't know."

"I did not see it for meself when we happened upon it, for I was still a tad too young to go into the mine. But from the sole survivor of the mining expedition that encountered it, I've heard that this thing lives in a pool of black water and is shaped
like a giant globe of solid darkness, or shadow. We know that it somehow commands the shadows, for it summoned shadow creatures while it attacked our lost kin. A terrible being indeed!"
A sign of wrought bronze hangs above the door of this establishment, reading: "The Merry Mermaid".
The place is quite full and very lively.
Just as you are to grab the knob on this door, a wench stops you: "Sorry, good gents. But patrons aren't allowed there."
"It may not be nectar, but it still hits the spot!" Sarin muses with a wink, while hoding up his drink for a toast.
"More of this awful stuff!" Starrune intones with a sniff of distaste. "I suppose we've not much of a choice."
"I knew adventuring implied sacrifices," Lindanyl muses with a grimace of distaste, "so eating this must be part of those sacrifices."
"Let's teach ye a lesson in manners instead!" The man replies with a snarl, as he and his comrades move against you!

A militia patrol barges in. "Just what's going on here?" The captain demands. As patrons identify your opponents as the instigators of the brawl, the captain orders his men to pick up the culprits and throw them in jail.
Not wishing to wait for a militia patrol to come and investigate, you swiftly make a run out the door!
"It's them!" You hear someone shout. "Let's do it!" To your surprise, you find yourself against assassins!

As the patrons return to their business and pleasures, you notice a parchment sheet on the floor. It must have been dropped by one of the assissins during the clash. Picking it up, you notice that it is a map.

This elf sits alone, enjoying a hearty meal and a goblet of wine. "Greetings, strangers! I see that you are adventurers like me." He offers his hand for a warm handshake. "My name is Sarin Moonbow. I come from the elven forest-kingdom of Lorill, just

north of here. I've been living the quiet life for a tad too long and I am looking to join a band of foolhardy adventurers to bring excitement and swashbuckling into my life. So, may I join your merry group?"
"Very well, then." Sarin replies with obvious disapointment. Bidding you a polite farewell, he returns his attention to his meal.
Sarin Moonbow is still sitting here, enjoying a meal. Do you reconsider and invite him to join your group?

"Praise the Fates!" Sarin replies, visibly happy at your acceptance. As he gathers his gear, he turns around with a frown: "Say ... before I left Lorill, I heard that a priestess of Labelas Enoreth -or Quanthaas, as you know him- was looking for a group

You notice a small draft coming from the surface, through small fissures in the rubble that is blocking the mine.

With surprise, you recognize this dwarf as being the same who was in charge of the branch of Adventurers Inc. in Aranys, a couple of years ago! He has likewise recognized you: "What? Ye again? Here, on Anarym?" He demands, seemingly outraged.

"It's because of ye that I'm stuck here, an ocean away from th' Sword Lands!" He adds, pointing an accusing finger. "Bad enough I had to leave Aranys an' work in Tanirith after ye did yer trouble there, then they sent me reopen the branch in Aranys after

Your intense search about this area allows you to spot the entrance to a grotto that has been heavily camouflaged. Just as you begin removing the underbrush covering the entrance, the residents of the grotto come out to investigate!
"Ye already have a job, ye lousy sonsoforcs!" The dwarf yells angrily. "Begone from here and don't ye come back until ye've finished th' job already assigned to ye!"
"Durn it! This job's been done already! I curse the paperwork mess I'm in! Ye have to choose something else!"

"The woodland park at th' center of Seacrest has a nice little lake in th' middle of it. Lately, weird monsters have been coming out of the lake to attack the poor citizens of th' city. So, find th' lair of these monsters and destroy them all."
"Ye'll get paid only once ye've done the job!" The dwarf adds, before returning to his business of ordering his impossibly messy paperwork.
"Back already, eh?" The dour dwarf snarls upon seeing you. "Here's yer money." He hands you your reward.

"A large group of bandits calling themselves th' Highwaymen Band have been attacking folks and caravans around th' bridge that crosses the Everspring River, just north and east of here. Find them and destroy them once and fer all!"

"Well, we've been having lots of problem with strange woodfolks, lately. Bad enough we get annoyed by nasties from the Scales Swamps every now and then, now these nasties from the woods just south and est of our town keep attacking good folks!"
"Greckles have been harassing folks near th' town of Edgemoor. We think that their lair is somewhere in th' small forest just south and east of th' town. Find them greckles and be rid of them!"

"Known as Black Kiss, this nasty female dragon has been terrorizing th' area on and off fer years. She's rumored to lair in th' Scales Swamps, far north of here. Find her, kill her and destroy her eggs, if she laid any. Just bring back one egg as proof!"

"This ancient undercity was abandoned thousands of years ago. To access it, you must reach Grag Keep, an ancient fortress-tower that used to be a trading post. It sits on th' island in the middle of Everspring Lake, just northeast of here. Good luck!"

"This nasty lich ruled over most of the Azure Coast hundreds of years ago, then retired to his crypt that was built somewhere in the Scales Swamps far north of here. Find his crypt and destroy the sonsoforc once and fer all!"
"Hello, there!" chimes a middle-aged, portly furfoot, smiling gingerly. "I am Rogo, professional cartographer! Welcome to my humble map shop!"
"Now, which one of my maps would be of interest to you?"
"No money to spend or that you wish to part with, eh? Very well! Come back anytime - I'm open between the ninth and the twenty-first hour of each day, every day of every sevenday!"
"Yes. This is the basic, usual map of the Greater Seacrest area of the Azure Coast. Nice to carry with you to easily find your way around here! That one costs 10 gold pieces." Do you pay?

"The dwarven clan of the Duhelarym founded a great city underneath Lake Everspring, some five thousand years ago. As elves and humans gradually settled along the Azure Coast, new opportunities of trade for the dwarves were available. Thus, they

constructed a fortress-tower on the small island that lies in the middle of the lake, which served not only as a trading post but also as a first line of defense. As kingdoms and cities were born and later destroyed, the duhelarym profited greatly from

trade and were renowned for their exquisite craftmanship in metals and gems. Their undercity, Duhelarholme, acquired many names in those time - the humans called it Tora-Khaar and the elves called it Arkelonia, for example. Interestingly, the dwarves

were excedingly overprotective of their holme, refusing anyone other than duhelarym dwarves to enter it - even excluding dwarves from other clans. This self-imposed isolation eventually cost them dearly, for they mined too deep in the underearth and,

according to legends, awoke some sort of great evil. No help was sent to the dwarves, and much of what happened really remains folklore at best, because the dwarves were too secretive about their affairs. One thing is certain: they never asked for help

and they were forced to abandon Duhelarholme. Again, legends say that only a few dozen kins of the clan survived whatever they awoke, deep down in the underearth. Since then, the undercity has been pretty much forgotten, whereas the fortress-tower built

by the duhelarhym would be occupied often by mages, lords and would-be warlords. Today, this place remains barely standing and is known as Grag Keep. Legends insist that the means to enter lost Duhelarholme are to be found in Grag Keep - hence, there
are many scholars and mages, seeking knowledge or power, are eager to know more of such means to enter Duhelarholme and plunder its secrets."
"Would you like to hear of another topic?"

You must understand that these two empires were incredibly advanced both in arcane arts and technology; hence, terrible weapons which blended the two arts were created and used during the Great War of the Empires; with devastating results as well.

"Where to begin? One must journey back in time some fifteen millennia, during the age of the empires of Telluria and Macremia. Both empires emerged on our continent of Anarym, with Macremia more to the north and east, and Telluria to the south and west.

Explorers from the two empires traveled far and wide, settling colonies nearly throughout the continent and beyond. One Tellurian colony was found north of here, in what is known today as the Scales Swamps. Back then, that area was a lush forest. But as

Such terrifying weapons were of course used by the major colonies of the empires over here, unleashing destruction and havok that not only shook the earth, but created new rivers, seas and mountains, while affecting the climate drastically.

As the Tellurian and Macremian empires destroyed each other on Anarym, so had their colonies here. Over time, the two empires were forgotten and their advanced knowledge was lost;  those ruins that remain, such as those north of here, have always been
Telluria and Macremia began their Great War, so did their respective colonies throughout the continent, and even those far away from here.

shunned and feared, as they are believed to be cursed. Nonetheless, throughout the ensuing millennia, many a tale was told of fantastic artifacts being found amidst such ruins. But at this point, we may be crossing the line between fact and fiction ..."

"One must first know of the Lankharhans. This people established an empire some twelve thousand years ago on our continent of Anarym. This was a 'psionic' empire, since all Lankharhans were born with innate powers of the mind, or psionic powers.

Also, the empire was a peaceful one, growing only through willfull adherance of other countries or cities to the empire. There came a time when powerful psionic individuals rose to become Lords, Regents, Princes and Emperors of the Empire.

Those were aptly named 'Mentarchs', or 'Mind Lords', and they brought about a golden age for all citizens of the Empire. Indeed, their mind powers almost equalled those of gods, and they could live for centuries if not even more.

However, most of the Mind Lords became increasingly mentally unstable with time, and they began to lust for the utter domination of all non-psionics (whom they considered mongrels fit only to be slaves), even of all ordinary Lankharhans.

In effect, the Mind Lords had become nothing short of evil, ruthless god-like monsters bent on conquest, enslavement and destruction; they even began warring among themselves. Indeed, three of them stood against the other evil-mad nine.

But in time, thanks to the three Mentarchs who managed to rally lankharhans and non-lankharhans alike, these devastating Wars brought about the fall of the Nine. Unfortunately, the Wars caused the fall of the Lankharhan civilization as well.

Interestingly, a lengend has been passed on from one generation to the next ever since our area of the Azure Coast was settled. This legend speaks of a secret lankharhan city lying deep within the Forgotten Valley; this legend also tells a story that all

Mentarchs were born there, and consequently the place was considered holy by all lankharhans at the time. The legend is still going around today and the secret lankharhan city is now called the Forbidden City. Rumor has it that it can be found in the

south-east end of the Forgotten Valley, but that only true lankharhans or folks of direct lankharhan descent may enter it. Other rumors insist that the way to the city was sealed off for all time, when the Lankharhan empire fell."

"The greater Seacrest area is but a portion of the whole of the Azure Coast, which extends north all the way to the great city of Southgate and south to the northern-most borders of the kingdom of Kalimshyr, one of the so-called 'Southern Kingdoms'.

By definition and convention, the greater Seacrest area comprise those lands that are nestled by the Scales Swamps to the north, the Azure Sea to the west, and the massive mountain range to its east and south, called the 'High Crystalmist Reaches'.

In the lands of the greater Seacrest area, you will find of course the port city of Seacrest, which is a major trading center of the Azure Coast, as well as the island-city of Calember, a rising competitor of Seacrest. Other mainly human settlements in

the area are Edgemoor, which borders the Scales Swamps, Springdale, which rests on the western shore of the Everspring Lake, and the farming town of Wavyn, which lies just southeast of here. The major demi-human enclaves in the area are the elven
forest-kingdom of Lorill, which encompasses nearly most of the Everspring Forest, and the gnomish mining town of Goldylock, which lies northeast of here."

"The Scales Swamps lie north of the greater Seacrest area. Until fifteen to twelve thousand years ago, the Scales Swamps were a lush forest rich in arable land. However, climate changes -some think brought about by the Great War of the Macremian and

Tellurian empires- modified the lush forest lands and slowly turned them into swamps, bogs and moors over a century or two. The Scales Swamps are a very dangerous place, being inhabited by trolls, lizard men, crocodiles and all sorts of terrible

creatures. In fact, many a time have lords and kings attempted to create a foothold in the swamps by constructing forts or guard towers - but inevitably, such places were overrun by disease-carrying insects, monsters and other nasties, forcing their

abandonment. From the point of view of those who would be foolhardy enough to explore the swamps, two facts of interest are known: one, ancient Tellurian ruins lie about the center of the swamps, and two, a large river runs through the

swamps from the Azure Sea to its eastern border, creating a passage through the massive High Crystalmist Reaches and connecting the swamps to the Forgotten Valley nestled within the Reaches. In any case, nothing else is known of the swamps,
because so few have tried to explore them and even less managed to return alive to tell of their findings."

"The Forgotten Valley is a large valley of tropical rainforest east of here, untouched by civilization. Nestled within the High Crystalmist Reaches, it remains essentially inaccessible by foot or horse, since the Reaches are too highly rugged and

treacherous to even attempt at crossing through them. The only relatively safe access to the Forgotten Valley is by a river that runs through the Scales Swamps and connects the two areas. However, with the Scales Swamps being very dangerous, no one has

ever attempted such a journey. Thus, the valley of rainforest eventually acquired the name of 'Forgotten Valley', since civilizations are aware of it but have 'forgot' about the idea of attempting to explore it, let alone settle it. Of course, not much

is known of this place, except for what tall tales and wild stories try to convey. Hence, folklore of the area has it that the valley is inhabited by lizard-like monsters, fearsome flying serpents, giant snakes and evil crocodiles. Other stories speak of

cannibal savages, blood-thirsty catmen and degenerate snakemen. However, there is a legend that is intriguing: apparently, a secret city of the lost Lankharhan empire is said to lie deep within the Forgotten Valley. But that remains to be proven."

"The elven forest-kingdom of Lorill is almost four thousand years old. Although these elves are peaceful, they are quite defensive of their borders. Thus, they allow passage into their kingdom only to trade caravans or to people accompanied by a subject

of the kingdom. Not even other elves are allowed, unless escorted by a native of Lorill. On the other hand, elves from Lorill often wander about outside of their kingdom. In any case, Lorill trades actively with Seacrest, Calember and the gnomes of

Goldylock, but remain fierce isolationists. This is probably due to the fact that their forest-kingdom is bordered to the north by the Scales Swamps and is often plagued by raids from trolls: not wishing to leave themselves open to invasion by

humans lords and kings, they prefer to close their borders as prevention. Indeed, although peace and prosperity reigns today between Lorill and its human neighbors, some of the older monarchs of Seacrest attempted to conquer the elves in the past

- and thus Lorill remains extremely wary to this day, knowing that the succeeding short lives of humans are all too often harbingers of quick changes in disposition and goodwill towards their kingdom."

"Librunae is a local folklore hero of note. This good witch was shunned most of her life by folks, ignorance and fear overlooking her good principles and devotion to help others. Ten years ago, the black dragon known as 'Black Kiss' began to terrorize

the area, attacking caravans and hunting cattle and folks for food. The good witch Librunae confronted Black Kiss and fought the dragon single-handedly, using her great knowledge and powers of magic. After a long and fierce battle that decimated

her house and destroyed the woods surrounding it, a dying Librunae broke one of her rings of wizardry to unleash its potent magical energies in one terrible -and final- assault. But the witch's sacrifice was in vain, for Black Kiss was brought to near

death, but was not killed. Thus, Librunae's body was completely destroyed in that final attack of hers, while Black Kiss managed to fly slowly away to heal. Although the dragon has not been seen since then, many fear her impending return. As for

Librunae, many a tale speak of her soul still wandering about the ruins of her house. Some folks even say that if you stand in the ruins of her abode and speak her name, the witch will appear in her ghostly form. But this is obviously local folklore."

"Rumor has it that the crazy druid Chlorophus is lying low in the old Watchtower in the swamps, just north of here. He once tried to conquer the Seacrest area with an army of earth creatures, but was driven out by adventurers. He is a dangerous man."

"It is rumored that Aztranak, a powerful lich of old, made his crypt centuries ago on a small island in the Scales Swamps. Aztranak once ruled over almost all of the Azure Coast, until he retired with his treasure into his heavily-protected crypt."

"In its rise as a competitor against Seacrest, Calember is seeking to enlist Edgemoor within its sphere of influence. While this results in diplomatic tensions between Seacrest and Calember, active trade and relations remain between the two cities."

"It is said that the Island-Nation of Umaldyr, which lies far to the northeast of here, is greatly benefiting from the rise of trade between Anarym and the far-away continent of Realmz. Indeed, it has become some sort of hub for oversea trading."

"The Sssethanti, a mysterious people who lives deep within the Forgotten Valley, are said to worship snakes and are seeking to transform themselves into half-humans, half-snakes, in order to conquer the Forgotten Valley. Take it for what it is -a rumor."

"A millennia-old monolith stands on a small island of the northern lake of the Forgotten Valley. No one knows what it represents or who constucted it, but scholars speculate that it points to the location of a secret lankharhan city within the valley."

"A large tribe of lizard men is said to be settled in the northern region of the Scales Swamps. However, with the exception of occasional raids around Edgemoor, the authorities do not think that this tribe represents a threat to our area."

"One of the kingdoms to the south of the Azure Coast, named Kalimshyr, is rumored to be plotting a conquest of Seacrest. But thanks to our alliance with the powerful city of Southgate to the north, I don't think we have anything to worry about."

A tombstone stands here amidst the rubble of what was once a house. The following is carved upon the stone: "In memory of Librunae, who gave her life in order to save all of us. May the Gods watch kindly on her soul."
A powerful ball of lightning is emitted from the tombstone, striking everyone about!

A ghostly spirit of a middle-aged woman suddenly appears next to you, her otherworldly eye boring right through you. "Why have ye called my name? I know ye not and I doubt ye are seeking the wyrm that felled me years ago. Begone and leave me be!"
At that, the ghostly apparition returns to the Great Beyond.
Finding yourselves standing again before Librunae's tombstone, you decide it would be best not to disturb her spirit without a valid reason.
You find yourselves standing once again before Librunae's tombstone.

A ghostly spirit of a middle-aged woman suddenly appears next to you, her otherworldly eye boring right through you. "I know why ye have called me, for us spirits see and hear much. If ye wish for my help in finding Black Kiss, I'll assist gladly."

"I will even join ye in doing the deed, and thus finally get my revenge on the foul wyrm that bested me. Whenever ye are ready, come back and I'll teleport all of us to the beast's lair - for indeed, I know where it be."

"Are ye ready to be transported to near the lair of Black Kiss?" You hear Librunae's disembodied voice ask you. After nodding firmly with determination, the spirit appears next to you, smiling warmly. "As I said, I shall accompany ye. Let us be off!"
Weaving a magic spell, Librunae transports all of you away!

The ghost of a middle-aged woman appears next to you, her otherworldly eye boring right through you. "Why have ye called my name? I know that ye have bested Black Kiss, thus avenging me at the same time. I thank ye, but now I wish to rest in peace."
Searching about the grotto of the greckles, you find their accumulated ill-gotten booty!

Do you wish to try to reach the underwater cave here?

Being able to breathe underwater, you return to the surface without any hassle.

"My comrades." Ssyslak interjects, his reptilian eyes obviously pained. "I find it bad enough that I will have to fight my kin when we reach my village. So, why not simply move on and out of the way of this group? I would appreciate this very much."

You enter this ancient crypt.

The upper hall of this old crypt is rather quite large and spacious. You notice statues of various kinds of demons, along with tall columns etched with bas-reliefs of people being tortured or executed. You also notice bones strewn all about the floor.
Above all, a stong smell of decaying flesh assaults your senses.
"Black Kiss is here, allright." Librunae whispers with a snarl. "I sense her presence very strongly."
"Well, let's do this then!" Draconia adds with determination, griping her weapon while flexing her muscles.

"I smell food!" A deep, growling female voice intones from further ahead of you. From behind one of the large columns, the large head of a black dragon peers at you: "Yesssss! Fresh food for me and later for my pets!" The black dragon crows.
The sight of such a huge black dragon grips you with a wave of dragonfear, making it quite hard to resist.

"I also sense another presence, one that I haven't felt since ..." The dragon mumbles, rumbling her apprehension. "Yes, wyrm!" Librunae exclaims as she materializes beside you. "It is I, your greatest foe coming back from the grave to finish you!"
With another fearsome snarl, the black dragon calls her 'pets' to her side and attacks!
Without a word, Draconia hacks off a horn from the black dragon, grinning with satisfaction.

"Well, it's been fun and all, folks!" Draconia suddenly exclaims, smiling mischievously. "But it's time fer me to go and claim me own reward!" Picking up her gear, she turns to you one last time: "And finally take a bath!" She adds with a wink.
With final partings, Draconia Nah'Li gets on her way.

"The cycle is now complete." Librunae whispers, looking at peace. She turns to you, smiling warmly: "Finaly, my spirit can be free to roam happily the Great Beyond. I thank ye for yer help." Without further due, she vanishes in a whisp of smoke!

You stumble upon Draconia Nah'Li fighting one-on-one against a huge female black dragon! As if this was not enough, the self-proclaimed dragonslayer has to fight off what appears to be the 'pets' of the black dragon.

"Well?" Draconia yells out to you, looking at you from the corner of her eyes as she fends off another attack from the dragon. "Are ye jumpin' in or not? All me needs from the wyrm is one of her horns, so ye take the rest!"
"At last!" Librunae intones as she materializes next to you, her ghostly eyes glaring with grim determination. "The time for my revenge is at hand!"

Without a word, a battered and bloodied Draconia hacks off a horn from the black dragon, grinning with satisfaction. Putting the horn in her backpack, she quaffs a couple of potions of healing in succession.
You remind yourself to pick up a dragon egg from Black Kiss, as proof to bring back to Adventurers Inc.
You come upon the hoard of the black dragon. Nestled in the heart of the hoard, you spot three black dragon eggs - they look to have been layed recently.
The insects of the swamps are particularly aggressive towards you at this time ... You hope that none of them are disease-carriers.
Scavenging creatures of the swamps have wandered in!
A statue or throne must have once stood over this slab of marble, most likely long before the black dragon covered it with her hoard.
Paying closer attention, you realize that this slab can be slid over! Doing so, you reveal a flight of stairs going down.
"Somethin's ain't right with this here floor tile." Galduur mumbles, as he pokes the stab of marble with the handle of his weapon.
Do you go down?

This place is surprisingly dusty and dry, considering where it was built. The walls are covered with canvases depicting a powerful lich dressed in flowing black robes, a king's crown resting upon its hooded skull. The lich is shown leading armies of

mercenaries and undead, conquering opposing armies and cities. At the center of this hall, a marble column-statue of the same lich stands silent, nestled by huge blocks of granite that surround it. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you decipher the words etched

at the foot of the column-statue: "Aztranak the Magnificent, Lord of all He surveys. Ye who have violated his place of rest, abandon all hope - for ye shall die here as surely as Aztranak's legacy lives on."
The column-statue of Aztranak stands silent, looming menacingly as if surveying all about it.
A magical trap is triggered!
A wall slides down behind you, as an otherwordly laugh echoes about.
You enter what appears to be a throne room. A large throne of obsidian stands at the far end of this hall.
Upon closer scrutiny, you notice a tiny knob underneath the left handle of the massive throne. Turning it, a drawer slides out from the base of the throne!
You are whisked away back to the surface!

You enter a chapel. From the bas-reliefs etched onto the walls and columns of the place, this hall is dedicated to Orcas, God of Horrors and Undeath. A large altar of obsidian stands at the far end of the chapel.
You find a few items of interest on the top of the altar.

This large room is a study room doubling as a library. However, all of the furniture has become brittle or has fallen apart, whereas the wall-to-wall bookshelves are seemingly holding nothing but dust-filled  book covers.
Amidst the decayed books and dust-covered (and useless) scrolls, you find something of interest!
This was once a lavishly decorated and furnished bedroom. However, the furniture has decayed, while the hanging tapestries and rich carpets are now useless, hole-ridden pieces of cloth.
This is a small kitchen, complete with pantry. Of course, the table and chairs are now crumbling, whereas the food stored in the pantry has dessicated a long time ago.

You notice on the granite wall next to you that what seems to be a small protruding imperfection is in fact a button that can be pushed. Pressing down on the button, you hear something heavy move, away to the west.
The door stubbornly refuses to give way.
Do you want to take some water from this fountain?
Who will do the deed?
The water is foul! Your comrade just found that out the hard way by taking a sip of the water while trying to fill up the waterskins!
Something suddenly rushes out from the fountain!
Do you pull on this rusting lever?
You find something of interest lying at the bottom of the shut-down fountain.
This rusting lever is hopelessly stuck.

This hall is filled with columns of solid marble. You notice six skeletal warriors, clad in dust-covered armors, standing silently as they gaze sightlessly at the ceiling. The moment you walk in, they animate and attack you!
The way is blocked by a massive slab of stone, upon which a demonic face has been sculpted. As if sensing your presence, the lifeless eyes of the demonic face begin to light up!
The skeleton key that you found begins to pulse, slowly levitating out of your hands and floating toward the slab of granite.
Suddenly, the key shatters! Immediately after, the eyes of the bas-relief return to lifelessness as the slab of granite slowly sinks into the floor!
From out of nowhere, an evil laugh echoes about the place.
You are then enveloped in a shroud of shimmering light and whisked away!
You look to your comrades in shock. In turn, they stare at you dumbfounded and speechless.

As you approach this sarcophagus, its cover begins to slide ... and out of it rises a lich, its baleful stare lit with a glow of blood-red hate. "You dare disturb my rest while my powerful spirit roams the Astral plane? I was alerted of your intrusion

when the skeleton key shattered, for my soul is linked with it. I must congratulate you, for no one -ever since I moved into my crypt centuries ago- has managed to get this far. However, your resourcefulness and bravery will bring you nothing but death!"
Summoning help from the Great Beyond to his side, Aztranak attacks!

Panting and tired, you watch with horror as the skull of Aztranak rises slowly from the ashes of his remains, bellowing an evil laughter. "Fools!" The skull exclaims. "I am not just any lich, but an arch-lich. Now, face me in my true, glorious form!"
At that, the arch-lich attacks!
Aztranak summons help from the Great Beyond!
You find something of interest inside the sarcophagus of Aztranak.
"That must be the key we need to find, as instructed by the Infinite One through my dreams!" An elated Lindanyl exclaims, gazing at the key in wonderment.
You have found Aztranak's treasure!

"I sense a patrol of my people in the nearby area." Ssyslak informs you. "I think it best to move on and evade them for now." You nod in agreement, appreciating the opportunity to circumvent a meaningless clash.
You run into wandering lizard men warriors - upon seeing you, they charge to repel the invaders that you are!
"We best make haste!" Ssyslak intones, visibly worried. "Otherwise, I'm afraid we'll have to fight my people at every step we take!"
As you approach the fortifications of this village, you notice numerous lizard men warriors standing watch on the battlements.
Unless you find some sort of 'inside' help, there doesn't seem to be any way to enter this village except by having to go through all of its inhabitants.

"This is my village." Ssyslak tells you. "The safest way to infiltrate it would be to attempt to pass through the gates when it's well dark. I know my fellow warriors - they tend to doze off easily at night, even when on guard duty."

"Once inside, I suggest we head straight to the cave at the north end: we'll find the chief of the tribe there. Once we defeat him, my people will run away out of confusion and fear -this will give us leeway to deal with the snake priests and their ilk!"
The gates of the seemingly abandoned lizard men village remain open and unguarded.
All too visible and conspicuous under the daylight, the lizard men on watch at the gates see you approach and sound the call to arms!
As you try to catch your breath, you see more lizard men rushing your way to fight. Do you run away in order to regroup?
More lizard men jump into the fray!
The gates of the lizard men village are closed shut. Fortunately, no guard seems to be on watch at the battlements.
Sleeping lizard men warriors on watch are aroused by the noise you make and sound the call to arms! The gates are quickly opened to let out a swarm of angry lizard men!

Deciding that discretion is the better part of valor, you run away to fight another day. It would seem that you will need to find another means, or another time, to infiltrate these lizard men fortifications.
Mrrysh growls with satisfaction: "Good battle. Bad odds fer us, bad place fer enemies to be!"
Ssyslak hisses angrily: "I hate having to fight for my life and for what is right, but sadly, that is the way of the world."
Having been alerted  to your presence, numerous lizard men are waiting for you!
You enter this cave.
This looks like the private quarters of the lizard man Chief. You find nothing of interest here.
You enter some sort of makeshift communal room. Many lizard men are here, as well as lizard men shamans. Upon seeing you, they attack!

A booming growl, mixed with a hiss, is heard: the largest lizard man you have ever seen enters, accompanied by warriors and shamans. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can understand the diatribe he is directing to you: "Ye intruders! Puny heretics! We the
pure followers of Sseth will best ye and sacrifice ye to his glory! As Chief, so me says!" At that, the lizard man Chief and his entourage attack!
Upon the death of their leader, many lizard men flee in confusion and fear!
You enter some sort of makeshift chapel, only to be confronted by lizard men shamans. Just as they step forth to attack, you notice that they are joined by horrible snakemen!

"We're not done, yet!" Ssyslak intones, wiping his weapon clean. "I know that there are more of of those snakemen priests about, as well as warriors. The lot of them who have bewitched my people must be hiding somewhere outside of the village."
This poorly sculpted statue bears the likeness of Sseth, the God of Evil and Reptiles. You also know this dark god as Neralkuur.
Strange-looking men covered with scales are guarding this cave!
"This is it!" Ssyslak hisses. "We must have found their hideout. I know there are more of them, so let us hunt!"
Unfortunately, the snakemen warriors living do not appreciate your intrusion!
You enter some sort of chapel, only to be confronted by more snakemen!

"It's done." Ssyslak intones as he wipes his weapon clean. "The snakemen priests that beguiled my people are now gone. I thank you for your help, my friends. Now that my quest is completed, it is now time for me to get on my way and find my destiny."

He shugs: "I do not know where it lies ... maybe here, in the Scales Swamps. Who knows? Perhaps I'll find some of my people who think more like me ... then again, maybe our paths will cross again!" With final partings, Ssyslak walks away.
Panting and tired, you set yourselves to explore the rest of this place.

You enter what appears to be the private quarters of the highpriest snakeman you just killed. Rummaging through the place, you find a letter written in a strange language. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you can decipher it: "Greetings, Loyal One. We wish to

congratulate you on the progress achieved so far. However, there is an increasing need for haste in winning the complete loyalty of those degenerate lizard men savages, if we are to secure our Valley for the Holiest Ones who speak for the Mighty Snake

Lord. Need we remind you that once the Valley is unified with the help of the lizard men and those mayaltec humans, then we will be poised to swarm over the Swamps and then beyond, all to the Glory of Sseth and us, His Children. Signed: Your Holy Queen."
Mulling over what you have just read, you also find a map.
Further searching the room allows you to find some additional, interesting items.
This old building in ruins is seemingly abandoned.
Its architecture is the same as those ancient tellurian ruins you explored last year, during the Time of the Great War.
The style of the remaining bas-reliefs sculpted on columns and walls is the same as those ancient tellurian ruins you explored last year, during the Time of the Great War.
Its overall architectural design and decorative art are the same as those ancient tellurian ruins you explored last year, during the Time of the Great War.
This ancient tomb now is empty.
Opening this ancient tomb, you end up facing creatures that have taken residence within!
This cave is unoccupied.
Savages on the prowl eye you as prey!

You come upon a peaceful and goodwilled jungle barbarian tribe. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you are able to parlay with them. They kindly allow you a safe stay and free water whenever you come to their village.
They do warn you that not all jungle peoples are friendly like them, and that you should be careful.
You come upon barbarian women who are busy at working furs and skins, while others are preparing a communal feast for the tribe. Children play happily around them.
You cross path with a hunting party of barbarians. Grinning and shouting their pride, they announce to all that their hunt has been successful. The others reply with bellows of approval.
You come upon a small group of barbarian elders teaching the oral legends and lore of their tribe to the children. The youngsters listen in awe of the older men and women.
