You come upon a group of warriors busying themselves at making tools and weapons from stone and woods. Although primitive, you can't help but admire their craftmanship.
You come upon a small group of warriors teaching the youngsters on how to use tools and weapons. Of course, the children are quite excited and are eager to learn.
You come upon a war-like jungle barbarian tribe. Upon seeing you, they attack!
After such a devastating defeat, the rest of the tribe scatters into the jungle for safety, abandoning their village!
You ascertain that you could well use this abandoned willage as a safe place to camp.
The abandoned village is eerily empty and quiet of human activity.
Seemingly out of nowhere, numerous cathoon warriors surround your party!
Their leader speaks; thanks to Oberon's spell, you understand him: "Strangers not allowed within our borders, unless escorted by one of our Pride! We offer choice of leaving in peace or by force!"
Choosing to leave peacefully, the cathoon warriors escort you politely outside the borders of their territory.
You spot a patrol of cathoon warriors. They leave you in peace.

"Me, Mrrysh Walksfar of the Pride, is with these strangers." Mrrysh announces to the warriors. "Free passage it is." A cathoon leader replies, before giving the sign to his troops to resume their stealthy patrol.
As the warriors disappear through the jungle, Mrrysh winks at you: "Good thing you have me along, eh?"
Seemingly out of nowhere, numerous cathoon warriors surround your party!
Panting and tired after this clash, you decide to leave the territory of the cathoons. You certainly do not wish to have more warriors drop on you.
"Repel them!" The cathoon commander orders his warriors.
You spot a patrol of mayaltec warriors. They leave you in peace.
Seemingly out of nowhere, numerous mayaltec warriors surround your party!
As you raise the Tiara of the Lost Highkings high above your head, the warriors back away into the jungle in awe and confusion.

"We must make haste." Tecoltitan tells you, obviously in earnest. "The sooner we confront Shamar-Tarac and the snakemen priest with those holy artifacts, the quicker my people will come back to their senses!"

Tecoltitan steps in front of you: "My apologies, but we must not go further. We have entered the territory of my people. Without the Tiara in our hands, they will remain under the influence of the snakemen and attack us. We should retreat instead."
Panting and tired after this clash, you decide to leave the territory of the mayaltecs. You certainly do not wish to have more warriors drop on you.
Women of the tribe are busy at working furs and skins, while others are picking up fruits and vegetables from the fields.
You cross path with a hunting party of mayaltecs. From the number of their catches that they are bringing back, they were obviously successful.
You cross paths with a patrol of mayaltecs warriors. They do not pay any particular attention to you.
You come upon a small group of elders teaching the oral legends and lore of their tribe to the children. The youngsters listen in awe of the older men and women.
You come upon a group of mayaltec men and women busying themselves at making tools and weapons from stone and woods. Although primitive, you can't help but admire their craftmanship.
You come upon a small group of mayaltec warriors teaching the youngsters on how to use tools and weapons. Of course, the children are quite excited and are eager to learn.
You cross paths with a patrol of mayaltec warriors: upon seeing you with the Tiara, they stand back away from you, obviously awed and confused.

This cathoon warrior seems quite out of place, sitting alone while brooding over a tankard of milk. As you approach him, Tecoltitan rushes ahead to greet him: "Mrrysh! Mrrysh Walksfar! It is me, Tecoltitan!" At first surprised, the cathoon returns the

warm and friendly handshake offered by your mayaltec comrade. "What ye doing here?" The cathoon growls, in the typical speech maneurism of his people. With earnest, Tecoltitan introduces you to his long-time friend and tells him of the recent happenings.

Mrrysh nods silently. "Me pride is peaceful, living off hunting and farming in the Forgotten Valley. The Mayaltecs not always evil, but snake priests have poisoned their brains. Now they want to destroy us Cat People. We need strong warriors and mages

like ye to help us defeat the snake priests and return peace between my pride and my friend's tribe." Tecoltitan nods fervently, smiling: "They will help us, my friend. We need to find the Tiara to help my people escape from the foul influence of the

snakemen. Then we have to fight the corrupted Highking of my tribe and the snakemen he serves, and then all will be set right again!" With a resolute nod, Mrrysh picks up his gear and hands you a map, before gathering his gear to join with you.
You come upon a fierce battle between a lone warrior and a group of snakemen. The warrior is quite tanned and is dressed with colorful feathers and trousers.
"That's me friend Tecoltitan! We help him!" Mrrysh yells out, just as he rushes ahead to fight at the side of the lone warrior.
Do you help the lone warrior?

The bloodied and battered warrior walks up to you -thanks to Oberon's spell, you understand his language: "You have my gratitude, good strangers. My name is Tecoltitan. My people call themselves the Mayaltecs. All of us are followers of the Great

Quetzalcoualt, the Good and Just God of the Sun. But snakemen like those we just fought have infiltrated my people and subverted their beliefs, making them follow the dark god Sseth." He shakes his head with sadness. "Quetzalcoualt is the Feathered

Serpent of Truth and Justice, while Sseth is the Dark Serpent of Evil. The snakemen have beguiled my people alright - but they had the help of our corrupted Highking, Shamar-Tarac. As one who refused to follow Sseth, I had to flee from my city lest I be

put to death. Furthermore, the snakemen have turned my people against our cathoon neighbors, waging war against them." He sighs with resignation. "My best friend is of the Cat people - his name is Mrrysh. The two of us have undertaken a quest to defeat

the snakemen and restore peace in our territories. Mrrysh set out to travel outside our Great Valley and the vast swamps, seeking the foreign lands beyond in order to recruit help from mighty warriors and mages. In the meantime, I was to find the Tiara

of the Lost Highkings, a relic holy to my people which would help me challenge our corrupted Highking. The Tiara was lost hundreds of summer solstices ago, when the evil dragon Death Emerald attacked our city. I have found the lair of Death Emerald!"

He smiles with grim determination. "I was then on my way to find Mrrysh when I was attacked by these snakemen, who are obviously seeking to prevent me from recovering the holy Tiara. Will you help me in this undertaking?"
"As you wish." Tecoltitan replies, visibly disapointed. Without further due, he slowly walks away.

Smiling, you show him the Tiara. "You have it!" Tecoltitan exclaims, surprised and dumbfounded. "Praise be the Feathered Serpent! We must go to my city as soon as possible in order to confront Shamar-Tarac!" At that, he hands you a map.
(Tecoltitan has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu.)
Not wishing to be bothered, you leave the lone warrior fend of for himself.
"Praise be the Feathered Serpent! Let us go and hunt Death Emerald, then!" Tecoltitan exclaims, obviously relieved. After handing you a couple of maps, he sets himself to follow you.
"We must help him!" Strider yells out, rushing ahead to lend a hand to the lone warrior!
"We must help him!" Galduur yells out, rushing ahead to lend a hand to the lone warrior!
"We must help him!" Ssyslak yells out, rushing ahead to lend a hand to the lone warrior!
"We must help him!" Lindanyl yells out, rushing ahead to lend a hand to the lone warrior!

put to death. Furthermore, the snakemen have turned my people against our cathoon neighbors, waging war against them." He then smiles warmly at Mrrysh. "My best friend here and I have undertaken a quest to defeat the snakemen and restore peace in our

territories. Mrrysh set out to travel outside our Great Valley and the vast swamps, seeking the foreign lands beyond in order to recruit help from mighty warriors and mages - I see that he has succeeded! In the meantime, I was to find the Tiara

He smiles with grim determination while giving on Mrrysh' shoulder a hearty clout. "I was then on my way to find my friend when I was attacked by these snakemen, who are obviously seeking to prevent me from recovering the holy Tiara."

Picking up his gear, he smiles warmly at you and then in turn to Mrrysh: "Praise be the Feathered Serpent! Let us go and hunt Death Emerald, then!" He exclaims, obviously relieved. After handing you a couple of maps, he sets himself to follow you.
Cathoon warriors are under attack by a mayaltec raiding party! With your best war cry, you rush in to help the cathoon!
After a polite nod in gratitude, the cathoon leader commands his warriors to return to their homes in order to heal themselves.

"I long for the day we are successful in restoring peace between my people and the Cat people." Tecoltitan muses, sighing with resignation. "It is hard enough for me to fight my own ..." He shakes his head with sadness at that.
"Me curse the snakemen fer making bad things happen between me people and mayaltecs!" Mrrysh growls, his eyes glaring with hate for the ssethanti.
You stumble onto a clash between cathoon warriors and mayaltecs. Do you jump in?
"We must help my Pride!" Mrrysh growls as he rushes ahead to give a hand to his kin.
"We must help the cathoon, for they are the ones being wronged by my people!" Tecoltitan yells out, as he rushes ahead to join the fray.
Not wishing to bother yourself, you keep on walking through the jungle.
Which side do you help?
Cathoons
Mayaltecs
You jump into the fray on the side of the Mayaltecs!
The Mayaltecs immediately turn on you!
It would seem that you have made the wrong choice in helping the Mayaltecs ...
You jump into the fray on the side of the cathoons!

This ancient monolith of solid granite is highly similar to the one you have seen in the Sword Lands of the past. However, it is featureless save for an etched arrow pointing in the southeast direction and the words "Tempus Utopia" etched under it.
With the Pride Leader of the cathoons most likely sleeping at this time, you decide not to bother him.
The pride leader of the cathoon is outside of his hut, making defense plans against mayaltec attacks and raids with his best warriors. Seeing that he is very busy, you decide not to bother him.
The pride leader of the cathoon is outside of his hut, planning patrols with his best warriors. Seeing that he is very busy, you decide not to bother him.
The pride leader of the cathoon is outside of his hut, planning hunting parties with his best warriors. Seeing that he is very busy, you decide not to bother him.
The pride leader of the cathoon is outside of his hut, planning forest clearings for more farm fields with his warriors. Seeing that he is very busy, you decide not to bother him.
Cathoon warriors are keeping an alerted eye from atop these wooden watch-towers.
However, the place seems to be abandoned.

"It has become worse than I thought." Tecoltitan mumbles angrily. "Now the snakemen priests have closed our holy temple. They must have set up a new temple for Sseth in the ziggurat of our Highking, then."

As you approach this large ziggurat, numerous mayaltec warriors raise their weapons in readiness to fight you. From behind them comes a man dressed in colorful attire, wearing a small crown of feathers and accompanied by mayaltec priests.

"I, Shamar-Tarac and Highking of Mayaltecs, demand that you surrender!" The man intones, quite confident. "The Tiara that you hold is mine by right, since I am the rightful Highking! Because you are returning it, I shall show you mercy." He adds.

"Liar!" Tecoltitan interjects, raising his fist in defiance. "A rightful Highking would not turn his back on Quetzalcoualt! A true Highking would never embrace Sseth or listen to the council of his dark minions!" The valiant mayaltec then casts his gaze

about the gathering crowd of his brethren. "We are the children of the Sun God, not of the Dark Lord!" He announces aloud, with pride and conviction. You notice that many among the increasing crowd of mayaltec onlookers nod silently in agreement.

"We are both." One of the priests standing next to the corrupt Highking replies, his beady eyes glaring with hate. "For the Serpent God is both - the feathered snake of wisdom and the mighty snake of power! That is why we needed to raise this ziggurat,

that is why we have a destiny to fulfill in His Glorious name!" The Highking then raises his hand at that: "Enough. The traitor Tecoltitan does not have a right to speak here and so we do not have to respond to his treacherous lies!"
In the heat of the battle, the mayaltec priests fighting against you shed their disguise to reveal their true nature!
At that, Shamar-Tarac orders his warriors to attack!

In spite of the eruption of outrage among the gathered mayaltecs at the sight of the dead snake-men, Shamar-Tarac raises his weapon and rushes to attack you. As his remaining priests shed their disguises in turn, more snake-men come out to join them!
At the death of the Highking they were sworn to follow and protect, the royal mayaltec warriors lose their will to continue this battle and seek to run away!
From seemingly out of nowhere, true mayaltec priests join the fray - on your side!
More Ssethanti join the fray!
With the foul snake-men exposed and realizing that they had been deceived all along, the mayaltecs mob the ziggurat to burn it down and destroy it!
This part of the hideout is half finished. From the rubble and digging tools lying about, the occupants obviously mean to extend their lair one of these days.
"I'm over here to your right - at my kitchen table." The woman mumbles with irritation.

An old priest then approaches amidst the commotion. As he walks slowly to stand before you, all mayaltecs -including a battered and bloodied Tecoltitan- bow in reverence in his presence. Smiling warmly, the old priest inclines his head to you:

"Ever since the snake-men came to our city and corrupted the Highking, all of the priesthood of the Wise Serpent were forced to flee into exile, hoping to return one day and deliver our people from the Dark Snake. You have our most heartfelt gratitude."

He bows his head again. Gently taking the Tiara from you, the old priest places it upon Tecoltitan's head: "As we set ourselves to make things right with our God, we need a noble leader that is pure of heart and rich in wisdom. The Feathered Serpent

has chosen Tecoltitan!" After placing the Tiara on Tecoltitan's head, the old priest turns to his people: "He is deserving to walk in Turoac's footsteps! Let us all hail our new Highking!" At that, the mayaltecs rise and cheer aloud with joy.

"With the snake-men gone," Tecoltitan announces to his people, "now is the time to make peace with our neighbors, the Cat People. Together, we will be ever vigilant and strong should the snake-men decide to return in our midst!" More cheers follow.

"Me goes bring news to me people!" An excited Mrrysh exclaims. After embracing is friend Tecoltitan, he turns to you: "You brave people! Me is proud to fight alongside you! Maybe we meet again, someday." After final partings, Mrrysh leaves.

As the mayaltecs rush to Tecoltitan to raise him onto their shoulders in celebration, you quietly slip away to mend your wounds and recuperate. "Come meet me at my old house the first chance you get!" You hear Tecoltitan yell out to you.

The old ziggurat lies in ruins. However, you notice piles of granite blocks of all sizes and shape lying about, as well as wooden scaffolds lying on the ground. Looks like the mayaltecs intend to rebuilt it for their new Highking.
The old ziggurat lies in ruins. However, numerous mayaltecs are busy working at rebuilding it for their new Highking.
This house looks abandoned.

Tecoltitan is standing at a table outside of this house, busy overlooking plans of some sort with mayaltec priests and architects. "Greetings, friends!" He welcomes you, smiling. "As you see, I have moved back into my old house. We are busying ourselves

with the plans of a new ziggurat. Once it is completed, then I will have to dwell there since I am the Highking." He then chuckles. "But I'm afraid it won't be completed soon - we build slowly but strongly, so it could take a couple of years!"

He then gives you a map. "The old priest stole this from the snake-men before he fled in exile. This looks like the location of the snake-men's city, along with a place holy to them. One day, I plan for us and the Cat People to march out against them."

He sighs at that. "But trust will take time to return between our two people, so chances are too much time will have passed before we can attack the snake-men. However, should you wish to try your hand at it by killing their queen ..."
He leaves the thought hanging at that, winking mischievously. "In any case, do not feel obligated in any way - after all, you have done so much for us already!"
"We should not stray too far into the jungle." Tecoltitan announces. "Besides, we have yet to fullfill our destiny and save my people!" Finding wisdom in his words, you turn around.
"Not too far into jungle, we should go." Mrrysh announces. "Much to do, we have left. Save my people, we must!" Finding wisdom in his words, you turn around.
Smiling in turn, you tell Tecoltitan that you have killed the Ssethanti queen. "Praise the Feathered Serpent!" He exclaims, embracing you with joy. "Then all will be right once more, truly!"
With final partings and wellwishes, you take your leave from Tecoltitan.
Mayaltec warriors stand in your way: "Our apologies, but the Highking cannot be disturbed right now. He sends you his best wishes." With a shrug, you move along.
Tecoltitan is standing at a table outside of this house, busy overlooking plans of some sort with mayaltec priests and architects. "Greetings, friends!" He welcomes you, smiling warmly.
Chuckling, Tecoltitan beams: "In any case, I bid you to keep Turoac's shield. You are most deserving of it! I hope that with this holy item, you will always remember us."

"Fools!" One of the priests standing next to the Highking intones, his beady eyes glaring with hate. You then notice a crowd of mayaltecs gathering slowly. "Only fools dare to challenge the Will of the true Serpent God, Sseth!" The priest yells out.

With much reluctance, you hand out the Tiara to a mayaltec warrior, who in turn rushes to the Highking in order to hand it to him. Smiling wickedly, Shamar-Tarac dones the Tiara: "Praise be the Serpent of Power!" He intones, his fist raised in the air.
"Aye!" Shamar-Tarac adds, smug with himself. "And He does not tolerate fools, nor gives mercy to them!"
An old priest then approaches the commotion. As he walks slowly to stand before you, all mayaltecs bow in reverence in his presence. Smiling warmly, the old priest inclines his head to you:

He bows his head again. Gently picking up the Tiara, the old priest stares at it with sadness: "As we set ourselves to make things right again with our God, we need a noble leader that is pure of heart and wise of mind. The Feathered Serpent willing,

one deserving to walk into Turoac's footsteps will come and rightfully claim the Tiara. With the snake-men gone, now is the time to make peace with our neighbors, the Cat People. Together, we will be ever vigilant and stronger should the snake-men
decide to return within our midst. This I proclaim to be the Will of Quetzalcoualt!" At that, the mayaltecs erupt in cheer.
"Me goes bring news to me people!" An excited Mrrysh exclaims. "You brave people! Me is proud to fight alongside you! Maybe we meet again, someday." After final partings, Mrrysh leaves.

As the mayaltecs rally around the old priest to celebrate, you walk away to mend your wounds. Gazing wearily to Turoac's shield, you wonder if you should not return it as well - but then decide against it, seeing it as a memento to remember these people.

You also wonder if you should not try to find the city of the Ssethanti, in order to somehow defeat them and prevent them from further attempts at controlling the region. You then notice a map lying at your feet. Picking it up, you are surprised to see

that it shows the location of the Ssethanti city, as well as a site holy to them. Looking about in amazement, you then spot the old priest winking at you mischievously, before returning his full attention to his joyous people and celebrate with them.
"The Will of Quetzalcoualt, eh?" Riel whispers in your ear, chuckling quietly.
Laughing to yourselves, you take your leave.

Numerous mayaltec warriors guard this tall ziggurat. you notice beady-eyed priests coming in and out of the place, carrying bowls of meat and fruits. Seeing the wary glances of the guards being thrown your way, you slowly walk away.

Oberon appears before you, smiling warmly: "You've done it! You've found the means to open the portals - I was watching all along, from the Hourglass Tower. Well, let us be off to face Primus/Maximus!" Clapping his hands, he sets himself to follow you.
(Oberon has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu).
From seemingly out of nowhere, psi-warriors make the jump on you!
You find yourselves at the entrance of a small cavern. From the tables and chairs about, it would seem that the psi-warriors used this place as a mess hall of some sort.
This large cave is occupied by psi-warriors!
Searching the cots and chest about this cavern, you find a few items of interest.
You come about a large, rugged crevasse going down for hundreds of feet. The psi-warriors must have been using their innate psionic abilities to levitate across.
You are transported across!
You float gently across!
This old, crumbling bridge hangs short above the raging river. The psi-warriors probably use their innate psionic abilities to levitate across.
You spot a group of strange creatures, half-women and half-tigers, locked in a grim fight against ssethanti warriors. Do you help the creatures?
"The enemy of the snake-men is my friend!" Tecoltitan yells out, as he runs forth to help the creatures.
"We must help the tigtaurs!" Striders roars, as he rushes forward to help the strange creatures.
"We help those attacked by them foul snake-men!" Galduur roars, as he rushes to the help of the creatures.
"Help tigtaurs, we must!" Mrrysh growls, before rushing ahead to help the strange creatures.
Suddenly, more ssethanti arrive on the scene and see you: it would seem that you have been caught into this battle after all!

After the battle, a battered and bloodied tigtaur comes to you. Thanks to Oberon's spell, you understand her language: "In the name of my sisters and our pride, I thank you, strangers. I am Sherrinka, shaman-warrior. As you saw, we have been under

constant attacks by the vile snake people. If you are their enemies as well, then you are welcome in our territory and free to pass through peacefully. Also, I would join you if you seek to topple the power behind the snake people!"
Do you accept Sherrinka into your ranks?

"As you wish." Sherrinka replies politely. "Perhaps it is better that I remain with my sisters to help defend our village. Be welcome in any case, as token of our gratitude for your help today." At that, the tigtaurs gather their wounded and leave.
"I am pleased by your decision." Sherrinka replies. As her sisters gather their wounded and dead, she sets herself to follow you.
(Sherrinka has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu).

You find yourselves surrounded by strange half-women, half-tiger creatures who have appeared out of the jungle, seemingly from nowhere! Thanks to Oberon's spell, you understand their language: "Leave our territory! Strangers are not welcome here!"

"Apologize do I, in the name of my friends." Mrrysh intervenes, bowing his head in respect. "Offend you, we did not mean." One of the tigtaurs approached the cathoon: "The Cat People have always been respectful of our ways and so we have been of theirs."

"Because of this," the tigtaur goes on, "then you are allowed free passage in our territory - your friends as well, but only if you are with them." At that, the tigtaurs leave. "With you, a good thing that I am, no?" Mrrysh adds with a grin.
Not wishing for meaningless fight, you leave the territory of the tigtaurs.
"So be it, then!" The tigtaur roars.
With stealth and quickness, the tigtaurs launch their assault!
Not wishing to be ambushed by more tigtaurs, you leave their territory as fast as you can.
"Why seek a meaningless fight?" Strider whispers in your ear. "They have every right to protect their lands. Let us leave in peace." Finding wisdom in his words, you change your mind and leave.
"Why seek a meaningless fight?" Tecoltitan whispers in your ear. "They have every right to protect their lands. Let us leave in peace." Finding wisdom in his words, you change your mind and leave.
"Why seek a meaningless fight?" Lindanyl whispers in your ear. "They have every right to protect their lands. Let us leave in peace." Finding wisdom in her words, you change your mind and leave.
"Why seek a meaningless fight?" Sarin whispers in your ear. "They have every right to protect their lands. Let us leave in peace." Finding wisdom in his words, you change your mind and leave.
You cross paths with a tigtaur patrol. After a few polite nods your way, they continue their patrol.
Tigtaurs appear seemingly out of nowhere. "Repel the intruders!" One of them roars.
Tigtaurs appear seemingly out of nowhere: "Leave our territory! Strangers are not welcome here!" One of them intones.
You spot a patrol of tigtaurs locked in a grim fight against ssethanti warriors. Do you help them?
"I long for the day when the head of these foul beings is finally cut off!" Sherrinka growls, as she wipes her weapon clean.
"Thank you so much for your help, good strangers." The patrol leader bids you, panting and tired. As the tigtaurs wearily gather their wounded and dead, you continue on your way.
"We must help my sisters!" Sherrinka roars, as she rushes ahead.
Not wishing to be bothered, you walk away - leaving the sounds of battle, amd the fate of the tigtaurs, far behind you.

You come upon tigtaurs who are busy at working furs and skins, while others are preparing a communal feast for the pride. Children play happily around them - you wonder how these creatures can reproduce at all.
You cross path with a hunting party of tigtaurs. Grinning and shouting their pride, they announce to all that their hunt has been successfull. The others reply with roars of approval.
You come upon a small group of tigtaur shamans teaching the oral legends and lore of their pride to the children. The youngsters listen in awe of the older tigtaurs.
You come upon a group of tigtaurs busying themselves at making tools and weapons from steel. You can't help but admire their craftmanship.
You come upon a small group of tigtaurs teaching the youngsters on how to use tools and weapons. Of course, the children are quite excited and are eager to learn.
Just as you are about to enter, a tigtaur shaman comes out: "Only our people may enter the House of the Beast Lord and be blessed by Him." She intones with finality.
Seeing Sherrinka with you, the shaman then bows her head respectfully. "However," she adds quickly with a tone of apology, "you need only ask me what it is you require."
You are ambushed by ssethanti warriors!
A large, dome-shaped field of energy stands here. Almost imperceptible, it prevents you from going on further!

You find another ancient monolith of solid endurinium standing here, looming silently and immutably over the jungle. An inscription is unevenly etched in large letters onto the megalithic structure; thanks to Oberon's spell, you manage to decipher it:

Oberon sniffs petulantly: "We of the Hourglass have always known that the Forbidden City -or Lankh'Nar, as it was known in the past- is shielded by a static field of psionic energies." He explains. "Only those with psionic powers may pass through it."

"But we could never figure out what is the source of this field or its location." He then smiles ruefully: "With me being a Kerydorhyan and direct descendant of the Lankharhans, one would think I'd manage to find out, no?" He shakes his head at that.

"I did uncover texts and scriptures which point to the ssethanti as being degenerated descendants of humans artificially-created by the Lankharhans. I have no idea how they did this, but I suspect that they eventually used an improvement of this

dark science to create the Mentarchs themselves. In any case, if the ssethanti are indeed grossly mutated descendants of the so-called 'creations' mentioned on this monolith, where then is the field's power source?" He then brightens up: "Well, at least

we know the name of this source: the 'Nexus Source', as etched on this monolith!" He then shrugs, acknowledging silently that this piece of information is rather useless without knowing where this source is located.
You read once again the unevenly etched inscription on this ancient monolith:

However, Oberon passes through the field as if it does not exist. Turning around to look at you, he shrugs: "This is a static field of psionic energies." He explains. "Only those with psionic powers can go through. Being keryndorhyan, I am so gifted."

With much frustration, you see that Strider is also able to pass through the barrier. "I've always suspected that there was some trace of lankharhan blood in you!" Oberon says to the ranger, with a wink. "Well, I do have psionic powers," Strider replies,
"but I don't know anything about having ancestry going back to Lankharh at some point or any other." With a nonplussed shrug, the ranger passes through the barrier again to rejoin you.

Gazing pensively at the structures of an ancient city peering out of the jungle ahead, Oberon sniffs petulantly: "Well, I can't go on by myself, now can I?" Chuckling, he passes through the barrier to rejoin you. "What now, then?" He wonders aloud.

With surprise, you see that Strider is able to pass through the barrier. "I wonder why this field is letting me through?" He muses. With a nonplussed shrug, the ranger passes through the barrier again to rejoin you.
The large, dome-shaped field of psionic energies still prevents you from going on further!
You run into a herd of dinosaurs on the search for food! Your presence greatly disturbs them!
"A good battle won by righteousness!" Tecoltitan muses while wiping his weapon clean.
"Again has the Feathered Serpent smiled upon us to give us victory!" Tecoltitan intones, bowing his head in silent prayer to his god.
"Praise be Quetzalcoualt for giving us strength against those who would stand to stop us!" Tecoltitan roars with joy, before getting to the business of cleaning up his weapon.
Once things have quieted down, you notice that this cave seems to extend deep into this mountain.
A large section of the cave wall here can be pushed to reveal a wide opening going deeper underground.
You go back underground.
You return above ground.
Death Emerald's hoard is now yours to take!
"We've found it!" An excited Tecoltitan bellows with joy. "The Tiara! Now, we must bring it back to my city and face the corrupt Highking Shamar-Tarac and the foul snake-men he takes council from!"

This large cavern is the lair of a huge emerald dragon. Flanked by numerous dragon lizards as pets, the emerald dragon scrutinizes you with a baleful stare: "Well, well! Intruders." It intones, showing its fearsome fangs in a cruel draconian smile.
The sight of those long, sharp fangs grips you with such fear that it takes all of your will to prevent you from simply running away!
"Lunch has arrived!" The emerald dragon announces to its pets. "Get it for me and you'll have some too!" At that, four of the dragon lizards move towards you with their fangs dripping with saliva.
"I'll get lunch for myself, then!" The emerald dragon roars, as he and his remaining dragon lizard pets move in for the kill!
Having dispatched the dragon, you set out to find its hoard.
As you enter this large cave, you find the mayaltec crusader -Tecoltitan- fighting for his life against dragon lizards. However, one of the beasts sees you, drawing you immediately into the fray!

A battered and bloodied Tecoltitan draws your attention to the back of the cave: "'Ware! Death Emerald is here!" At that, you spot the emerald dragon standing erect, showing its fearsome fangs in a cruel draconic smile.

Tecoltitan walks up to you, his demeanor quite solemn: "The Fates have conspired for us to meet again. With Death Emerald gone, I can retrieve the lost Tiara of the Highkings from its hoard. Whether you like it or not, we must walk together now!"
(Tecoltitan has joined your party. Check out the Allies menu).
However, one of the snake-men has seen you! Yelling out a warning to his comrades, he moves forward in your direction: it looks like you will have to fight in spite of your wishes!
This small, ancient ziggurat serves as a compound for psi-warriors!
This small, ancient ziggurat is abandoned and quite empty, except for dust and critters.

Standing under the stars, this large, ancient ziggurat is brightly lit by torches and fire wells. At the foot of the ziggurat's steps stand numerous psi-warriors, all lined up in formation and prepared to do battle. Obviously, you were expected ...

An armor-clad woman standing behind the line of psi-warriors calls you out: "On behalf of Consul Yavis Shuul, Ninth Speaker," she motions to the hooded man standing next to her, "and myself, Praetor Varlys Qui and Second Speaker, I bid you all welcome!"
You can't help but wince at the mention of this woman's name, for you remember well another warrior-woman of the Inner Council of the Overlords who also bore the name of 'Qui': General Arla Qui.

"As you have guessed," Praetor Qui continues with a cruel smile, "we two are the last Speakers of the Inner Council of Overlords. Last, that is, not counting our esteemed First Speaker, the High Praetor Primus Ankh." She lets out a dry chuckle.

"He did warn us about your annoying stubborness and that you would likely show up in Lankh'Nar, sooner or later. We hoped Commander Sura would be competent enough to neutralize you in Seacrest - but your presence here means that she failed us."

"Enough of this nonsense!" Oberon intervenes, glaring angrily at the two Overlords. "Don't you realize the abomination that Primus Ankh is seeking to unleash? Don't you know that he hosts the essence of the dreaded Hierarch?"

"Of course we do, traitor." Consul Yavis Shuul replies smugly. "Yes: I call you a traitor. As one of our kin, you should be standing with us, instead of against us and on the side of these filthy, degenerate mongrels!" Praetor Qui smiles at that.

"We may be kin," Oberon replies with disdain, "but truly you are fools to believe that you are superior to non-psionic races. You are even bigger fools if you believe that the Mentarchs will show you any special consideration. For in their mad eyes,
all of us are nothing but fodder for their evil whims!"

"Regardless," Praetor Qui goes on, "we cannot tolerate any interference from anyone, or anything! We stand here to destroy you once and for all, in the name of the Glorious Mentarchs!" Consul Yavis Shuul nods firmly in agreement.
"In addition", Qui adds between clenched teeth, "I finally get to avenge my younger sister Arla!"
At that, the two Overlords and their psi-warriors attack!
"I must admit," Oberon mumbles, panting and tired, "I am getting a bit too old for such sport!"
A battered Oberon moans loudly: "Now I remember why I never chose the life of adventurers!"
A bloodied Oberon sits down, wiping the copious sweat from his brow: "I swear I'll never, ever leave the comfort of the Hourglass Tower again, should I make it alive through this adventure!"
You decide to take a bit of rest before going inside the ziggurat.

This large, ancient ziggurat looms tall under the shining sun of the day. Standing at the foot of the ziggurat's steps are numerous psi-warriors, all lined up in formation and ready for the attack. Obviously, you were expected ...
You enter the ziggurat of Lankh'Nar.

The insides of the ziggurat are well preserved and quite clean. The main hall you find yourselves in has numerous library shelves, with each shelf filled with books. A quick survey tells you that these books are scientific and technomagic treatises.
Although the place seems as quiet as a tomb, you know that Primus/Maximus, and perhaps even the Mentarchs brought back from the past, are lurking around ... somewhere.
A small pool of continually flowing water is here. It adds a nice decorative touch to the place.
This place is a large laboratory. Jars, vials and containers of all sorts of strange concoctions and elixirs are strewn about on the floor and on work tables.

This ancient slab of solid obsidian serves as a landmark of some sort. Etched onto the slab are decorative bas-reliefs as well as the following: "THE LANKH'NAR NEW DAWN PROJECT: THE GLORIOUS FUTURE OF THE EMPIRE OF LANKHARH BEGAN HERE".
The sides of the slab are in turn etched with the names of various men and women, each one with lofty titles such as "Master Technomancer", "Master Technician", "Master Alchemist", etc.

"Glorious future indeed." Oberon mumbles sarcastically. "They created the Mentarchs and their very creations brought about the fall of the empire they sought to secure. What were those fools thinking?" He sighs with resignation at that.

Upon closer inspection, you notice that one of the decorative bas-reliefs of the obsidian slab can be depressed. After pushing on it, a segment of the wall behind the slab sinks into the floor to reveal a door!

You find in this room strange cylinders of glass set into what appears to be machines. Most of the cylinders are empty or broken, while the machines they are set into are lifeless. However, four of these cylinders are filled with some bubbling liquid.
Furthermore, the machines they are set into are alive with humming and blinking lights of many colors.

"In the name of Quanthaas!" Oberon exclaims. He is as white as ghost, his face contorted by dread and fear. "The worst possible nightmare! Primus/Maximus is trying to generate new Mentarch bodies to be used as hosts, in these active incubators!"

You wonder aloud why he would go through the trouble, since all the Mentarchs need are human hosts, preferably ones gifted with psionic powers. Oberon shakes his head vigorously at that: "Remember that the Mentarchs were long-lived! Not only are their

essences nearly immortal as long as they are hosted, but their physical bodies could last for a thousand year, if not more! Primus/Maximus not only wants to bring back the reign of the Mind Lords, but he also wants himself and his siblings to be whole!"

You then cast a suspicious glance in Strider's direction. Seeing that, he throws up his hands in helpless surrender: "Now wait here!" He intones, almost ruefully. "Yes, I *am* long-lived and I *do* have mental powers, but I'm *not* a Mentarch!"

"I was born a normal human who happened to have somehow inherited psionic powers. My long-life is magical in nature since, as I told you already, I fell into a vat filled with some sort of longevity potion made by a dark wizard I had just destroyed!"
Knowing that Strider speaks the truth, you nonetheless pretend to still harbor suspicions about him - just to rattle his chains a little.
To your satisfaction, you see Galduur fighting hard not laugh out loud.
"Let us not waste any time!" Oberon continues, very much in earnest. "We have to destroy those active incubators!"
You notice that a small mass of living tissue is floating within the liquid of this container. Blebbling and contorting, it seems to be alive ... and growing. Do you try to break the cylinder?

Hefting your hardest weapon, you give it your best shot! As all of the cylinder's contents spill on the cold floor, the living mass of tissue undergoes death spasms while the machine of the cylinder shuts down.
Primus Ankh stands defiant before you. It is with much surprise that you find him flanked by Varlys Qui and Yavis Shuul, who seem rather healthy despite the fact that you killed them earlier.
Only then you notice in the back of the room a vortex of shimmering flames swirling and twisting above the floor.

"While you were busy destroying his holy work," Primus snarls, "our Omniscience the Hierarch left my body and returned to his abode in the Astral Plane, taking with him the revered Mentarchs he rescued from the past." He chuckles coldly at that.

"At the same time, I revived my collegues, Varlys and Yavis, then simply waited for you. Once we are done with you mongrels, I'll then stabilize my dimensional machine and give the good news to our revered Hierarch, so that he may return once more."

"How could mites like you have succeeded time and again at foiling me, then we the Overlords, and even our revered Hierarch? Well, it doesn't matter anymore: now, *finally*, I get my chance to personally destroy you once and for all!"
At that, the fight is on!

Primus then explodes with anger: "How dare you? How dare you intervene in the grandest plan of them all? We were so close to bring about the Second Rising in the past! And now, here, yet again you seek to prevent us from achieving our holy endeavor!"
Panting and tired, you set yourself to examine the strange vortex floating above the floor at the back of this room.
Primus' dimensional machine lies still, power-depleted and probably broken as well.

The vortex of shimmering flames still swirls wildly above the floor. You notice that its size fluctuates greatly, as if being unstable: chances are that Primus' dimensional machine which created this hole to the Astral Plane will soon breakdown.
Knowing that going through the vortex is almost assuredly a one-way trip, do you jump into the vortex to follow Maximus and his siblings in the Astral Plane?

"The Mind Lords must be destroyed once and for all, even if hunting them down in the Astral Plane means that maybe we'll never come home. But if we don't try, what will prevent Maximus from finding another host and seek to return once again?"

He shakes his head at that. "Whether it takes a week, a year or thousands of years, Maximus will try again - that is for certain. So, if you do not go, then I will - even if alone!" Without further due, Strider jumps into the vortex!
"Wait fer me, ye crazy fool!" Galduur yells out, before following his friend.
"I must fulfill my duty to the Eternal One." Lindanyl announces. "With or without you, I must attempt to destroy the Mentarchs once and for all." With a curt nod, she walks into the vortex!

"Lady Goldenfair is a very respected highpriestess, among my people." Sarin muses aloud, with a shrug. "I'd be remiss if I did not accompany her on this dangerous journey." At that, he follows Lindanyl's footsteps.

"I'm saddened by your decision." Oberon tells you, his head hanging low. "But I suppose, you have the right of it - especially after all you have accomplished. I will now return to the Hourglass Tower, where I will inform my peers of this development."

"The world will be safe from Maximus and his siblings for a while - how long, I do not know. Perhaps a hundred years, perhaps a few thousands. One thing I do know: one day, the Mind Lords will again return to threaten all of us."
Sighing, he extends his hand to shake yours: "Thus I bid you here goodbye, as well as safe journeys and safer returns." Without another word, Oberon weaves a spell and vanishes.

"Well, it's been fun!" Galduur mumbles as he shakes your hand. "But me got some Mind Lord huntin' to do, ye know? An' me don't care where the huntin' ground be!" With a final salute with his axe, Galduur goes through the vortex.
Soon enough, Primus' machine runs out of power, shutting down the vortex and your only known mean to go to the Astral Plane.
Gazing blankly at the now lifeless machine, you wonder if you made the right decision by not going to the Astral Plane, and attempt to destroy Maximus and his siblings once and for all.

With a shrug, you push away those questions. You have accomplished much, and even more - so, perhaps it is time to let others take care of the problems of the world. Taking a deep breath, you realize that you have a whole, new continent to explore.

Who knows now, what mysteries will you uncover on the continent of Anarym? Who knows what new adventures you are to find on this vast, unknown continent? Revitalized and elated by these prospects, you set yourself to undertake your next journeys!

(Congratulations! You have completed one possible ending to the main story-arc of Wrath of the Mind Lords! Feel free to explore more, for there are many other smaller adventures and encounters for you to experience.)
(Thank you again for registering the scenario. We hope you have enjoyed this conclusion of the Sword Lands Trilogy. Safe journeys and safer returns!)
Without any further thought, you jump into the vortex!

You then feel as if you are floating in a void, not sure whether you are alive or dead. But suddenly, all your senses come back to you as you find yourself standing in the middle of a very eerie place!

You find Primus Ankh in this room, guarded by his personal lieutenants. Upon your entrance, he calmly rises from his bed -as if expecting you. Only then do you notice three glowing globes set in the back of the room -the essences of the other mentarchs.

"Greetings, fools." Primus/Maximus snarls with his otherworldly voice. "Yes, it is I, Maximus, who is speaking to you. It seems our meetings are often oh-so-fleeting: for once again, I will depart shortly." He adds with a dry chuckle.

He then glares at Oberon: "I recognize the symbol that you are wearing." He intones, pointing to the hourglass embroidered upon Oberon's robe. "Now I understand much of what has transpired. A traitor *and* and Time Master. Yes." He nods to himself.
A machine suddenly activates, opening a vortex of shimmering flames, swirling and twisting above the floor.
Wordlessly, Primus/Maximus then calmly turns his gaze to the far back of the room.
Primus then screams, his body convulsing violently. At the same time, he is bathed in a blinding light.

Your are then face to face with the essence of Maximus. Casting an angry glare at you, he floats to the back of the room: "TAKE CARE OF THIS NUISANCE!" You hear him order Primus, as he lifts the essence-orbs and jumps into the vortex!

A fully recovered Primus snarls: "Our Omniscience the Hierarch just left my body and returned to his abode in the Astral Plane, taking with him the revered Mentarchs he rescued from the past." He chuckles coldly at that.

"I, along with my personal aides, are to prevent you from following him. Once we are done with you mongrels, I'll then stabilize my dimensional machine and give the good news to our revered Hierarch, so that he may return once more."
Primus Ankh's personal fortune is now yours to take.

Chuckling, you manage to get a word in edgewise and tell them that you have taken care of the problem concerning the bandits and marauders, by defeating the electromancer Stygiax and his conspirators. "Me be impressed!" Galduur grunts. "Aye!" Raack adds.
The ranger then shrugs: "Well, I'm sure we'll find some other mischief for us to do together, in the meantime!" Both he and Galduur chuckle at that.
You decide that perhaps you should investigate the monolith at the next opportunity that you get - that is, once you are done with Stygiax.
Yavis Shuul's personal fortune is now yours to take!
Varlys Qui's personal fortune is now yours!
This strange diagram etched permanently into the psionic matter here pulses with powerful magic.

You are suddenly enveloped in a shroud of psionic energies! You then feel as if you are floating in a void, unsure whether you are alive or dead. Immediately after, all your senses come back to you as you find yourself back in the ziggurat of Lankh'Nar!
You and your comrades celebrate with joy and great relief your safe return on Lhari Orin.

"Praise be Quanthaas! We've done it!" An elated Oberon exclaims, clapping his hands with happiness. "I must give the news and a full account to my peers as soon as possible!" He then shakes your hand with much warmth. "What an extraordinary feat!"

He laughs with excitement. "Truly, you are more than heroes! Knowing that, had Maximus or any other of his siblings remained safely back in the Astral Plane, then the menace of the Mind Lords would most certainly have eventually returned!"

He then sighs. "I must admit that all of this adventuring and excitement makes me long for the comforts of the Hourglass Tower. I *am* a scholar after all!" He adds, with a wink. "I bid you all safe journeys and safer returns! Perhaps, one of these days,
we shall meet again! I sincerely hope so, Quanthaas willing!" With final partings, the chronomancer vanishes into thin air.

Strider claps you on the shoulder, grinning from ear to ear: "Once again, we have saved the day - and the world-, eh?"  He then sighs. "Truly, it was an honor for me to walk alongside of you, friends. But now I must take my leave, for I find myself back

on the continent of my birth and I wish to revisit my old stomping grounds - the city of Southgate, to be precise. Who knows? If you decide to explore more of Anarym, the Fates will surely make our paths cross again!" He shakes your hand warmly at that.
With final partings and well-wishes, Strider whips up a rod of teleportation and activates it.

Lindanyl comes up to you and gives you a warm embrace. "Much we've lived together, no?" She speaks softly, with a beaming smile. "I'm afraid that now I must return to my homeland, if only to inform my church of the latest developments." She sighs.

"Then I will have to journey anew, as I must travel far up north to the Great Citadel of Quanthaas and give a full account as well to the High Council of my priesthood. Whether we meet again or not, I will never forget you!"
With final goodbyes, Lindanyl weaves a spell of teleportation.

"Not that I want to quell the festivities," Starrune announces to you, "but now that we've set things a-right and destroyed the Mentarchs, I wish to return to my abode and continue my magical research." She bows her head at that:
"It is an honor to have known you and to have journeyed with you all." Without further due, the ever-aloof Starrune weaves a spell and teleports herself away.

"Well, me dunno about ye, but me sure longs fer some good drinks, eh?" Galduur exclaims with a grin, clapping you hard on the shoulder. "So, what say ye we leave this accursed place and head fer the nearest tavern? Maybe we'll find some more tourism
to do along the way too!" He adds with a wink. You can't help but laugh at that.

A tired Nasslass comes up to you. "Me dunno about ye, but me sure longs fer a rest." He breathes deeply, smelling the ambient jungle aromas. "Yup. Me'll lost meself a bit in this warm and cozy jungle, perhaps even find a nice place to make me a home!"
"It sure was fun, eh?" He adds with a wink, before embracing you warmly. Without another word, Nasslass picks up his gear and slowly walks away.

"Another saga for me to write about!" A beaming Riel intones, chuckling at the same time. "So, my friends: what's next? I don't know about you, but I'm curious to explore this continent of Anarym. But of course, first we must find a good inn to rest!"
You nod at his suggestion, laughing along with him.

"Well, that was -um- interesting!" Nerylka muses with a mischievous smile. "Truly, I still can't believe we managed to pull it off! So, what's next for us?" Before you can answer, she waves her hand in warding: "No, no, no! First, I need a good meal,
a good drink *and* a good bath! *Then* you can tell me where else you think we should go to risk our lives and limbs!" She then laughs out loud at that; you can't help but join her.

"Now that we've tried our hand at destroying God-like beings, I suggest that we find ourselves an actual God and slay him!" A deadpan Sarin announces aloud. As everyone erupt in laughter, the elf adds with mock seriousness: "Okay, then! Let us find
an inn first to rest, *then* find ourselves a God or two to slay!" At that, Sarin can't hold himself any longer and joins everyone in the laughter.
As the merriment begins to die down, it dawns on you that you do have a whole new continent to explore.
(Congratulations! You have completed the main story-arc of Wrath of the Mind Lords! Feel free to explore more, for there are many other smaller adventures and encounters for you to experience.)

Strider then turns to Galduur with a mischievous grin: "And what about you, old friend? Want to do some tourism along with me?" Galduur pretends to be offended: "Tourism? Tourism? Me tell ye what: ye'll do the durn tourism and me'll do the fightin'!"

"Besides," the dwarven hero mumbles, "who else is going to make sure that ye don't always burden yerself with all the problems of the world?" Galduur then gives you a friendly clout on the shoulder: "Well, it's been fun, eh?" He chuckles.

"Safe journeys and safer returns, friends!" The dwarf adds. "Me sure we'll meet again one of them days - when this happens, we'll have to remember this day over a nice mead, or two, or even more!" He winks at that.
No one is about this dais at this time of the evening, leaving a small boat unwatched and unguarded.
Do you want to steal that boat?
This dais is guarded by ssethanti warriors. One of the warriors sounds the call to arms upon spottting your approach!
With the dais unguarded, you are free to take the small boat anchored here.
The gate of these fortifications is guarded by ssethanti warriors. One of the warriors sounds the call to arms upon spottting your approach!
This large ziggurat is quite ancient. You notice that its top has a metallic spire set into it. The spire, itself reaching quite high in the sky, pulses rhythmically with a strange blueish light.
The gate of these fortifications seems unguarded at this time of the evening.
Thankfully, no one is guarding the entrance of the ziggurat at this time.
However, the ziggurat is well guarded by ssethanti warriors!
Panting and tired, you enter the ziggurat.

The main hall of the ziggurat is filled with marble columns etched with numerous bas-reliefs of snakes of all sizes and shapes. In the center stands a large statue of a snake, sculpted and painted with intricate details, making it seem almost alive.

You also notice other statues about the place, bearing the likeness of Sseth in its demonic form. Obviously, this place is some sort of holy shrine dedicated to the dark god of evil, reptiles and snakes.

Case in point:  numerous ssethanti priests are currently standing before the large snake statue, quite busy chanting and praising Sseth in some sort of religious ceremony. Of course, none of them appreciate your intrusion!
Numerous ssethanti priests live here!
You have been spotted by psi-warriors!
Numerous ssethanti warriors live here!
You have been spotted by ssethanti warriors!
Ssethanti highpriests live here!
With a primal and terrifying scream, the ssethanti Queen summons more help!

A truly repulsive sight is offered to you upon entering this room. Sitting on a throne is a creature -an abomination- that is half-woman and half-snake, with snake-like hairs moving and writhing sickeningly about her head. She flicks a forked tongue

at you, her reptilian eyes glaring with evil and hatred. All about her are snakes of many species, gliding and twisting in contentment at being near her - in fact, a mammoth snake is wrapped protectively around her, affectionately flicking its tongue

in her direction. "I was expecting you." The ssethanti Queen announces with a hiss. "Your impending arrival was foretold to me by those that my people were originally created to serve." She chuckles - or rather, gurgles- at your confusion.

"We were created a long time ago by the lankharhans of old. We were perfect humans, designed with enhanced capacities for endurance and adaptation. But not long after the fall of the Lankharhan empire, this perfection in us proved to be a flaw."

She hisses again. "Left on our own to live in this jungle, our design-enhanced adaptive capabilities caused us to mutate to mimic the attributes of reptiles, the best suited to survive in such an environment. Only us Queens have ever known this truth."

She then flicks her tongue in the air. "But our people were at a loss, so the Cult of Sseth was instituted to keep them under control and give them pride. Thus, my people do not know our true purpose, which is to watch over the ruins of Lankh'Nar."

She then slithers to the south wall, where a strange machine is obviously activated, humming and crackling with energy. "And to guard the Nexus Source," the Queen adds, "which generates a shield over what is called the Forbidden City, in order to prevent

anything from despoiling it. Anything, that is, but those endowed with mental powers like our creators of old." She chuckles anew. "Of course, to my people, the Nexus Source is a holy relic from Sseth, which can be looked upon only by Queens, like me."

The ssethanti slithers back to her throne. "Likewise, queens like me are worshiped by my people as being blessed by the Mighty Serpent Sseth - and so is this ziggurat holy and sacred to them." She take a deep, hissing breath at that. "But enough of this
chatter. It is time for me to honor the word of my ancestors, if only in gratitude for my race having been given life by the lankharhans!" At that, the ssethanti Queen and her pets attack!
"My people ..." The dying queen hisses. "They will be lost ... without a queen ... But we were made ... perfect ... We will ... regroup ... and adapt." At that, the abomination dies.
Felled by a fatal attack, the ssethanti Queen lets out a primal, otherworldly scream that echoes loudly throughout the place. Her death knell was probably heard a league or two away from here!
The ssethanti Queen's throne is set with numerous gems and gem stones. Do you pry them off?
The Nexus Source now lies inactive and dormant.
Having faced the ssethanti Queen, you understand quite well what this riddle is all about.

The Nexus Source, as called by the defunct ssethanti Queen, consists of a strange dome-like machine with protruding spires. Energy is somehow produced at the tip of the spires; these sparks of energy coalesce into a crystal-shaped lattice which seems to

float above the machine. In turn, the lattice discharges pulses of energy to the ceiling: looking up, you see that these pulses are aimed at a metallic spike set into the ceiling. You then realize that this spike is the bottom end of the tall, pulsating
spire that you saw atop the ziggurat when you entered it. Looking back down, you notice on the machine two sets of square colored panels: one on the right and one on the left.
Hefting your hardest weapon, you give one good whack at the dome-shaped machine!
With a few lucky bashes, the broken machine shuts off without a hitch!
The Nexus Source lies broken and inactive.
The machine explodes violently, the released energies vaporizing everything in the immediate vicinity!
The machine explodes violently!
There are two sets of colored panels on the Nexus Source: one on the right and one on the left. Which side to you wish to begin with?
Right.
Left.
Looking on the right side, you see three square-shaped panels which can be pushed on: one is Blue, one is Yellow and one is Black. The Blue one is currently depressed. What do you do?
Pressing on the Yellow square causes the machine to hum louder as the crystal-shaped lattice of energy changes color to yellow.
Do you wish to reconsider your action?
Pressing on the Blue square, the crystal-shaped lattice of energy remains blue.
Pressing on the Black square, the crystal-shaped lattice of energy dissipates and disappears.
Looking on the left side, you see three square-shaped panels which can be pushed on: one is Green, one is Yellow and one is Red. The Green one is currently depressed. What do you do?
The machine shuts down gradually, its humming dying out.
The humming of the machine becomes louder.
The machine hums along.
Success! The Nexus Source shuts down completely and without a hitch!
The shutting down of the lattice while keeping the machine feeding it functional creates a fatal feedback of energy, causing a tremendous explosion that vaporizes everything in the vicinity!
Shutting off the machine without killing off the crystal-shaped energy lattice causes the lattice to implode violently!

To your surprise, you find the ssethanti city abandoned by its people. They probably heard the unnatural death knell of their revered Queen when you fell her and, as she mumbled while rendering her last breath, they panicked and fled to the jungle.
By your estimation, they are most likely scattered throughout the jungle by now, making them no more a threat to the region ... at least for the time being.

"It is best that I leave and bring news to my sisters!" An elated Sherrinka announces, having come to the same conclusion as you. "In the name of my pride, I thank you. Peace and security will come back, now that the snake people have scattered."
She inclines her head respectfully to you: "I am honored to have walked and fought by your side. I wish you success and long life!" With a final goodbye, the tigtaur leaves to return home.
The gates of the ssethanti walled city are heavily guarded. Do you really want to attempt at forcing your way in?
Seeing that more ssethanti are mobilizing quickly to repel your assault, do you change your mind and run away to fight another way?
From the few items left behind in this building, it would seem that this place used to be some kind of shop.
From the looks of it, this small ziggurat was a temple dedicated to Sseth before it was abandoned.
Native creatures of the Astral Plane are disturbed by your presence!
Suddenly, the ambient psionic energies of the Astral Plane begin to twist and swirl about you. In no time, you find yourselves caught in the middle of a raging psychic storm!

Thanks to your increased awareness, you sense the ambient psionic energies of the Astral Plane begining to twist and swirl. Sensing danger, you move away as fast as you can, allowing your escape from being caught in the middle of a raging psychic storm!
An instant later, the eerie storm dissipates - but not without leaving you unscathed.
Going deeper into the Astral Plane would surely spell your doom, for you do not have the necessary magic and knowledge to find your way -let alone survive- in the Deep Astral.
You run into an Ashaan'ru raiding party!

An Ashaan'ru ship seemingly appears out of nowhere. Try to outrun it as you might, the ship manages to catch up with you: you barely have time to brace yourself when an Ashaan'ru raiding party boards your ship!
You are jumped upon by an Ashaan'ru raiding party!
You are caught unaware by an Ashaan'ru raiding party that swiftly boards you!
Considering that finding the means to return to the Astral Plane are remote at best, you decide to complete the task of destroying Xenon Maximus, before seeking to return to Lhari Orin.

The Astral PLane appears as a trackless and featureless expanse of ambient psionic energies, punctuated by small floating islands of what appears to be proto-psionic matter. The place is quite disorienting, as there doesn't seem to be any "up" or "down",

and the ambient psionic energies keep assaulting your brain -giving you a mild headache. You suspect that after an hour or two, your senses and perceptions will adjust themselves to the eerie surroundings. Likewise, the mild headache will also fade away.

"I'm not an expert," Oberon muses, "but what I know of the Astral PLane is this: mind and thought rule here, and those with powerful minds can mold and sculpt the psionic energies of the place into large matter-like constructions." He raises an eyebrow.

"Once the mind of a matter-creator leaves the Astral Plane or dies, then his matter-like creation very slowly degrades in order to return to its ambient psionic energy state. One more thing: terrible creatures roam this place! We must be extremely wary!"

Standing at the end of this pier, you take in the full vastness of the Astral Plane. Thinking that the place looks like a trackless sea that goes in every direction, psionic energies suddenly begin to coalesce at the end of the pier!
A boat-like creation of psionic proto-matter forms before your amazed eyes!
"See?" An elated Oberon exclaims. "Mind and thought rule here! Even minds like ours can create proto-matter here for basic things like transportation!"

Standing at the end of the pier, you think hard about how the Astral Plane looks like a trackless sea - and sure enough, you manage to create another boat-like vessel out of the ambient psionic energies!
"Talk about me going where me's never gone before!" A bewildered Galduur mumbles while stroking his beard nervously.
"This place sure gives me the creeps!" Nasslass muses to himself, his eyes blinking with fright.
"I'm at a loss for words!" Riel whispers, enthralled by the alien surroundings.
"We're not in Tanirith anymore!" Nerylka muses, very much in awe.
"This is *very* interesting!" Starrune intones, more to herself than to anyone else.
"How I long for my homeland!" Sarin whispers, visibly unsettled by the eerie surroundings.
You see Lindanyl uttering a whispered prayer to Quanthaas, the god she serves, as well as to Astrane, the Goddess of the Moons and the Stars.

"Well, we better get on our way!" Strider announces with a smile. He appears absolutely unaffected by the experience. "I doubt the Mind Lords will do the courtesy of waiting for us!" He adds with a wink.

An eerie castle with twisted towers and spires stands here. Twisted, haunting tree-like creations also stand about, making you wonder who -or what- is mad enough to create such a horrific caricature of life back in the world.
As you approach, you are assaulted by waves of psionic energies!
Then out of the castle emerges the essence of a Mentarch!

"So, you are the little worms who have been such trouble to my brother Xenon." The essence muses with a lustful, seductive feminine voice. She chuckles cruely: "Well I, Sappho Nynex, know how to command the respect that a goddess like me requires."

She pauses for a moment, then grins maliciously: "So, my little worms, I offer you a choice: prostrate yourselves before me and I shall prove merciful; refuse, and I promise you a very slow and painful death!" Do you accept and bow down to her?
"Good little worms." Sappho Nynex crows, still smiling maliciously. "Yes. I shall be merciful and slay you quickly, then!" At that, the female Mind Lord attacks!
Sappho Nynex goes into a fit. "How dare you refuse *me*, impudent worms that you are! You will pay dearly for this affront to me!" At that, the female Mind Lord attacks!
You decide to mend your wounds before entering the castle.
"Back for more, eh?" You hear the disembodied voice of Sappho Nynex, echoing with cruelty and sadism. An instant later, she appears before you and attacks!
You enter this foreboding castle.

In contrast to its intricately twisted exteriors, the indoors of the castle are a testament of bland, rigid order and calmness. Surprisingly, the castle appears to be made up of one large hall filled with sparkling columns of marble,
its ceiling seemingly reaching as high as you can see. Although you do not spot any torches or lanterns, this strange hall is bathed with an ambient soft, white light.

"Welcome to my abode." A booming voice intones. Ahead of you, further down the hall, you see three Mind Lord essences floating soundlessly above the floor. With dread, you recognize the distinctive voice of Xenon Maximus as the one who has greeted you.
Steeling your nerves, you move on forward.

As you near the Mind Lords, two of them move slightly forward to flank protectively the third one. "So, the end-game is upon us at last!" Intones the Mentarch in the middle; by his voice, you recognize him as Maximus. "As you can see, our essences can be

free of the need for a corporeal body almost indefinitely, as long as we remain here on the Astral Plane." Maximus continues, quite smug. "That is how I managed to last for thousands of years without a host. Nonetheless, I was quite happy when Primus

contacted me, after finding Lankh'Nar and the dimensional machine I myself used to escape here in the first place. That was ten years ago." He pauses at that, then chuckles. "A very short time, granted. But for beings such as we, time is meaningless as

long as we remain here. I shall miss Primus, for he was a very loyal lackey. But there will be other opportunities for us to reclaim our birthright as Ruling Gods of Lhari-Orin, for time is on our side." In unisson, the three Mentarchs chuckle wickedly.

"This is where you err, Maximus!" Oberon intejects, his eyes glaring with determination. "We have come here to put an end to your existence, to rid the world of your menace once and for all! You who believe that might makes right, that power grants you

superiority, will finally learn the truth: only wisdom and compassion make right! This truth the Noble Three -Kith Khanaan, Umma Porogrove and Shalym Relimanab- did always understand. That is why they sought initially to save you from madness!"

"These names are not to be mentioned in my presence! How dare you address me, traitor to your race!" Maximus roars, his essence glowing with anger and hatred. "My race?" An indignant Oberon replies. "See my point? Whether you like it or not, lankharhans

created you, using lankharhan tissues and bodies! They were irresponsible in trying to create the highest advanced lankharhans possible, but at least they were naively well intentioned. The Noble Three always understood that the Mentarchs were meant

to be *lankharhans* first, enlightened teachers second, and kind rulers third. But your ilk selfishly rejected this basic truth of your creation. Instead, you chose in your arrogance to become the worst of racists - even to your own, true, blood!"

"Be that as it may," a suddenly aloof Maximus interjects, "upon my return here, I have sensed that a mage has settled in the Astral Plane - and relatively near my abode at that. This means that she has the knowledge to travel the Planes and thus is

possessed of great power. Herein lies my new plan to bring about our Second Rising: although this mage may not be of lankharhan descent, she will be quite suitable nonetheless as a host for me! Indeed, she will allow me to travel the Planes easily!"
You then realize that the mad Hierarch is talking about the Sceptanar!

Maximus continues in earnest, turning to his two remaining siblings: "So harken, Nuul Zarrakian and Azure Malachys! We will yet succeed, provided that we rid ourselves of these dangerous individuals! Remember that they destroyed Uther and Sappho!"
"Now it is their turn!" The Mentarch Nuul intones with a snarl. "Indeed." Adds the Mentarch Azure. "They will pay for their heresy and defiance!" At that, the two Mentarchs attack!

Maximus bellows with laughter. "No more must I, the Hierarch, burden myself with any of my lesser siblings. They have served their purpose to weaken you, so that I may deliver the final blow and send you to the netherworld were filth like you belong!"

"From now on, only I alone will rule the world like a God." Maximus adds. " This is my birthright, my destiny!" With another crazed bellow of laughter, the truly mad Hierarch summons denizens of the Astral Plane to his help and then attacks!

As you rejoice at having finally defeated Maximus, you can't help but think that you should dare not celebrate just yet: indeed, you must leave the Astral Plane and return safely home before you can fully celebrate your victory.
The only burning question nagging at you is: how exactly do you go about it?
You return to the surface.
A large crystal-like stucture of proto-psionic matter has been created here, sparkling as if it contains milions of minute stars.

As you approach, the facade of this building begins to change shape, taking on the gigantic features of the face of a very comely woman. At first as impassive as the crystal-like matter she appears to be made from, she then opens her crystalline eyes.
"I am the Sceptanar, a powerful mage." She intones with a booming voice. " Who are you and why have you come to the doorstep of my Sanctum Sanctorum?"
"Very well." The crystalline apparition of the Sceptanar replies. "I bid you safe journeys and safer returns." At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features.

"I do not bow to arrogant demands and extorsion threats!" An indignant Sceptanar replies. "Begone from here and better not return until you learn some manners!" At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features.
As you approach, the facade of this building changes shape again to take on the gigantic features of the face of its owner, the Sceptanar. This time, she looks somewhat annoyed.
"You again?" She asks. "What is it you want, now?"
"Very well. But I would appreciate not being bothered for no valid reason!" The crystalline apparition of the Sceptanar replies. At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features.
As you approach, the facade of this building changes shape again to take on the gigantic features of the face of its owner, the Sceptanar. This time, she looks quite angry.

"Fools! You will pay for your arrogance!" An indignant Sceptanar replies. As the facade of the building returns to its original features, creatures summoned by the Sceptanar appear to teach you a lesson!
"You know, she does have a point!" Oberon mumbles.
"Sometimes, I just don't understand you." Strider mumbles, quite critical of your attitude.

"Very well. Nice to see that you have manners after all. But I would appreciate not being bothered for no valid reason!" The crystalline apparition of the Sceptanar replies. At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features.

"I see." The Sceptanar replies. "Like me, you are not of the Astral Plane. In the course of my ascension as a powerful mage, I discovered magic spells and devices which allow for anyone to travel between the world and this plane."

She smiles at that. "After mastering this knowledge, I decided to come here and create my private sanctum sanctorum out of psionic proto-matter, so that I could continue my research in quietude - and yet being able to return at will to the world."
She then frowns in thought, before continuing: "I have the knowledge which will allow you to return to the world. However, I ask in exchange that you perform a task for me." Do you accept?

"Good!" The Sceptanar replies, quite pleased. "To the west of here is a fortress. It is inhabited by a brood of Ashaan'ru, creatures indigenous to the Astral Plane. Each brood has one Queen, who in fact spawns all of the drones who serve her."

"The Ashaan'ru", the Sceptanar goes on, "have a pirate-like culture, continually roaming the Astral Plane to raid and pillage, bringing back the spoils to the Queen they love like a mother. Many sevendays ago, three of my summoned servants were

attacked by an Ashaan'ru astral vessel, as they were journeying back to my abode with treasure that I bade them to get for me. Aside from gems and other baubles, one of the items that was stolen by the Ashaan'ru was the serpent's head, which I sorely

need for my magical research. I do not have the time to get it back myself. Thus, the task that I ask of you is to raid the Ashaan'ru fortress and retrieve the serpent's head for me. Bring it back and I shall provide you with the means to return home."
At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features. With a determined nod, you get on your way.
As you stand again before the abode of the Sceptanar, do you reconsider and accept the offer she made earlier?
As if having read your mind, the Sceptanar causes the facade of her abode to adopt once more the features of her face. This time, she smiles warmly at you.
You proudly announce to the Sceptanar that you have killed the Ashaan'ru Queen, scattering the remnants of her brood for the time being.

"Have you the serpent's head?" She asks. Unfortunately, you are unable to produce the item for her. "Then return to the fortress and search better!"  She replies with annoyance. At that, the facade of the building returns to its original features.

"Have you the serpent's head?" She asks. As you produce the item, it vanishes before your eyes. "Thank you. As agreed, I now respect my end of the bargain. There is an island of psionic proto-matter north and west of here. No one knows who or what

of your trek in the Astral Plane. "Step on the diagram," the Sceptanar continues, "and speak the words 'ethro astranox'. This will activate a gate and send you home. Use this gate only if you are truly ready to leave, for this will be a one-way trip!"

created it - interestingly enough, it appears to be permanent in nature. In any case, you will find on this island a magic diagram permanently etched onto the ground." It is now obvious to you that she speaks of the place where you arrived at the start
"You again?" She asks. "Haven't you left the Astral Plane yet? Our business is concluded: leave me be or face the consequences!"
"What is it now?" She asks. "Our business is concluded: leave this plane already, so that I may finally get some peace and quiet to perform my magical research!"
"You again?" She asks. "Don't you have someone else to bother? The Astral Plane is big enough for you to get lost and leave me be!"
Without further due, the facade of the building returns to its original features.
"You again?" She asks. "Why don't you bother me once you have completed your own part of the bargain!" Without further due, the facade of the building returns to its original features.
You board this Ashaan'ru astral vessel!
The now unoccupied ashaan'ru vessel dissipates into the ambient psionic energies of the Astral Plane.
The doors of this fortress are heavily guarded!
You decide to mend your wounds as best as you can before entering the fortress.
You enter the fortress.
You enter a communal hall ... filled with ashaan'ru warriors!
This is a dormitory.
The place looks abandoned. You find nothing of interest.
Unfortunately, it is occupied!

This is a food storage room. Strangely, none of the food you find here is edible for you - you then realize that since you have landed in the Astra Plane, not once have you ever felt the pangs of thirst or hunger.
It would seem that, as 'extra-planar' non-natives, you do not need sustenance while traveling the Astral Plane, whereas creatures native to the plane do.
An ashaan'ru patrol has found you!
This is the breeding chamber of the Ashaan'ru Queen. Protected by her elite drones and breeders, she screams her outrage at your intrusion!

This room is damp, the floor covered with some sort of green mucus-like goo. Numerous sarcophagi are placed about the place, also covered with mucus. Being semi-transparent, you see that the sarcophagi are filled with larva-like creatures, squirming and
