writhing as they eat away at the goo. Without their mother and her helpers to take care of them, these ashaan'ru larvae are doomed to die. Taking your attention away from this gruesome scene, you spot the treasure-bed of the Queen at the end of the room.
The ashaan'ru Queen dies with a hideous scream. Confused and lost without their mother and leader, the breeders and drones scatter in panic!
The ashaan'ru Queen's hoard is now yours!

Formely occupied by an ashaan'ru brood, this island appears to be completely abandoned now, the remaining drones having scattered throughout the Astral Plane until a new queen rises among them - perhaps to establish yet another brood.

Without a word, you take the tellurian key that you found and show it to Lindanyl. At first surprised and shocked, she then smiles, excitement lighting her amber eyes: "Very well, then! As for my second task," Lindanyl goes on,
"One more notch to my blade." Strider comments laconically. He then winks at you with a grin.
"You know," Strider muses while wiping his weapon clean, "things just never get any easier. I wonder which God or Goddess we have angered to deserve this?" He then sighs wearily.
"Why is it that beasties keep trying to kill us? Haven't they figured out yet that we are too strong?" Strider intones, before winking at you mischievously.
Without further due, you walk away.
"Praise the Fates!" Sarin exclaims, visibly happy at your decision. Gathering his gear, he sets himself to follow you.

"My comrades." Tecoltitan interjects. "We need to find my cathoon friend, Mrrysh Walksfar, if we are to bring peace between my people and his. He told me he was headed to the place called Edgemoor - I insist that we go there to find him!"

"My apologies," Tecoltitan interjects, "but I insist that we must find my cathoon friend, Mrrysh Walksfar, if we are to bring peace between my people and his. He told me he was headed to the place called Edgemoor - we should go there first, then!"

"My apologies," Tecoltitan interjects. "but we need to find my cathoon friend, Mrrysh Walksfar, if we are to bring peace between my people and his. He told me he was headed to the place called Edgemoor - I insist that we go there to find him!"
Seeing that he is not about to compromise on this, you shrug and turn around to head back to the greater Seacrest area.

There doesn't seem to be any way to enter this village except by having to go through all of its inhabitants. Considering that these lizard men seem to be keeping to themselves without bothering anyone, you decide to leave them be.
You stumble unto the nearly-fossilized remains of hundreds of dwarven warriors here. It seems that they died in some horrendous battle, judging by the way their remains lie scattered about the place.

Paying closer attention, you guess that these unfortunate ones were running away from a location further south from your position, before making their fatal standoff. However, searching among the remains, you find nothing of interest.
Dozens more nearly-fossilized skeletons of dwarven warriors lie scattered here, confirming your earlier hunch.

"By Moradin!" Galduur gasps, horrified by the scene. "What could've happened to cause all of this death?" He then spits on the rocks in a superstitious gesture, as if trying to ward off whatever caused the downfall of these dwarves.
Dozens more nearly-fossilized skeletons of dwarven warriors lie scattered here.

Paying closer attention, you guess that these unfortunate ones were running away from a location just west and north from your position, before making their fatal standoff. However, searching among the remains, you find nothing of interest.

Dozens more nearly-fossilized skeletons of dwarven warriors lie scattered here, confirming your earlier hunch. Furthermore, you notice that they seemed to have been running away from a cave entrance just to the northeast, before meeting their demise.
A truly horrific sight is now before you: hundreds -if not thousands- of nearly-fossilized remains of fallen dwarven warriors seem to fill the lenght of this passage, pilled up one upon another.
In your mindseye, you can almost see the frozen looks of pure fear they displayed before their death.
The sight of such an alien entity and the aura of cold darkness it emanates assault you with waves of gut-wrenching fear, making it quite hard to resist from simply running away.

Entering the mines of Duhelarholme, you notice numerous, near-fossilized fallen dwarven warriors scattered here and there about the place. You wonder what killed them so long ago. However, you find nothing of interest among the remains.
You find it extremely difficult -as well as repulsive- to negociate your way through those piles of near-fossilized remains.

Getting deeper into the mines, you notice the remains of fallen gnome warriors and miners that are scattered here and there about the place. You wonder what killed them seemingly not so long ago. However, you find nothing of interest among the remains.
Maximus then unleashes a psionic attack to soften you up!
Maximus summons denizens of the Astral Plane to his help!

At this thought, you can't help but marvel at the long and weary road you have traveled since your first days in the Sword Lands. You grin with nostalgia at the memory of how you stumbled for the first time upon Maximus/Primus and his Overlords.

You think fondly of those people you have met along the way and whom provided friendship and help in defeating the schemes of those same Overlords, as you also discovered their true intent in bringing about the Second Rising of the Mind Lords.

But despite all the odds, you not only managed to defeat the Overlords once and for all, but also destroyed the God-like Mentarchs - including the most powerful and dangerous of them all. At this last thought, you take a deep breath with contentment.
Truly, you have accomplished the seemingly impossible!

This in turn brings back fully the memories of the Great War: how ironic that in an alternate reality, Anthraxus Storm would turn out to be one of the good guys? You also can't help but wonder how would the temporal meddlings of Primus/Maximus could

have been averted without the help of the Gods themselves? With a heavy sigh, you then think of Naryl Thezzat, hoping that the same goodly Gods keep on watching over her heroic soul with kindness and warmth.
How you wish Naryl would be alive still and with you now, to savor this moment to its fullest - and you also wonder how easier things would have been, with her fighting by your side all along.

Having spoken with Zorg and heard what he had to say, you wonder whether you are doing the right thing by leaving the mines this way. Perhaps you would deny the destiny the old half-orc spoke about? Maybe you should instead do the seemingly impossible
and instead initiate a revolt, as intimated by Zorg? Uncertain, you turn back in order to ponder carefully on this course of action.
